def rand_rot(rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Random rotation matrix (QR of a Gaussian matrix, determinant forced to +1)."""
    A = rng.normal(size=(3, 3))
    Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(A)
    if np.linalg.det(Q) < 0:
        Q[:, 0] = -Q[:, 0]
    return Q

docs.title: sample_direction(variables, inputs, env, rng)
docs.text:
Random perturbation direction tangent to the constraints.

Returns (raw, pert). raw holds the generators used by perturbed_state (ξ, w, a for S²; η, δΩ, δΩ̇ for SO(3); δx, δẋ, δẍ for R³; δs, δṡ, δs̈ for R; δu). pert maps the printed perturbation symbols of linearize (states, velocity dstates and input variations) to their numeric values; for S² the induced velocity direction is δω = ξ × ω + w and δω̇ = ξ × ω̇ + a.

Source code in geomech/numeric.py 
def sample_direction(
    variables: SystemVariables, inputs: Sequence[Expr], env: dict, rng: np.random.Generator
) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """Random perturbation direction tangent to the constraints.

    Returns ``(raw, pert)``. ``raw`` holds the generators used by ``perturbed_state``
    (ξ, w, a for S²; η, δΩ, δΩ̇ for SO(3); δx, δẋ, δẍ for R³; δs, δṡ, δs̈ for R; δu).
    ``pert`` maps the printed perturbation symbols of ``linearize`` (states, velocity
    dstates and input variations) to their numeric values; for S² the induced
    velocity direction is δω = ξ × ω + w and δω̇ = ξ × ω̇ + a.
    """
    raw: dict[str, Any] = {}
    pert: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for var, (kq, kv, ka) in _kinematic_symbols(variables):
        if isinstance(var, Scalar):
            ds, dv, da = (float(rng.normal()) for _ in range(3))
            raw[kq] = (ds, dv, da)
            d = var.delta()
            pert[str(d)], pert[str(d.t_diff())], pert[str(d.t_diff().t_diff())] = ds, dv, da
        elif isinstance(var, S2):
            q = env[kq]
            xi, w, a = (_perp(None, q, rng) for _ in range(3))
            raw[kq] = (xi, w, a)
            omega = var.get_tangent_vector()
            pert[str(var.get_variation_vector())] = xi
            pert[str(Variation(omega))] = _cross(xi, env[kv]) + w
            pert[str(Variation(omega).t_diff())] = _cross(xi, env[ka]) + a
        elif isinstance(var, SO3):
            eta, dW, ddW = (rng.normal(size=(3, 1)) for _ in range(3))
            raw[kq] = (eta, dW, ddW)
            Om = var.get_tangent_vector()
            pert[str(var.get_variation_vector())] = eta
            pert[str(Variation(Om))] = dW
            pert[str(Variation(Om).t_diff())] = ddW
        else:
            dx, ddx, dddx = (rng.normal(size=(3, 1)) for _ in range(3))
            raw[kq] = (dx, ddx, dddx)
            d = var.delta()
            pert[str(d)], pert[str(d.t_diff())], pert[str(d.t_diff().t_diff())] = dx, ddx, dddx
    for u in inputs:
        du = float(rng.normal()) if isinstance(u, Scalar) else rng.normal(size=(3, 1))
        raw[str(u)] = du
        pert[str(u.delta())] = du
    return raw, pert

docs.title: sample_state(variables, inputs, rng)
docs.text:
Random trajectory point on the manifold: |q| = 1, q·ω = 0, q·ω̇ = 0, R ∈ SO(3).

Returns an env for Evaluator holding the configuration, velocity and acceleration of every configuration variable and a value for every input.

Source code in geomech/numeric.py 
def sample_state(
    variables: SystemVariables, inputs: Sequence[Expr], rng: np.random.Generator
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Random trajectory point on the manifold: |q| = 1, q·ω = 0, q·ω̇ = 0, R ∈ SO(3).

    Returns an ``env`` for ``Evaluator`` holding the configuration, velocity and
    acceleration of every configuration variable and a value for every input.
    """
    env: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for var, (kq, kv, ka) in _kinematic_symbols(variables):
        if isinstance(var, Scalar):
            env[kq], env[kv], env[ka] = (float(rng.normal()) for _ in range(3))
        elif isinstance(var, S2):
            q = rng.normal(size=(3, 1))
            q /= np.linalg.norm(q)
            env[kq] = q
            env[kv] = _perp(None, q, rng)
            env[ka] = _perp(None, q, rng)
        elif isinstance(var, SO3):
            env[kq] = rand_rot(rng)
            env[kv] = rng.normal(size=(3, 1))
            env[ka] = rng.normal(size=(3, 1))
        else:
            env[kq], env[kv], env[ka] = (rng.normal(size=(3, 1)) for _ in range(3))
    for u in inputs:
        env[str(u)] = float(rng.normal()) if isinstance(u, Scalar) else rng.normal(size=(3, 1))
    return env

Code generation: numeric functions from the symbolic output of the pipeline.

StateLayout maps the symbols of a system to flat arrays; to_source/lambdify turn one expression into Python source or a callable; generate_module writes a module with the blocks of a compute_eom, to_standard_form or linearize result; energy_function generates the total energy of a Lagrangian. docs.title: StateLayout(variables, inputs=(), params=())
docs.text:
How the configuration, velocity, acceleration, input and parameter symbols of a system map to the flat arrays state, a, u and the dict p.

One layout serves every module of a system: build it with the SystemVariables and the inputs list (same order) passed to to_standard_form and linearize, and generate the standard-form and the linearization module from it (generate_module checks the linearization against it). pack/unpack convert between named slot values and the flat state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default variables SystemVariables

the SystemVariables of the system (scalars, then vectors, then matrices; each matrix an SO3).

required inputs Sequence[Expr]

input leaves (Scalar/Vector), stacked into u in this order; validated by geomech.dynamics.eom.check_inputs (an ordered sequence, no constant, no configuration variable, nothing printed like a velocity or acceleration), the check of to_standard_form and linearize.

() params Sequence[Expr]

named constants (any Scalar/Vector/Matrix leaf that is neither a configuration variable nor an input, or the TimeDerivative of one for a prescribed rate), passed as p[str(symbol)]. Numeric literals are inlined by the code generator and are not parameters; tangent and variation vectors (ω, ξ, Ω, η) are rejected. collect_params lists them.

()

Raises TypeError/ValueError naming the symbol for an invalid entry and for two symbols that print alike (str is the identity of a symbol in the engine and the key of p).

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
):
    if not isinstance(variables, SystemVariables):
        raise TypeError(
            f"StateLayout: variables must be a SystemVariables, got {type(variables).__name__}"
        )
    check_variables(variables, caller="StateLayout")
    self.variables = variables
    # the input checks of to_standard_form/linearize, without equations to compare
    self.inputs = tuple(check_inputs(inputs, variables, (), "StateLayout"))
    self.params = tuple(_as_sequence(params, "params"))
    self._slots: dict[str, Slot] = {}
    self._names: set[str] = set()
    self.configuration: list[Slot] = []
    self.velocity: list[Slot] = []
    self.acceleration: list[Slot] = []
    self._build_state()
    self.input_slots = self._build_inputs()
    self.param_slots = self._build_params()

def env_from_arrays(self, state, a=None, u=None, p=None) -> dict:
    """The ``Evaluator`` env of flat arrays: the inverse of the ``*_from_env`` methods."""
    env: dict[str, Any] = {}
    groups = [(self.configuration + self.velocity, state), (self.acceleration, a)]
    groups.append((self.input_slots, u))
    for slots, arr in groups:
        if arr is None:
            continue
        arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        for s in slots:
            env[s.key] = _column(arr[s.slice], s.shape)
    for key, val in (p or {}).items():
        env[key] = val if np.isscalar(val) else _column(np.asarray(val, float), None)
    return env

docs.text:
The flat state from named slot values.

Keys are the slot names of unpack (the Python identifiers of the generated code: x_L, q, R, x_L_dot, omega_q, Omega_R, s_dot …), as keyword arguments, or those names or the printed symbols ("\omega_{q}") as keys of values. Every configuration slot is required; a velocity slot that is not given is zero. R may be a 3×3 matrix or its 9 row-major entries. Values are not projected onto the manifold: simulate and lqr check |q| = 1, q·ω = 0 and RᵀR = I.

Raises KeyError for an unknown or missing configuration slot and ValueError for a value of the wrong size.

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def pack(self, values: dict | None = None, /, **slots) -> np.ndarray:
    """The flat ``state`` from named slot values.

    Keys are the slot names of ``unpack`` (the Python identifiers of the generated
    code: ``x_L``, ``q``, ``R``, ``x_L_dot``, ``omega_q``, ``Omega_R``, ``s_dot`` …),
    as keyword arguments, or those names or the printed symbols (``"\\omega_{q}"``)
    as keys of *values*. Every configuration slot is required; a velocity slot that
    is not given is zero. ``R`` may be a 3×3 matrix or its 9 row-major entries.
    Values are not projected onto the manifold: ``simulate`` and ``lqr`` check
    ``|q| = 1``, ``q·ω = 0`` and ``RᵀR = I``.

    Raises ``KeyError`` for an unknown or missing configuration slot and
    ``ValueError`` for a value of the wrong size.
    """
    given: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, val in [*(values or {}).items(), *slots.items()]:
        slot = self._state_slot(str(key) if not isinstance(key, str) else key)
        if slot.key in given:
            raise ValueError(f"StateLayout.pack: '{slot.name}' given twice")
        given[slot.key] = val
    missing = [s.name for s in self.configuration if s.key not in given]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"StateLayout.pack: no value for the configuration slot(s) {missing}")
    out = np.zeros(self.n_state)
    for s in self.configuration + self.velocity:
        if s.key not in given:
            continue
        val = np.asarray(given[s.key], dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if val.size != s.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"StateLayout.pack: '{s.name}' needs {s.size} entries (shape"
                f" {s.shape}), got {val.size}"
            )
        out[s.slice] = val
    return out

def unpack(self, state) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """``{slot name: value}`` of a flat ``state`` (or of a ``(..., n_state)`` array,
    such as ``Trajectory.state``): the inverse of ``pack``. Scalars have shape ``()``,
    vectors ``(3,)`` and ``R`` ``(3, 3)`` (with the leading axes of *state*)."""
    x = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if x.shape[-1:] != (self.n_state,):
        raise ValueError(
            f"StateLayout.unpack: state must have {self.n_state} entries on its last"
            f" axis, got shape {x.shape}"
        )
    lead = x.shape[:-1]
    return {
        s.name: x[..., s.slice].reshape(lead + s.shape)
        for s in self.configuration + self.velocity
    }

exprs is what the system is made of: [L, dW] (or [L] plus the equations), the dict returned by compute_eom or by to_standard_form, a LinearizedSystem, one Expr, or an iterable of these. Anything else (a number, a string, an object without symbols) raises TypeError rather than giving [].

Numeric literals and the zero/identity constants are left out (they are inlined), as are the configuration, velocity and acceleration symbols of variables, their tangent and variation vectors (ω, ξ, Ω, η, which δW and compute_eom hold) and the inputs. The rest, sorted by printed name, are the parameters to pass as params.

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def collect_params(exprs, variables: SystemVariables, inputs: Sequence[Expr] = ()) -> list[Expr]:
    """The symbols of *exprs* that a ``StateLayout(variables, inputs)`` does not cover.

    *exprs* is what the system is made of: ``[L, dW]`` (or ``[L]`` plus the
    equations), the dict returned by ``compute_eom`` or by ``to_standard_form``, a
    ``LinearizedSystem``, one ``Expr``, or an iterable of these. Anything else (a number,
    a string, an object without symbols) raises ``TypeError`` rather than giving ``[]``.

    Numeric literals and the zero/identity constants are left out (they are inlined), as
    are the configuration, velocity and acceleration symbols of *variables*, their
    tangent and variation vectors (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``, which ``δW`` and
    ``compute_eom`` hold) and the *inputs*. The rest, sorted by printed name, are the
    parameters to pass as ``params``.
    """
    known = StateLayout(variables, inputs)
    found: dict[str, Expr] = {}
    _walk(exprs, found)
    return [
        sym
        for key, sym in sorted(found.items())
        if known.slot(key) is None
        and not is_literal_leaf(sym)
        and not isinstance(sym, (TS2, TSO3))
    ]

def energy_expr(L: Expr, variables: SystemVariables) -> Expr:
    """The total energy ``Σ (∂L/∂v)·v − L`` as an expression tree (simplified)."""
    terms: list[Expr] = []
    for v, p in momenta(L, variables).values():
        if p.is_zero:
            continue
        terms.append(Mul(p, v) if v.type == ExprType.SCALAR else Dot(p, v))
    return full_simplify(sum_of(terms, ExprType.SCALAR) - L)

def energy_function(L: Expr, layout: StateLayout, target: str = "numpy") -> Callable:
    """The total energy of *L* as a callable ``energy(state, p)`` (generated code).

    ``E = Σ (∂L/∂v)·v − L`` over the velocities of ``layout.variables``, derived
    symbolically (``energy_expr``) and generated through the same code path as every
    other block. The callable carries its expression in ``.expr`` and its source in
    ``.source``. Every leaf of ``L`` other than the configuration and velocity symbols
    must be a parameter of *layout*.
    """
    E = energy_expr(L, layout.variables)
    src = "_PARAMS = " + repr(tuple(layout.param_names)) + "\n\n\n"
    src += energy_source(L, layout, target, expr=E)
    ns = namespace(target)
    exec(compile(src, "<geomech.codegen.energy>", "exec"), ns)
    fn = ns["energy"]
    fn.source = src
    fn.expr = E
    return fn

def load_module(source_or_path, name: str = "geomech_generated"):
    """Execute generated source (or a generated file) and return it as a module object."""
    import types

    text = str(source_or_path)
    if isinstance(source_or_path, Path) or "\n" not in text:
        text = Path(text).read_text()
    module = types.ModuleType(name)
    target = "casadi" if "import casadi as ca" in text else "numpy"

    exec(compile(text, f"<{name}>", "exec"), module.__dict__)

docs.text:
The source of the module generate_module writes (see there).

Source code in geomech/codegen/module.py 
def module_source(
    system: dict | LinearizedSystem,
    layout: StateLayout,
    target: str = "numpy",
    *,
    lagrangian: Expr | None = None,
    description: str = "",
) -> str:
    """The source of the module ``generate_module`` writes (see there)."""
    kind = _kind(system)
    tgt = get_target(target)
    builders: dict[str, Callable] = {
        "standard_form": _standard_form,
        "eom": _eom,
        "linearized": _linearized,
    }
    functions = builders[kind](system, layout, tgt)
    if lagrangian is not None:
        functions.append(energy_source(lagrangian, layout, target))
    desc = "\n" + description.strip() + "\n\n" if description.strip() else "\n"
    head = _HEADER.format(target=tgt.name, what=_WHAT[kind], description=desc)
    imports = "import copy\n\n" + "\n".join(tgt.imports)
    parts = [head + "\n\n" + imports + "\n\n" + "LAYOUT = " + pyliteral(layout.to_dict())]
    if isinstance(system, LinearizedSystem):
        parts.append("LINEARIZATION = " + pyliteral(_linearization_data(system)))
    parts.append("_PARAMS = " + pyliteral(tuple(layout.param_names)))
    parts += [h.strip() for h in tgt.helpers.strip().split("\n\n\n")]
    parts.append(_LAYOUT_FN)
    parts += [f.rstrip("\n") for f in functions]
    return "\n\n\n".join(parts) + "\n"

docs.text:
{str(v): (v, ∂L/∂v)} for the velocity v of every configuration variable.

∂L/∂v is a scalar for a scalar variable and a column vector otherwise (for S², the full gradient in ω, which may have a component along q).

def momenta(L: Expr, variables: SystemVariables) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """``{str(v): (v, ∂L/∂v)}`` for the velocity ``v`` of every configuration variable.

    ``∂L/∂v`` is a scalar for a scalar variable and a column vector otherwise (for S², the
    full gradient in ``ω``, which may have a component along ``q``).
    """
    check_variables(variables, caller="momenta")
    cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts = perturbation_variables(variables)
    dL = expand(full_simplify(L.delta()))
    buckets = partition_terms(dL, vel_perts + cfg_perts, "L")
    out = {}
    for var, pert, terms in zip(cfg_vars, vel_perts, buckets):
        coeff = extract_linear_coeff(sum_of(terms, ExprType.SCALAR), pert)
        v = _velocity(var)
        out[str(v)] = (v, full_simplify(coeff))
    return out

    """Python source of ``def name(state, u, p, a=None)`` returning the value of *expr*.

    ``state``, ``u``, ``a`` and ``p`` follow *layout* (``StateLayout``). ``a``, the
    stacked accelerations, is required only when *expr* holds an acceleration (an equation
    of ``compute_eom``), and ``u`` only when it holds an input; a required argument given
    as ``None`` raises ``ValueError``, an unused one may be ``None``. ``None`` never means
    zero here. The source is preceded by ``_PARAMS``, the parameter names, and uses the
    helpers ``_arr``, ``_scalar``, ``_vec``, ``_mat``, ``_hat``, ``_vee``, ``_cross``
    (NumPy) and ``_check_params`` that ``generate_module`` emits (``lambdify`` provides
    them). A vector is returned as a
    ``(3,)`` array, a matrix as ``(3, 3)``.

docs.text:

Source code in geomech/codegen/casadi_target.py 
def block_matrix(self, row_spans, col_spans, blocks) -> list[str]:
    """``ca.vertcat`` of one ``ca.horzcat`` per block row; a missing block is a zero
    ``DM``, and a scalar row's 3-vector block is transposed to ``1×3``."""
    if not col_spans or not row_spans:
        n_rows, n_cols = sum(n for _, n in row_spans), sum(n for _, n in col_spans)
        return [f"return ca.DM.zeros({n_rows}, {n_cols})"]
    lines = []
    for i, (_, nr) in enumerate(row_spans):
        items = []
        for j, (_, nc) in enumerate(col_spans):
            code = blocks.get((i, j))
            if code is None:
                items.append(f"ca.DM.zeros({nr}, {nc})")
            elif nr == 1 and nc == 3:
                items.append(f"{code.operand()}.T")
            else:
                items.append(code.text)
        lines.append(f"_r{i} = ca.horzcat(")
        lines += [f"    {item}," for item in items]
        lines.append(")")
    rows = ", ".join(f"_r{i}" for i in range(len(row_spans)))
    return lines + [f"return ca.vertcat({rows})"]

docs.title: emitter
docs.text:
Translate expression trees into the body of a generated Python function.

Emitter walks a tree once per node class (the same match/case dispatch as the rest of the engine) and produces Python source through a target (NumpyTarget or CasadiTarget) that knows how to write each operation. Shared by both targets:

  • Leaves are resolved through the StateLayout: configuration, velocity, acceleration, input and parameter symbols are bound once at the top of the function, numeric literals and the zero/identity constants are inlined. Anything else raises ValueError naming the leaf (the codegen analogue of the stray-symbol check).
  • Rows: there is one VECTOR type; every vector, row or column, is generated as the same 3-vector, and the row/column structure (is_row_vector) only decides between the inner and the outer product of a VVMul and the side of an MVMul (vᵀM is Mᵀv).
  • Common subexpressions: a subtree that occurs more than once is computed once into a local _tN. Subtrees are identified structurally: a leaf by its class and str (the engine's identity), an operation by its class and the identities of its operands. The identity of each node object is computed once per emission pass (a dict keyed by id(node)), so generation is linear in the number of distinct node objects, also on trees that share subtrees, whose str grows exponentially with depth. A long expression is also split into locals so that every generated line stays short (and ruff-clean).

def assign(self, code: Code) -> Code:
    """Bind *code* to a new local and return the local's name."""
    if code.atomic and code.text.isidentifier():
        return code
    name = f"_t{self._n_temps}"
    self._n_temps += 1
    self.lines.append(f"{name} = {code.text}")
    return Code(name, atomic=True)

def emit(self, node) -> Code:
    """The code of *node*; statements it needs are appended to ``self.lines``."""
    key = self._key(node)
    if key in self._cache:
        return self._cache[key]
    code = self._dispatch(node)
    if _children(node) and (self._counts[key] > 1 or len(code.text) > MAX_INLINE):
        code = self.assign(code)
    self._cache[key] = code
    return code

def preamble(self) -> list[str]:
    """The statements that bind every slot the expressions used, in layout order."""
    order = {key: i for i, key in enumerate(s.key for s in self.layout)}
    slots = sorted(self.used.values(), key=lambda s: order[s.key])
    arrays = [a for a in ("state", "a", "u") if any(s.array == a for s in slots)]
    lines = [self.target.convert_array(a, self._array_size(a)) for a in arrays]
    lines += [f"{s.name} = {self.target.unpack(s)}" for s in slots]
    return lines

docs.title: energy
docs.text:
Total energy E = Σ (∂L/∂v)·v − L of a Lagrangian, derived with the engine.

For every configuration variable the velocity v is its velocity slot: ṡ, ẋ, ω (S²) or Ω (SO(3)). Σ (∂L/∂v)·v is the derivative of L(q, λv) at λ = 1 (for L = L₂ + L₁ + L₀, homogeneous of degree 2, 1, 0 in the velocities, it is 2L₂ + L₁, so E = L₂ − L₀). It does not depend on the velocity coordinates as long as they are linear in the rates: on S², q̇ = ω × q with ω ⊥ q, so scaling ω scales q̇; on SO(3), Ṙ = R Ω̂. E is therefore the energy of Lee et al. (the Legendre transform on TS² and TSO(3)), conserved when δW = 0.

∂L/∂v is the coefficient of the velocity perturbation in the first variation of L: δL = Σ (∂L/∂v)·δv + (configuration terms), with the velocity perturbations of linearize (δṡ = d/dt(δs), δẋ = d/dt(δx), δω, δΩ). δL is expanded, its terms are partitioned by perturbation symbol exactly as linearize does, and extract_linear_coeff gives the coefficient of each velocity perturbation.

{str(v): (v, ∂L/∂v)} for the velocity v of every configuration variable.

∂L/∂v is a scalar for a scalar variable and a column vector otherwise (for S², the full gradient in ω, which may have a component along q).

Source code in geomech/codegen/energy.py 
def momenta(L: Expr, variables: SystemVariables) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """``{str(v): (v, ∂L/∂v)}`` for the velocity ``v`` of every configuration variable.

    ``∂L/∂v`` is a scalar for a scalar variable and a column vector otherwise (for S², the
    full gradient in ``ω``, which may have a component along ``q``).
    """
    check_variables(variables, caller="momenta")
    cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts = perturbation_variables(variables)
    dL = expand(full_simplify(L.delta()))
    buckets = partition_terms(dL, vel_perts + cfg_perts, "L")
    out = {}
    for var, pert, terms in zip(cfg_vars, vel_perts, buckets):
        coeff = extract_linear_coeff(sum_of(terms, ExprType.SCALAR), pert)
        v = _velocity(var)
        out[str(v)] = (v, full_simplify(coeff))
    return out

docs.title: layout
docs.text:
StateLayout: how the symbols of a system map to flat numeric arrays.

One layout is the single source of truth for the generated code and its callers:

========================== =================== ================= ==================== Variable Configuration slot Velocity slot Acceleration symbol ========================== =================== ================= ==================== s: Scalar (R) s (1) ṡ (1) s̈ x: Vector (R³) x (3) ẋ (3) ẍ q: S2 q (3, unit) ω (3, ⊥ q) ω̇ R: SO3 R (9, row-major) Ω (3) Ω̇ ========================== =================== ================= ====================

state holds every configuration slot in variable order (SystemVariables order: scalars, vectors, matrices), then every velocity slot in the same order. a stacks the accelerations in the same order, u the inputs in the given order (scalars 1, vectors 3) and p is a dict keyed by str(symbol) of every parameter.

docs.title: Slot(symbol, key, name, kind, array, shape, start=None, stop=None, manifold='') dataclass
docs.text:
One symbol of a layout.

array is the argument that holds it ("state", "a", "u" or "p"), start:stop its entries there (None for a parameter), shape its numeric shape ((), (3,), (3, 3); an SO(3) point occupies 9 row-major entries) and name the Python identifier the generated code binds it to. manifold is "R", "R3", "S2" or "SO3" for the slots of a configuration variable.

docs.title: StateLayout(variables, inputs=(), params=())
docs.text:
How the configuration, velocity, acceleration, input and parameter symbols of a system map to the flat arrays state, a, u and the dict p.

One layout serves every module of a system: build it with the SystemVariables and the inputs list (same order) passed to to_standard_form and linearize, and generate the standard-form and the linearization module from it (generate_module checks the linearization against it). pack/unpack convert between named slot values and the flat state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default variables SystemVariables

the SystemVariables of the system (scalars, then vectors, then matrices; each matrix an SO3).

required inputs Sequence[Expr]

input leaves (Scalar/Vector), stacked into u in this order; validated by geomech.dynamics.eom.check_inputs (an ordered sequence, no constant, no configuration variable, nothing printed like a velocity or acceleration), the check of to_standard_form and linearize.

() params Sequence[Expr]

named constants (any Scalar/Vector/Matrix leaf that is neither a configuration variable nor an input, or the TimeDerivative of one for a prescribed rate), passed as p[str(symbol)]. Numeric literals are inlined by the code generator and are not parameters; tangent and variation vectors (ω, ξ, Ω, η) are rejected. collect_params lists them.

()

Raises TypeError/ValueError naming the symbol for an invalid entry and for two symbols that print alike (str is the identity of a symbol in the engine and the key of p).

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
):
    if not isinstance(variables, SystemVariables):
        raise TypeError(
            f"StateLayout: variables must be a SystemVariables, got {type(variables).__name__}"
        )
    check_variables(variables, caller="StateLayout")
    self.variables = variables
    # the input checks of to_standard_form/linearize, without equations to compare
    self.inputs = tuple(check_inputs(inputs, variables, (), "StateLayout"))
    self.params = tuple(_as_sequence(params, "params"))
    self._slots: dict[str, Slot] = {}
    self._names: set[str] = set()
    self.configuration: list[Slot] = []
    self.velocity: list[Slot] = []
    self.acceleration: list[Slot] = []
    self._build_state()
    self.input_slots = self._build_inputs()
    self.param_slots = self._build_params()

def env_from_arrays(self, state, a=None, u=None, p=None) -> dict:
    """The ``Evaluator`` env of flat arrays: the inverse of the ``*_from_env`` methods."""
    env: dict[str, Any] = {}
    groups = [(self.configuration + self.velocity, state), (self.acceleration, a)]
    groups.append((self.input_slots, u))
    for slots, arr in groups:
        if arr is None:
            continue
        arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        for s in slots:
            env[s.key] = _column(arr[s.slice], s.shape)
    for key, val in (p or {}).items():
        env[key] = val if np.isscalar(val) else _column(np.asarray(val, float), None)
    return env

docs.title: pack(values=None, /, **slots)
docs.text:
The flat state from named slot values.

Keys are the slot names of unpack (the Python identifiers of the generated code: x_L, q, R, x_L_dot, omega_q, Omega_R, s_dot …), as keyword arguments, or those names or the printed symbols ("\omega_{q}") as keys of values. Every configuration slot is required; a velocity slot that is not given is zero. R may be a 3×3 matrix or its 9 row-major entries. Values are not projected onto the manifold: simulate and lqr check |q| = 1, q·ω = 0 and RᵀR = I.

Raises KeyError for an unknown or missing configuration slot and ValueError for a value of the wrong size.

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def pack(self, values: dict | None = None, /, **slots) -> np.ndarray:
    """The flat ``state`` from named slot values.

    Keys are the slot names of ``unpack`` (the Python identifiers of the generated
    code: ``x_L``, ``q``, ``R``, ``x_L_dot``, ``omega_q``, ``Omega_R``, ``s_dot`` …),
    as keyword arguments, or those names or the printed symbols (``"\\omega_{q}"``)
    as keys of *values*. Every configuration slot is required; a velocity slot that
    is not given is zero. ``R`` may be a 3×3 matrix or its 9 row-major entries.
    Values are not projected onto the manifold: ``simulate`` and ``lqr`` check
    ``|q| = 1``, ``q·ω = 0`` and ``RᵀR = I``.

    Raises ``KeyError`` for an unknown or missing configuration slot and
    ``ValueError`` for a value of the wrong size.
    """
    given: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, val in [*(values or {}).items(), *slots.items()]:
        slot = self._state_slot(str(key) if not isinstance(key, str) else key)
        if slot.key in given:
            raise ValueError(f"StateLayout.pack: '{slot.name}' given twice")
        given[slot.key] = val
    missing = [s.name for s in self.configuration if s.key not in given]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"StateLayout.pack: no value for the configuration slot(s) {missing}")
    out = np.zeros(self.n_state)
    for s in self.configuration + self.velocity:
        if s.key not in given:
            continue
        val = np.asarray(given[s.key], dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if val.size != s.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"StateLayout.pack: '{s.name}' needs {s.size} entries (shape"
                f" {s.shape}), got {val.size}"
            )
        out[s.slice] = val
    return out

docs.text:

def unpack(self, state) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """``{slot name: value}`` of a flat ``state`` (or of a ``(..., n_state)`` array,
    such as ``Trajectory.state``): the inverse of ``pack``. Scalars have shape ``()``,
    vectors ``(3,)`` and ``R`` ``(3, 3)`` (with the leading axes of *state*)."""
    x = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if x.shape[-1:] != (self.n_state,):
        raise ValueError(
            f"StateLayout.unpack: state must have {self.n_state} entries on its last"
            f" axis, got shape {x.shape}"
        )
    lead = x.shape[:-1]
    return {
        s.name: x[..., s.slice].reshape(lead + s.shape)
        for s in self.configuration + self.velocity
    }

docs.title: collect_params(exprs, variables, inputs=())
docs.text:
The symbols of exprs that a StateLayout(variables, inputs) does not cover.

exprs is what the system is made of: [L, dW] (or [L] plus the equations), the dict returned by compute_eom or by to_standard_form, a LinearizedSystem, one Expr, or an iterable of these. Anything else (a number, a string, an object without symbols) raises TypeError rather than giving [].

Numeric literals and the zero/identity constants are left out (they are inlined), as are the configuration, velocity and acceleration symbols of variables, their tangent and variation vectors (ω, ξ, Ω, η, which δW and compute_eom hold) and the inputs. The rest, sorted by printed name, are the parameters to pass as params.

Source code in geomech/codegen/layout.py 
def collect_params(exprs, variables: SystemVariables, inputs: Sequence[Expr] = ()) -> list[Expr]:
    """The symbols of *exprs* that a ``StateLayout(variables, inputs)`` does not cover.

    *exprs* is what the system is made of: ``[L, dW]`` (or ``[L]`` plus the
    equations), the dict returned by ``compute_eom`` or by ``to_standard_form``, a
    ``LinearizedSystem``, one ``Expr``, or an iterable of these. Anything else (a number,
    a string, an object without symbols) raises ``TypeError`` rather than giving ``[]``.

    Numeric literals and the zero/identity constants are left out (they are inlined), as
    are the configuration, velocity and acceleration symbols of *variables*, their
    tangent and variation vectors (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``, which ``δW`` and
    ``compute_eom`` hold) and the *inputs*. The rest, sorted by printed name, are the
    parameters to pass as ``params``.
    """
    known = StateLayout(variables, inputs)
    found: dict[str, Expr] = {}
    _walk(exprs, found)
    return [
        sym
        for key, sym in sorted(found.items())
        if known.slot(key) is None
        and not is_literal_leaf(sym)
        and not isinstance(sym, (TS2, TSO3))
    ]

def is_literal_leaf(node) -> bool:
    """A number, or a zero or identity constant: inlined in the generated code."""
    if is_number_literal(node):
        return True
    if isinstance(node, (Scalar, Vector, Matrix)) and node.is_zero:
        return True
    return isinstance(node, Matrix) and node.flags.is_identity

docs.title: module
docs.text:
generate_module: a self-contained Python module for a derived system.

Standard form (to_standard_form)::

LAYOUT                                  # StateLayout.to_dict()
mass(state, p)          -> (n, n_a)     # block matrix of M[aⱼ] per equation
bias(state, p)          -> (n,)         # stacked f
input_matrix(state, p)  -> (n, n_u)     # block matrix of G[uₖ]
kinematics(state)       -> (n_config,)  # ṡ, ẋ, ω × q, R hat(Ω) (row-major)

so that mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0. compute_eom output gives residual(state, a, u, p) (the stacked equations E) and kinematics; a LinearizedSystem gives M_lin, A_lin, B_lin of (state, a, u, p) with the row and column order of LinearizedSystem.rows/dstates/states/inputs (recorded in LINEARIZATION); they must follow the layout's variables and inputs, see generate_module. With lagrangian=L the module also has energy(state, p). Equations are ordered like the configuration variables of the layout.

required layout StateLayout

the StateLayout of the system (variables, inputs, params). Generate the standard-form and the linearization module of one system from the same layout, built with the SystemVariables and inputs (same order) passed to to_standard_form and linearize.

'numpy' lagrangian Expr | None

None description str

''

The module needs only numpy (and casadi for that target), not geomech. See the module docstring of geomech.codegen.module for the functions it defines; signs and shapes follow docs/conventions.md (M = −physical inertia, a scalar equation with a vector acceleration contributes a 1×3 block). An S² equation holds only on the tangent plane, and its mass block may be singular (Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²) or already full rank (−m l² I); the module does not solve for the accelerations: geomech.simulation.accelerations does, with the tangency constraint q·ω̇ = 0.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

system is none of the three kinds.

ValueError

def generate_module(
    system: dict | LinearizedSystem,
    layout: StateLayout,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    target: str = "numpy",
    *,
    lagrangian: Expr | None = None,
    description: str = "",
) -> str:
    """Write a Python module computing the blocks of *system* and return its source.

    Args:
        system: the dict returned by ``compute_eom``, the ``dict[str,
            StandardFormEquation]`` of ``to_standard_form``, or a ``LinearizedSystem``.
        layout: the ``StateLayout`` of the system (variables, inputs, params). Generate
            the standard-form and the linearization module of one system from the same
            layout, built with the ``SystemVariables`` and ``inputs`` (same order) passed
            to ``to_standard_form`` and ``linearize``.
        path: the ``.py`` file to write (``None``: only return the source).
        target: ``"numpy"`` (default) or ``"casadi"`` (the module imports ``casadi``).
        lagrangian: if given, the module also defines ``energy(state, p)``, the total
            energy ``Σ (∂L/∂v)·v − L`` (``energy_function``).
        description: text for the module docstring.

    The module needs only ``numpy`` (and ``casadi`` for that target), not ``geomech``.
    See the module docstring of ``geomech.codegen.module`` for the functions it defines;
    signs and shapes follow ``docs/conventions.md`` (``M`` = −physical inertia, a scalar
    equation with a vector acceleration contributes a 1×3 block). An S² equation holds
    only on the tangent plane, and its mass block may be singular (``Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²``)
    or already full rank (``−m l² I``); the module does not solve for the accelerations:
    ``geomech.simulation.accelerations`` does, with the tangency constraint ``q·ω̇ = 0``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: *system* is none of the three kinds.
        ValueError: equations that do not match the layout's variables, a block of the
            wrong shape, or a ``LinearizedSystem`` whose variables (rows and states) or
            inputs are not those of the layout in the same order (``B_lin`` would
            otherwise pair its columns with the wrong entries of ``u``).
    """
    src = module_source(system, layout, target, lagrangian=lagrangian, description=description)
    if path is not None:
        Path(path).write_text(src)
    return src

def load_module(source_or_path, name: str = "geomech_generated"):
    """Execute generated source (or a generated file) and return it as a module object."""
    import types

    text = str(source_or_path)
    if isinstance(source_or_path, Path) or "\n" not in text:
        text = Path(text).read_text()
    module = types.ModuleType(name)
    target = "casadi" if "import casadi as ca" in text else "numpy"
    if target == "casadi":
        namespace("casadi")  # raises ImportError with an install hint when absent
    exec(compile(text, f"<{name}>", "exec"), module.__dict__)
    return module

docs.text:
The source of the module generate_module writes (see there).

Source code in geomech/codegen/module.py 
def module_source(
    system: dict | LinearizedSystem,
    layout: StateLayout,
    target: str = "numpy",
    *,
    lagrangian: Expr | None = None,
    description: str = "",
) -> str:
    """The source of the module ``generate_module`` writes (see there)."""
    kind = _kind(system)
    tgt = get_target(target)
    builders: dict[str, Callable] = {
        "standard_form": _standard_form,
        "eom": _eom,
        "linearized": _linearized,
    }
    functions = builders[kind](system, layout, tgt)
    if lagrangian is not None:
        functions.append(energy_source(lagrangian, layout, target))
    desc = "\n" + description.strip() + "\n\n" if description.strip() else "\n"
    head = _HEADER.format(target=tgt.name, what=_WHAT[kind], description=desc)
    imports = "import copy\n\n" + "\n".join(tgt.imports)
    parts = [head + "\n\n" + imports + "\n\n" + "LAYOUT = " + pyliteral(layout.to_dict())]
    if isinstance(system, LinearizedSystem):
        parts.append("LINEARIZATION = " + pyliteral(_linearization_data(system)))
    parts.append("_PARAMS = " + pyliteral(tuple(layout.param_names)))
    parts += [h.strip() for h in tgt.helpers.strip().split("\n\n\n")]
    parts.append(_LAYOUT_FN)
    parts += [f.rstrip("\n") for f in functions]
    return "\n\n\n".join(parts) + "\n"

docs.title: numpy_target
docs.text:
The NumPy target: vectors are (3,) arrays, matrices (3, 3), scalars floats.

===================== ========================================== ========================= Node NumPy Note ===================== ========================================== ========================= Add/VAdd/MAdd a + b + … Mul/SVMul/SMMul a * s scalar times anything MVMul M @ v a row vᵀ M is Mᵀ v MMMul A @ B VVMul inner a @ b, outer np.outer(a, b) by is_row_vector Dot a @ b Cross _cross(a, b) helper, component-wise Hat / Vee _hat(v) / _vee(M) helpers emitted once Transpose M.T; of a vector, the vector itself zero / identity 0.0, np.zeros(3), np.zeros((3, 3)), np.eye(3) ±inf / nan literal np.inf, -np.inf, np.nan ===================== ========================================== =========================

Argument helpers of the generated code: _arr converts state, a and u and raises ValueError for a wrong size or for None (a function converts only the arrays its expressions use, so u=None is accepted by a function without inputs); _scalar, _vec and _mat convert the parameter values. _cross is the component-wise cross product of two 3-vectors: np.cross gives the same values but costs about 10 µs per call on 3-vectors.

def block_matrix(self, row_spans, col_spans, blocks) -> list[str]:
    """Statements building and returning the matrix ``out`` whose block rows and
    columns are the ``(start, size)`` spans, from ``{(i, j): code}``."""
    n_rows = sum(n for _, n in row_spans)
    n_cols = sum(n for _, n in col_spans)
    lines = [f"out = np.zeros(({n_rows}, {n_cols}))"]
    for (i, j), code in sorted(blocks.items()):
        ri, ci = _index(*row_spans[i]), _index(*col_spans[j])
        lines.append(f"out[{ri}, {ci}] = {code.text}")
    return lines + ["return out"]

    """Statements building the flat vector ``out`` of length *n* from
    ``(start, size, code)`` parts; the last statement returns it."""
    lines = [f"out = np.zeros({n})"]
    for start, size, code in parts:
        lines.append(f"out[{_index(start, size)}] = {code.text}")
    return lines + ["return out"]

docs.text:
Generated functions: one expression (to_source, lambdify) or several blocks.

function_source is the one code path every generated function goes through: it runs an Emitter over the expressions, binds the slots they use and lets a finish callback write the statements that assemble and return the result.

docs.title: function_source(name, args, doc, layout, target, exprs, finish, *, kinds=ALL_KINDS, what='expression', params_const='_PARAMS')
docs.text:
Source of def name(args) computing exprs and returning what finish builds.

finish receives the emitter and the code of each expression and returns the final statements (assembly and return). A slot whose array is not among args raises ValueError (an energy that depends on an input).

Source code in geomech/codegen/source.py 
def function_source(
    name: str,
    args: Sequence[str],
    doc: str,
    layout: StateLayout,
    target,
    exprs: Sequence[Expr],
    finish: Callable[[Emitter, list[Code]], list[str]],
    *,
    kinds=ALL_KINDS,
    what: str = "expression",
    params_const: str = "_PARAMS",
) -> str:
    """Source of ``def name(args)`` computing *exprs* and returning what *finish* builds.

    *finish* receives the emitter and the code of each expression and returns the final
    statements (assembly and ``return``). A slot whose array is not among *args* raises
    ``ValueError`` (an energy that depends on an input).
    """
    em = Emitter(layout, target, kinds=kinds, what=what)
    em.prepare(exprs)
    codes = [em.emit(e) for e in exprs]
    tail = finish(em, codes)
    arg_names = {a.split("=")[0] for a in args}
    for slot in em.used.values():
        if slot.array not in arg_names:
            raise ValueError(
                f"codegen: {what} depends on the {slot.kind} '{slot.key}', but {name}() has"
                f" no '{slot.array}' argument"
            )
    body = _docstring(doc)
    if "p" in arg_names:
        body.append(target.check_params(params_const))
    body += em.preamble() + em.lines + tail
    head = f"def {name}({', '.join(args)}):"
    return "\n".join([head] + [_INDENT + line if line else "" for line in body]) + "\n"

def lambdify(expr: Expr, layout: StateLayout, target: str = "numpy") -> Callable:
    """``to_source`` compiled: a callable ``f(state, u, p, a=None)``.

    The callable carries its source in ``f.source``. With ``target="casadi"`` the
    arguments may be CasADi expressions and the result is a CasADi object; ``casadi`` must
    be installed (``ImportError`` otherwise).
    """
    src = to_source(expr, layout, target)
    ns = namespace(target)
    exec(compile(src, "<geomech.codegen>", "exec"), ns)
    fn = ns["f"]
    fn.source = src
    return fn

Source code in geomech/codegen/source.py 
def pyliteral(obj: Any, indent: str = "") -> str:
    """Python source of plain data (dict, list, tuple, str, int, float), in the layout
    ``ruff format`` keeps: collections expanded one item per line with a trailing comma,
    short lists of numbers or strings inline."""
    inner = indent + _INDENT
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        if not obj:
            return "{}"
        items = [f"{inner}{pystr(str(k))}: {pyliteral(v, inner)}," for k, v in obj.items()]
        return "{\n" + "\n".join(items) + f"\n{indent}}}"
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        opener, closer = ("[", "]") if isinstance(obj, list) else ("(", ")")
        if not obj:
            return opener + closer
        flat = [pyliteral(v) for v in obj]
        if all(not isinstance(v, (dict, list, tuple)) for v in obj):
            text = ", ".join(flat) + ("," if isinstance(obj, tuple) and len(obj) == 1 else "")
            if len(text) <= 40:
                return opener + text + closer
        items = [f"{inner}{pyliteral(v, inner)}," for v in obj]
        return opener + "\n" + "\n".join(items) + f"\n{indent}{closer}"
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        return pystr(obj)
    if isinstance(obj, bool) or obj is None:
        return repr(obj)
    if isinstance(obj, (int, float)):
        return repr(obj)
    raise TypeError(f"pyliteral: cannot write {type(obj).__name__}")

Python source of def name(state, u, p, a=None) returning the value of expr.

state, u, a and p follow layout (StateLayout). a, the stacked accelerations, is required only when expr holds an acceleration (an equation of compute_eom), and u only when it holds an input; a required argument given as None raises ValueError, an unused one may be None. None never means zero here. The source is preceded by _PARAMS, the parameter names, and uses the helpers _arr, _scalar, _vec, _mat, _hat, _vee, _cross (NumPy) and _check_params that generate_module emits (lambdify provides them). A vector is returned as a (3,) array, a matrix as (3, 3).

Raises ValueError naming the symbol for a leaf that is not in the layout, a TimeDerivative of a non-leaf, a variation or a time integral.

def to_source(expr: Expr, layout: StateLayout, target: str = "numpy", *, name: str = "f") -> str:
    """Python source of ``def name(state, u, p, a=None)`` returning the value of *expr*.

    ``state``, ``u``, ``a`` and ``p`` follow *layout* (``StateLayout``). ``a``, the
    stacked accelerations, is required only when *expr* holds an acceleration (an equation
    of ``compute_eom``), and ``u`` only when it holds an input; a required argument given
    as ``None`` raises ``ValueError``, an unused one may be ``None``. ``None`` never means
    zero here. The source is preceded by ``_PARAMS``, the parameter names, and uses the
    helpers ``_arr``, ``_scalar``, ``_vec``, ``_mat``, ``_hat``, ``_vee``, ``_cross``
    (NumPy) and ``_check_params`` that ``generate_module`` emits (``lambdify`` provides
    them). A vector is returned as a
    ``(3,)`` array, a matrix as ``(3, 3)``.

    Raises ``ValueError`` naming the symbol for a leaf that is not in the layout, a
    ``TimeDerivative`` of a non-leaf, a variation or a time integral.
    """
    tgt = get_target(target)
    const = f"_PARAMS = {pyliteral(tuple(layout.param_names))}\n\n\n"
    doc = f"Generated by geomech.codegen: {name}."
    return const + function_source(name, _ARGS, doc, layout, tgt, [expr], _return)

docs.text:
Shared numeric literals and the typed zero / negation helpers.

Every rewrite that needs -1, -2 or 1/2 uses the leaves below instead of building its own: NEG_ONE prints (-1), exactly as Number(-1) and the -1 the operators wrap (x * -1, -x), so a rule's output and a user's -x are the same tree. The leaves are ordinary Number literals (is_number_literal is true for each), shared by every tree that uses them; that is safe because nodes are never mutated.

negate(expr) is expr * (-1) for an expression of any type (Mul, SVMul or SMMul; a row vector stays a row), and zero_like(expr) is the zero leaf of the type of expr (Zero, ZeroVector, ZeroMatrix); zero_of(expr_type) the same for a bare ExprType.

The same tree as -expr (Expr.__neg__): a scaled row vector stays a row ((v s)ᵀ). Raises TypeError for an object without an expression type.

def negate(expr: Expr) -> Expr:
    """``expr · (-1)``: ``Mul`` for a scalar, ``SVMul`` for a vector, ``SMMul`` for a matrix.

    The same tree as ``-expr`` (``Expr.__neg__``): a scaled row vector stays a row
    (``(v s)ᵀ``). Raises ``TypeError`` for an object without an expression type.
    """
    if getattr(expr, "type", None) not in (ExprType.SCALAR, ExprType.VECTOR, ExprType.MATRIX):
        raise TypeError(f"negate: cannot negate {type(expr).__name__} {expr!r}")
    return expr * NEG_ONE

docs.text:
Same class, same printed form and, for a calculus node, the same operand class.

str is the identity of a tree (the product family prints a separator that no leaf name may contain, decision D2, so two products print alike only when they multiply the same factors in the same order, up to regrouping); the class guard keeps Scalar("x") and Vector("x") apart, and _identity_extra lets a node add what its printed form leaves out (Variation(Scalar x) vs Variation(Vector x) both print \delta{x}). Commutative rearrangements are different trees.

def __eq__(self, other) -> bool:
    """Same class, same printed form and, for a calculus node, the same operand class.

    ``str`` is the identity of a tree (the product family prints a separator that no
    leaf name may contain, decision D2, so two products print alike only when they
    multiply the same factors in the same order, up to regrouping); the class guard keeps
    ``Scalar("x")`` and ``Vector("x")`` apart, and ``_identity_extra`` lets a node add
    what its printed form leaves out (``Variation(Scalar x)`` vs ``Variation(Vector x)``
    both print ``\\delta{x}``). Commutative rearrangements are different trees.
    """
    if type(self) is not type(other):
        return False
    return str(self) == str(other) and self._identity_extra() == other._identity_extra()

docs.title: Number(value)
docs.text:
Anonymous numeric constant (value).

value is an int or float (numpy integer and floating scalars are converted to the equal Python number) or a str name; bool is rejected.

Number(0) carries the Zero flag and Number(1) the Ones flag, so the zero/identity rules of simplify see them like Zero/One.

Source code in geomech/core/base/expressions.py 
def Number(value):
    """Anonymous numeric constant ``(value)``.

    ``value`` is an ``int`` or ``float`` (numpy integer and floating scalars are converted
    to the equal Python number) or a ``str`` name; ``bool`` is rejected.

    ``Number(0)`` carries the ``Zero`` flag and ``Number(1)`` the ``Ones`` flag, so the
    zero/identity rules of ``simplify`` see them like ``Zero``/``One``.
    """
    if isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"Number expects int, float, or str, got bool {value}; write Number(1) or Number(0)"
        )
    # numpy scalars become the equal Python number, so that str() is the same as for
    # the literal (np.int64(2) -> "(2)", np.float64(0.5) -> "(0.5)")
    if isinstance(value, np.integer):
        value = int(value)
    elif isinstance(value, np.floating):
        value = float(value)
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        attr = ["Constant"]
        if value == 0:
            attr.append("Zero")
        elif value == 1:
            attr.append("Ones")
        return Scalar("(" + str(value) + ")", value=value, attr=attr)
    elif isinstance(value, str):
        return Scalar(s=value, attr=["Constant"])
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"Number expects int, float, or str, got {type(value).__name__}")

docs.text:
True for an anonymous numeric constant: a Scalar leaf printed as its own value.

Number(2) ((2)), Zero/One (0/1), Scalar("0.5", value=0.5) and the numbers the operators wrap (2 * x) are literals; the simplifier folds them. A named scalar with a value, Scalar("m", value=2), is a symbol: the value is only what geomech.numeric evaluates it to, and simplification keeps the name (fix plan decision D1).

Source code in geomech/core/base/expressions.py 
def is_number_literal(expr) -> bool:
    """True for an anonymous numeric constant: a ``Scalar`` leaf printed as its own value.

    ``Number(2)`` (``(2)``), ``Zero``/``One`` (``0``/``1``), ``Scalar("0.5", value=0.5)`` and
    the numbers the operators wrap (``2 * x``) are literals; the simplifier folds them.
    A *named* scalar with a value, ``Scalar("m", value=2)``, is a symbol: the value is
    only what ``geomech.numeric`` evaluates it to, and simplification keeps the name
    (fix plan decision D1).
    """
    if not isinstance(expr, Scalar) or expr.value is None or getattr(expr, "nodes", None):
        return False
    name = expr.name
    if not isinstance(name, str):
        return False
    text = name[1:-1] if name.startswith("(") and name.endswith(")") else name
    value = expr.value
    # an int is compared exactly: float() of an int beyond the float range overflows
    if isinstance(value, int):
        try:
            return int(text) == value
        except ValueError:
            pass  # e.g. "2.0" for the value 2
    try:
        a, b = float(text), float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
        return False
    return a == b or (math.isnan(a) and math.isnan(b))  # Number(nan) prints "(nan)"

Source code in geomech/core/base/types.py 
@classmethod
def from_attr_list(cls, attrs: list[str] | None, name: str | None = None) -> ExprFlags:
    """Build the flags for a leaf from its ``attr`` strings.

    An attribute outside ``VALID_ATTRS`` raises ``ValueError`` naming the symbol
    (*name*) and the attribute instead of being ignored; a bare string instead of a
    list raises ``TypeError``. Attribute names are case-sensitive.
    """
    if isinstance(attrs, str):
        where = f" for symbol '{name}'" if name is not None else ""
        raise TypeError(
            f"attr must be a list of strings, got str {attrs!r}{where}; write attr=[{attrs!r}]"
        )
    if not attrs:
        return cls()
    values = {}
    for a in attrs:
        if not isinstance(a, str) or a not in _ATTR_FLAGS:
            where = f" for symbol '{name}'" if name is not None else ""
            raise ValueError(
                f"attr: unknown attribute {a!r}{where}; valid attributes are"
                f" {sorted(VALID_ATTRS)}"
            )
        for flag in _ATTR_FLAGS[a]:
            values[flag] = True
    return cls(**values)

docs.text:
Collect expr with respect to vec.

Rearranges so vec appears on the left of every Dot that contains it. Only a scalar expression can hold a Dot; anything else raises TypeError.

Source code in geomech/core/math/collecting.py 
def collect(expr, vec):
    """Collect *expr* with respect to *vec*.

    Rearranges so *vec* appears on the left of every Dot that contains it. Only a scalar
    expression can hold a ``Dot``; anything else raises ``TypeError``.
    """
    if getattr(expr, "type", None) != ExprType.SCALAR:
        kind = getattr(getattr(expr, "type", None), "name", None)
        raise TypeError(
            f"collect: expected a scalar expression, got {type(expr).__name__} '{expr}'"
            f" of type {kind}"
        )
    match expr:
        case Add(nodes=nodes):
            return Add(*[collect(n, vec) for n in nodes])

        case Mul():
            return Mul(collect(expr.left, vec), collect(expr.right, vec))

        case Dot():
            return _collect_dot(expr, vec)

        case VVMul() if expr.has(vec):
            # an inner product rᵀb holding the target: as Dot(r, b) the Dot rules apply
            return _collect_dot(
                rule("collect.inner_product_to_dot", expr, Dot(column_of(expr.left), expr.right)),
                vec,
            )

        case _:
            return expr

def extract_linear_coeff(expr, query):
    """Extract the coefficient of *query* from *expr*.

    Dispatches based on the types of query and expr:
      scalar query + scalar expr → scalar coefficient
      scalar query + vector expr → vector coefficient
      scalar query + matrix expr → matrix coefficient
      vector query + scalar expr → vector coefficient
      vector query + vector expr → matrix coefficient
      vector query + matrix expr → matrix coefficient
    """
    q_type = getattr(query, "type", None)
    e_type = getattr(expr, "type", None)

    match (e_type, q_type):
        case (ExprType.SCALAR, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_scalar(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.VECTOR, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_vector(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.SCALAR, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_scalar(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.VECTOR, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_vector(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.MATRIX):
            return _matrix_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case _:
            raise AlgebraicError(
                f"extract_linear_coeff: a {q_type.name if q_type else q_type} query has no"
                f" left coefficient in a {e_type.name if e_type else e_type} expression"
                f" | query='{query}', expr='{expr}'"
            )

docs.title: collecting
docs.text:
Collect: rearrange a scalar expression so that a target vector appears on the left side of Dot.

This is a preprocessing step for integration by parts (ibp), which only matches Dot(target, ...) on the left.

Rules (name, identity, hypothesis the code checks):

collect.inner_product_to_dot VVMul(rᵀ, b) = Dot(r, b), with r = column_of(rᵀ) ((vᵀ)ᵀ = v, (vᵀM)ᵀ = Mᵀv, (vᵀs)ᵀ = v s); only for an inner product that contains the target, so v.T() * A * v in a kinetic energy can be integrated by parts collect.flip_target_right Dot(a, v) = Dot(v, a) the target is the right operand collect.flip_cross_mvmul Dot(b×c, M x) = Dot(M x, b×c) the target is on either side; the MVMul goes left for the rules below collect.flip_mvmul_pair Dot(M x, N f(v)) = Dot(N f(v), M x) the target is in the right MVMul collect.flip_mvmul_left Dot(M x, f(v)) = Dot(f(v), M x) the target is in the non-MVMul side collect.flip_mvmul_right Dot(a, M f(v)) = Dot(M f(v), a) the target is in the right MVMul collect.flip_cross_left Dot(f(v)×c, a) = Dot(a, f(v)×c) the target is in the left Cross all six are commutativity of Dot (no hypothesis); the names say which call site flipped collect.triple_product_left a·(v×c) = v·(c×a) the target v is the left operand of the Cross collect.triple_product_right a·(b×v) = v·(a×b) the target is the right operand collect.triple_product_left_nested a·(f(v)×c) = f(v)·(c×a) the target is inside the left operand (collect then recurses) collect.triple_product_right_nested a·(b×f(v)) = f(v)·(a×b) inside the right operand collect.triple_product_mvmul_left collect.triple_product_mvmul_right collect.triple_product_mvmul_left_nested collect.triple_product_mvmul_right_nested the same four rotations when the other operand of the Dot is a matrix product, a = M x (the cases of Dot(MVMul, Cross)); all eight are the cyclic scalar triple product, so none needs a hypothesis collect.peel_matrix Dot(M f, w) = Dot(f, Mᵀ w) the target is in the vector operand f, not in M collect.strip_rotation Dot(R a, R b) = Dot(a, b) both matrices are SO3 points equal by name

A target that occurs on both sides of a Dot is not linear; collect raises NonLinearError instead of looking for a rotation that cannot exist. A target that sits inside the matrix factor of an MVMul (Hat(v), v cᵀ, M Hat(v)) cannot be exposed by transposition, which only moves the matrix: collect raises AlgebraicError naming the term and the target.

docs.title: collect(expr, vec)
docs.text:
Collect expr with respect to vec.

Rearranges so vec appears on the left of every Dot that contains it. Only a scalar expression can hold a Dot; anything else raises TypeError.

Source code in geomech/core/math/collecting.py 
def collect(expr, vec):
    """Collect *expr* with respect to *vec*.

    Rearranges so *vec* appears on the left of every Dot that contains it. Only a scalar
    expression can hold a ``Dot``; anything else raises ``TypeError``.
    """
    if getattr(expr, "type", None) != ExprType.SCALAR:
        kind = getattr(getattr(expr, "type", None), "name", None)
        raise TypeError(
            f"collect: expected a scalar expression, got {type(expr).__name__} '{expr}'"
            f" of type {kind}"
        )
    match expr:
        case Add(nodes=nodes):
            return Add(*[collect(n, vec) for n in nodes])

        case Mul():
            return Mul(collect(expr.left, vec), collect(expr.right, vec))

        case Dot():
            return _collect_dot(expr, vec)

        case VVMul() if expr.has(vec):
            # an inner product rᵀb holding the target: as Dot(r, b) the Dot rules apply
            return _collect_dot(
                rule("collect.inner_product_to_dot", expr, Dot(column_of(expr.left), expr.right)),
                vec,
            )

        case _:
            return expr

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Coefficient extraction: extract a query from an expression.

Dispatch grid (query_type × expr_type → result_type):

query \ expr  |  Scalar  |  Vector  |  Matrix
--------------|---------|---------|--------
Scalar        | Scalar  | Vector  | Matrix
Vector        | Vector  | Matrix  | (raises)
Matrix        | (raises)| (raises)| Matrix (partial)

extract_linear_coeff(expr, query) dispatches to the appropriate function.

The coefficient is always a left factor: c·s, cᵀ·v, C·v or C·N. A term that is linear in the query but has no such factor (a vector query inside a matrix expression, M·Hat(v) or v wᵀ, whose coefficient would be a 3-tensor; a scalar factor ⟨a, M b⟩ of a matrix query) raises AlgebraicError; a term where the query occurs in both children of a product raises NonLinearError. Nothing that contains the query is ever returned as a zero coefficient.

def extract_linear_coeff(expr, query):
    """Extract the coefficient of *query* from *expr*.

    Dispatches based on the types of query and expr:
      scalar query + scalar expr → scalar coefficient
      scalar query + vector expr → vector coefficient
      scalar query + matrix expr → matrix coefficient
      vector query + scalar expr → vector coefficient
      vector query + vector expr → matrix coefficient
      vector query + matrix expr → matrix coefficient
    """
    q_type = getattr(query, "type", None)
    e_type = getattr(expr, "type", None)

    match (e_type, q_type):
        case (ExprType.SCALAR, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_scalar(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.VECTOR, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_vector(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.SCALAR):
            return _scalar_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.SCALAR, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_scalar(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.VECTOR, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_vector(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.VECTOR):
            return _vector_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case (ExprType.MATRIX, ExprType.MATRIX):
            return _matrix_from_matrix(expr, query)
        case _:
            raise AlgebraicError(
                f"extract_linear_coeff: a {q_type.name if q_type else q_type} query has no"
                f" left coefficient in a {e_type.name if e_type else e_type} expression"
                f" | query='{query}', expr='{expr}'"
            )

docs.title: has_algebraic(expr, query)
docs.text:
Check if query appears algebraically in expr (not inside calculus ops).

Calculus operators (d/dt, δ, ∫) are opaque boundaries — d/dt(η) does not algebraically contain η. The pipeline always expands d/dt(A+B) → d/dt(A) + d/dt(B) before extraction, so calculus ops only wrap leaf nodes by the time this is called.

Raises AlgebraicError if the query is found only inside a calculus operator that is not itself the query (e.g. query ẍ inside d/dt(ẍ), or δx inside d/dt(δx)): such a term has no linear coefficient and must never be silently dropped.

Source code in geomech/core/math/extract.py 
def has_algebraic(expr, query) -> bool:
    """Check if query appears algebraically in expr (not inside calculus ops).

    Calculus operators (d/dt, δ, ∫) are opaque boundaries — d/dt(η) does
    not algebraically contain η. The pipeline always expands
    d/dt(A+B) → d/dt(A) + d/dt(B) before extraction, so calculus ops
    only wrap leaf nodes by the time this is called.

    Raises ``AlgebraicError`` if the query is found *only inside* a calculus
    operator that is not itself the query (e.g. query ẍ inside d/dt(ẍ), or
    δx inside d/dt(δx)): such a term has no linear coefficient and must
    never be silently dropped.
    """
    if same_node(expr, query):
        return True
    if isinstance(expr, (TimeDerivative, TimeIntegral, Variation)):
        if expr.has(query):
            raise AlgebraicError(
                f"extract_linear_coeff: '{query}' appears only inside the calculus"
                f" operator '{expr}' (a higher order derivative, a variation or an"
                " integral of the query); such a term has no linear coefficient"
            )
        return False
    nodes = getattr(expr, "nodes", None)
    if nodes:
        return any(has_algebraic(n, query) for n in nodes)
    return False

docs.text:
Node identity: same type and, for leaves, same name; otherwise ==.

The type guard is the one Expr.__eq__ uses, so the leaf Scalar("k") never matches Vector("k") (a leaf name cannot contain the product separator *, so no leaf prints like the product k*x), and == on a calculus node or a Transpose also compares the class of its operand, so Variation(Scalar("x")) is not Variation(Vector("x")).

Source code in geomech/core/math/extract.py 
def same_node(expr, query) -> bool:
    """Node identity: same type and, for leaves, same name; otherwise ``==``.

    The type guard is the one ``Expr.__eq__`` uses, so the leaf ``Scalar("k")`` never
    matches ``Vector("k")`` (a leaf name cannot contain the product separator ``*``, so no
    leaf prints like the product ``k*x``), and ``==`` on a calculus node or a ``Transpose``
    also compares the class of its operand, so ``Variation(Scalar("x"))`` is not
    ``Variation(Vector("x"))``.
    """
    if type(expr) is not type(query):
        return False
    e_name, q_name = getattr(expr, "name", None), getattr(query, "name", None)
    if e_name is not None or q_name is not None:
        return e_name == q_name
    return expr == query

docs.title: ibp
docs.text:
Integration by parts for scalar expressions.

integrate_by_parts(expr, targets) — expand → full_simplify, then for each target in
order: collect → one IBP pass → full_simplify

IBP identity (boundary terms dropped): ∫ Dot(ẋ, f) dt = -∫ Dot(x, ḟ) dt

So: Dot(target, rhs) → Dot(-target.t_integrate(), rhs.t_diff())

Only a Dot whose left operand is the target, or a scalar Mul chain with the target as a direct factor, is integrated; collect is what brings each term into that shape. A target left anywhere else survives, and extraction then fails on it (compute_eom names the term).

Rules (name, identity, hypothesis):

ibp.dot a Dot(ẋ, f) → a Dot(-x, ḟ) target is the left operand; a is constant (or absent) ibp.dot_prefactor a Dot(ẋ, f) → a Dot(-x, ḟ) - Dot(x, ȧ f) a is a non-constant scalar factor ibp.scalar_factor ẋ g → -x ġ target is a factor of a Mul chain ibp.product_rule d/dt(∏ fᵢ^nᵢ) → Σ nᵢ fᵢ^(nᵢ-1) ḟᵢ ∏_{j≠i} fⱼ^nⱼ the rate ȧ of ibp.dot_prefactor; constant factors are skipped and repeated factors merged

The column vector whose transpose is the row vector row, built structurally.

(vᵀ)ᵀ = v, (rᵀ M)ᵀ = Mᵀ r, (r s)ᵀ = rᵀ s, a sum of rows maps addend by addend, and d/dt, δ, ∫ commute with the transpose. A row of any other shape falls back to Transpose(row). Source code in geomech/core/operations/geometry.py 
def column_of(row):
    """The column vector whose transpose is the row vector *row*, built structurally.

    ``(vᵀ)ᵀ = v``, ``(rᵀ M)ᵀ = Mᵀ r``, ``(r s)ᵀ = rᵀ s``, a sum of rows maps addend by
    addend, and d/dt, δ, ∫ commute with the transpose. A row of any other shape falls back
    to ``Transpose(row)``. For a ``Transpose`` node this is the same object as
    ``Transpose(row)``; for the other row shapes (``aᵀK``, ``s aᵀ``) it gives a column the
    engine can work with, where ``Transpose(MVMul(aᵀ, K))`` would be opaque.
    """
    match row:
        case Transpose():
            return row.expr
        case MVMul() if row.left.type == ExprType.VECTOR:
            return MVMul(Transpose(row.right), column_of(row.left))
        case SVMul() if is_row_vector(row.left):
            return SVMul(column_of(row.left), row.right)
        case VAdd() if is_row_vector(row):
            return VAdd(*[column_of(n) for n in row.nodes])
        case TimeDerivative() if is_row_vector(row.expr):
            return TimeDerivative(column_of(row.expr))
        case Variation() if is_row_vector(row.expr):
            return Variation(column_of(row.expr))
        case TimeIntegral() if is_row_vector(row.expr):
            return TimeIntegral(column_of(row.expr))
        case _:
            return Transpose(row)

docs.text:
True if the vector-typed expr is a row vector.

The tree has one VECTOR type for columns and rows; orientation is structural. A row is Transpose(column), a row times a matrix (MVMul(vᵀ, M)), a scalar multiple of a row, a sum whose first addend is a row, or a calculus operator (d/dt, δ, ∫) of a row. Every other vector expression is a column.

Source code in geomech/core/operations/geometry.py 
def is_row_vector(expr):
    """True if the vector-typed *expr* is a row vector.

    The tree has one ``VECTOR`` type for columns and rows; orientation is structural.
    A row is ``Transpose(column)``, a row times a matrix (``MVMul(vᵀ, M)``), a scalar
    multiple of a row, a sum whose first addend is a row, or a calculus operator
    (d/dt, δ, ∫) of a row. Every other vector expression is a column.
    """
    if getattr(expr, "type", None) != ExprType.VECTOR:
        return False
    match expr:
        case Transpose():
            return not is_row_vector(expr.expr)
        case MVMul():
            return expr.left.type == ExprType.VECTOR
        case SVMul():
            return is_row_vector(expr.left)
        case VAdd():
            return is_row_vector(expr.nodes[0])
        case TimeDerivative() | Variation() | TimeIntegral():
            return is_row_vector(expr.expr)
        case _:
            return False

Walks the expression tree and replaces Variation(TS2) and Variation(TSO3) nodes with their kinematic expansions.

def apply_manifold_rules(expr, variables: SystemVariables):
    """Apply manifold kinematic substitutions to an expression.

    Walks the expression tree and replaces Variation(TS2) and
    Variation(TSO3) nodes with their kinematic expansions.
    """
    tangent_map: dict[str, tuple[str, Expr, Expr, Expr]] = {}

    # S2 manifolds (vectors)
    for vec in variables.vectors:
        if isinstance(vec, S2):
            omega = vec.get_tangent_vector()
            xi = vec.get_variation_vector()
            tangent_map[str(omega)] = ("S2", vec, omega, xi)

    # SO3 manifolds (matrices)
    for mat in variables.matrices:
        if isinstance(mat, SO3):
            Omega = mat.get_tangent_vector()
            eta = mat.get_variation_vector()
            tangent_map[str(Omega)] = ("SO3", mat, Omega, eta)

    if not tangent_map:
        return expr

    return _substitute(expr, tangent_map)

def expand(expr):
    """Distribute every product over sums, bottom up (rules in the module docstring)."""
    match expr:
        # --- N-ary additions: expand each term ---
        case Add(nodes=nodes):
            return Add(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        case VAdd(nodes=nodes):
            return VAdd(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        case MAdd(nodes=nodes):
            return MAdd(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        # --- Scalar * Scalar ---
        case Mul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Mul, Add, Add, Add, "expand.mul_over_add", expr)

        # --- Dot product (vector x vector → scalar) ---
        case Dot():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Dot, Add, VAdd, VAdd, "expand.dot_over_vadd", expr)

        # --- Cross product (vector x vector → vector) ---
        case Cross():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Cross, VAdd, VAdd, VAdd, "expand.cross_over_vadd", expr)

        # --- Scalar * Vector  (left=vector, right=scalar) ---
        case SVMul() if is_row_vector(expr.left):
            return _expand_row_svmul(expr)

        case SVMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, SVMul, VAdd, VAdd, Add, "expand.svmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Matrix * Vector ---
        case MVMul() if expr.left.type == ExprType.VECTOR:
            return _expand_row_mvmul(expr)

        case MVMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, MVMul, VAdd, MAdd, VAdd, "expand.mvmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Scalar * Matrix  (left=matrix, right=scalar) ---
        case SMMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, SMMul, MAdd, MAdd, Add, "expand.smmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Matrix * Matrix ---
        case MMMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, MMMul, MAdd, MAdd, MAdd, "expand.mmmul_over_madd", expr)

        # --- Vector * Vector (outer product → matrix, inner product → scalar) ---
        case VVMul():
            return _expand_vvmul(expr)

        # --- Unary ops: recurse into child ---
        # Hat is linear: Hat(a + b) = Hat(a) + Hat(b)
        case Hat():
            inner = expand(expr.expr)
            if isinstance(inner, VAdd):
                return rule("expand.hat_over_vadd", expr, MAdd(*[Hat(n) for n in inner.nodes]))
            return Hat(inner)

        # Vee is linear: Vee(A + B) = Vee(A) + Vee(B)
        case Vee():
            inner = expand(expr.expr)
            if isinstance(inner, MAdd):
                return rule("expand.vee_over_madd", expr, VAdd(*[Vee(n) for n in inner.nodes]))
            return Vee(inner)

        case Variation():
            return calculus_node(Variation, expand(expr.expr))

        case TimeDerivative():
            return calculus_node(TimeDerivative, expand(expr.expr))

        case TimeIntegral():
            return TimeIntegral(expand(expr.expr))

        # --- Leaves and everything else ---
        case _:
            return expr

def full_simplify(expr, max_iter=10):
    """Expand once, then loop simplify until convergence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    max_iter : int
        Safety cap on the number of passes (default 10). Hitting it emits a
        ``RuntimeWarning`` ("no confirmed fixed point after N passes") naming the
        expression: the result may be unsimplified. A pass that changes nothing ends the
        loop, so the warning fires only when the last allowed pass still changed the
        expression; that last result may already be the fixed point, which only one more
        pass could confirm (hence "confirmed").
    """
    expr = expand(expr)
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        prev = expr
        expr = simplify(expr)
        if str(expr) == str(prev):
            break
    else:
        why = (
            "max_iter=0: no simplify pass ran"
            if max_iter <= 0
            else f"the last pass still changed the expression, so no fixed point after"
            f" {max_iter} passes was confirmed by an unchanged pass"
        )
        warnings.warn(
            f"full_simplify: no confirmed fixed point after {max_iter} passes ({why});"
            f" result may be unsimplified: {expr!r}",
            RuntimeWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return expr

    combine numeric constants — single call does everything."""
    expr = pull(expr)
    expr = vector_rules(expr)
    return _eliminate(expr)
