docs.title: expansion
docs.text:
Distribute multiplication over addition (expand products).

Bottom-up traversal: expand children first, then distribute at the current node. Single pass.

Distribution rules (name, identity; none needs a hypothesis: they are bilinearity of each product and linearity of Hat). A rule fires only when an operand is a sum.

expand.mul_over_add Mul over Add → Add (scalar) expand.dot_over_vadd Dot over VAdd → Add (scalar from vectors) expand.cross_over_vadd Cross over VAdd → VAdd (vector) expand.svmul_over_sum SVMul over VAdd/Add → VAdd (vector, left=vector right=scalar) expand.row_svmul_over_sum a scaled row rᵀ s over a sum of rows or an Add scalar expand.mvmul_over_sum MVMul over MAdd/VAdd → VAdd (vector) expand.row_mvmul_over_sum a row times a matrix, rᵀ M, over a sum of rows on the left or an MAdd on the right expand.smmul_over_sum SMMul over MAdd/Add → MAdd (matrix, left=matrix right=scalar) expand.mmmul_over_madd MMMul over MAdd → MAdd (matrix) expand.vvmul_outer_over_vadd VVMul over VAdd → MAdd (outer product v wᵀ; a VAdd in v or inside Transpose(w)) expand.vvmul_inner_over_vadd VVMul over VAdd → Add (inner product vᵀ w; a VAdd inside Transpose(v) or in w) expand.hat_over_vadd Hat(a + b) = Hat(a) + Hat(b) expand.vee_over_madd Vee(A + B) = Vee(A) + Vee(B)

Transpose is not expanded on its own (Transpose(MAdd) and Transpose(VVMul) are left intact); the VVMul rule is the only place that looks through a Transpose(VAdd) factor, because a bare VAdd of transposed vectors is not a valid VVMul operand.

Row vectors that are not a Transpose node (aᵀK, s aᵀ, aᵀ + bᵀ) are distributed in place and keep their row form: (aᵀ(K + J)) b expands to aᵀK b + aᵀJ b. Inside such a row, a Transpose(VAdd) factor is split the same way as in a VVMul.

docs.title: expand(expr)
docs.text:
Distribute every product over sums, bottom up (rules in the module docstring).

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/expansion.py 
def expand(expr):
    """Distribute every product over sums, bottom up (rules in the module docstring)."""
    match expr:
        # --- N-ary additions: expand each term ---
        case Add(nodes=nodes):
            return Add(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        case VAdd(nodes=nodes):
            return VAdd(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        case MAdd(nodes=nodes):
            return MAdd(*[expand(n) for n in nodes])

        # --- Scalar * Scalar ---
        case Mul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Mul, Add, Add, Add, "expand.mul_over_add", expr)

        # --- Dot product (vector x vector → scalar) ---
        case Dot():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Dot, Add, VAdd, VAdd, "expand.dot_over_vadd", expr)

        # --- Cross product (vector x vector → vector) ---
        case Cross():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, Cross, VAdd, VAdd, VAdd, "expand.cross_over_vadd", expr)

        # --- Scalar * Vector  (left=vector, right=scalar) ---
        case SVMul() if is_row_vector(expr.left):
            return _expand_row_svmul(expr)

        case SVMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, SVMul, VAdd, VAdd, Add, "expand.svmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Matrix * Vector ---
        case MVMul() if expr.left.type == ExprType.VECTOR:
            return _expand_row_mvmul(expr)

        case MVMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, MVMul, VAdd, MAdd, VAdd, "expand.mvmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Scalar * Matrix  (left=matrix, right=scalar) ---
        case SMMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, SMMul, MAdd, MAdd, Add, "expand.smmul_over_sum", expr)

        # --- Matrix * Matrix ---
        case MMMul():
            l, r = expand(expr.left), expand(expr.right)
            return _distribute(l, r, MMMul, MAdd, MAdd, MAdd, "expand.mmmul_over_madd", expr)

        # --- Vector * Vector (outer product → matrix, inner product → scalar) ---
        case VVMul():
            return _expand_vvmul(expr)

        # --- Unary ops: recurse into child ---
        # Hat is linear: Hat(a + b) = Hat(a) + Hat(b)
        case Hat():
            inner = expand(expr.expr)
            if isinstance(inner, VAdd):
                return rule("expand.hat_over_vadd", expr, MAdd(*[Hat(n) for n in inner.nodes]))
            return Hat(inner)

        # Vee is linear: Vee(A + B) = Vee(A) + Vee(B)
        case Vee():
            inner = expand(expr.expr)
            if isinstance(inner, MAdd):
                return rule("expand.vee_over_madd", expr, VAdd(*[Vee(n) for n in inner.nodes]))
            return Vee(inner)

        case Variation():
            return calculus_node(Variation, expand(expr.expr))

        case TimeDerivative():
            return calculus_node(TimeDerivative, expand(expr.expr))

        case TimeIntegral():
            return TimeIntegral(expand(expr.expr))

        # --- Leaves and everything else ---
        case _:
            return expr

docs.title: manifold_rules
docs.text:
Manifold kinematic substitutions applied during EOM derivation.

For S2 (unit sphere) with manifold point q, tangent vector ω, variation vector ξ: - Variation(ω) → ξ̇ - 2 ω × ξ (Lee et al. eq. 5.13 on the constraint set ξ ⊥ q)

For SO3 (rotation group) with tangent vector Ω, variation vector η: - Variation(Ω) → η̇ + Ω × η (body-frame angular velocity convention)

Derivation for S2. The kinematics are q̇ = ω × q with ω ⊥ q (so ω = q × q̇) and the variation is δq = ξ × q with ξ ⊥ q. Lee et al. eq. (5.13) give the variation of the angular velocity as

δω = -S(ω) ξ + (I - q qᵀ) ξ̇ = ξ̇ - ω × ξ - q (q · ξ̇).

The last term is not zero. Differentiating the constraint ξ · q = 0 along the curve,

q · ξ̇ = -ξ · q̇ = -ξ · (ω × q) = q · (ω × ξ),

and because ω and ξ both lie in the tangent plane, ω × ξ is parallel to q, so q (q · ξ̇) = q (q · (ω × ξ)) = ω × ξ. Hence, on the constraint set,

δω = ξ̇ - 2 ω × ξ.

δω is not tangent to the sphere: its normal component is q · δω = -q · ξ̇ = -q · (ω × ξ), which is what keeps δ(ω · q) = 0. The earlier rule ξ̇ - ω × ξ is only the tangential projection (I - q qᵀ) δω; it is correct whenever ∂L/∂ω ⊥ q (every Lagrangian that depends on ω only through q̇ = ω × q) and wrong otherwise: with ∂L/∂ω = m l² ω + c the gyroscopic term 2 ω × c came out as ω × c, i.e. at half strength.

For SO3, with Ṙ = R·Hat(Ω) and δR = R·Hat(η), equating the mixed derivatives d/dt(δR) = δ(Ṙ) gives δΩ = η̇ + Ω × η exactly (Lee et al. eq. 6.9).

Rules (name, identity, hypothesis):

manifold.s2_variation_omega δ(ω) → ξ̇ - 2 ω × ξ ω is the tangent vector of an S2 point listed in SystemVariables (matched by printed name) manifold.so3_variation_Omega δ(Ω) → η̇ + Ω × η Ω is the tangent vector of an SO3 point listed in SystemVariables

docs.title: apply_manifold_rules(expr, variables)
docs.text:
Apply manifold kinematic substitutions to an expression.

Walks the expression tree and replaces Variation(TS2) and Variation(TSO3) nodes with their kinematic expansions.

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/manifold_rules.py 
def apply_manifold_rules(expr, variables: SystemVariables):
    """Apply manifold kinematic substitutions to an expression.

    Walks the expression tree and replaces Variation(TS2) and
    Variation(TSO3) nodes with their kinematic expansions.
    """
    tangent_map: dict[str, tuple[str, Expr, Expr, Expr]] = {}

    # S2 manifolds (vectors)
    for vec in variables.vectors:
        if isinstance(vec, S2):
            omega = vec.get_tangent_vector()
            xi = vec.get_variation_vector()
            tangent_map[str(omega)] = ("S2", vec, omega, xi)

    # SO3 manifolds (matrices)
    for mat in variables.matrices:
        if isinstance(mat, SO3):
            Omega = mat.get_tangent_vector()
            eta = mat.get_variation_vector()
            tangent_map[str(Omega)] = ("SO3", mat, Omega, eta)

    if not tangent_map:
        return expr

    return _substitute(expr, tangent_map)

docs.title: pulling
docs.text:
Pull scalar factors out of vector/matrix operations.

Bottom-up traversal over every node class (map_children in transformations.utils): the operands are pulled first, then the rules below are tried at the node. O(n), one pass; full_simplify repeats it to a fixed point.

Rules (name, identity; none needs a hypothesis beyond the operand classes shown; s, t are scalars, SVMul(v, s) is printed vs, a row is any row vector, see is_row_vector):

pull.dot_scaled Dot(a s, b t) = s (t Dot(a, b)); Dot(a s, b) = s Dot(a, b); Dot(a, b t) = t Dot(a, b) pull.svmul_nested (v s) t = v (s t) pull.cross_scaled Cross(a s, b t) = Cross(a, b) (s t); Cross(a s, b) = Cross(a, b) s; Cross(a, b t) = Cross(a, b) t pull.mvmul_scaled (A s)(v t) = (A v)(s t); (A s) v = (A v) s; A (v t) = (A v) t pull.row_mvmul_scaled (rᵀ s)(A t) = (rᵀ A)(s t); (rᵀ s) A = (rᵀ A) s; rᵀ (A t) = (rᵀ A) t a row times a matrix pull.smmul_nested (M s) t = M (s t) pull.mmmul_scaled (A s)(B t) = (A B)(s t); (A s) B = (A B) s; A (B t) = (A B) t pull.vvmul_scaled_row (rᵀ s) b = (rᵀ b) s inner product, the left factor is a scaled row SVMul(row, s) pull.vvmul_scaled rᵀ (b t) = (rᵀ b) t (inner product, scaled column); (a s) rᵀ = (a rᵀ) s and a (rᵀ t) = (a rᵀ) t (outer product) pull.transpose_scaled (v s)ᵀ = vᵀ s; (M s)ᵀ = Mᵀ s pull.hat_scaled Hat(v s) = Hat(v) s pull.vee_scaled Vee(M s) = Vee(M) s

An inner product (aᵀ s) b (a scaled row SVMul(aᵀ, s), which a.T() - b.T() builds for its second addend, or (a s)ᵀ, which becomes aᵀ s first) becomes aᵀb s, so it merges with s (aᵀ b). The calculus nodes have no rule: d/dt(v s) is not d/dt(v) s unless s is constant, so their operands are only recursed into.

docs.title: simplification
docs.text:
Simplification passes.

simplify(expr) — one pass: pull (hoist scalars), vector_rules (geometric identities), then _eliminate (bottom-up zeros, identities and numeric folding, the rules below). full_simplify(expr) — expand once, then simplify until the printed tree stops changing (at most max_iter passes; hitting the cap warns).

Rules of _eliminate (name, identity, hypothesis the code checks). "Zero" means the operand is flagged zero (Zero, ZeroVector, ZeroMatrix, a Constant symbol's variation...), "one" a numeric leaf with value 1, "identity" a leaf flagged Identity.

simplify.add_fold Add: zeros dropped, numeric leaves summed, like terms merged; float sums within 1e-12 of the largest magnitude are cancelled to 0 (_CANCEL_RTOL) simplify.vadd_fold VAdd: zeros dropped, like terms merged simplify.madd_fold MAdd: zeros dropped, like terms merged

Like terms (all three folds): an addend is split into a number (the product of every numeric literal in its flattened Mul chain and, for vectors and matrices, in the scalars of its SVMul/SMMul), its other scalar factors and its vector/matrix base; two addends merge when their bases are equal and their factors are equal as multisets (x(2)y + xy(3) → xy(5), v a + v a(-1) → 0, (vᵀw)s + s(vᵀw) → (vᵀw)s(2)). "Equal" is term_key: the operands of a Dot and of an inner product aᵀb commute (aᵀb s − bᵀa s → 0) and so do the factors of a Mul; every other product keeps its order. Grouping is one pass over the addends, keyed by term_key. Numeric literals are anonymous numbers only: a named Scalar("m", value=2) is a symbol and is never folded (decision D1); its value is used by geomech.numeric only. simplify.mul_fold Mul: a zero factor gives 0, a factor one is dropped, numeric factors of a Mul chain are multiplied into one number placed last; a float with an integer value becomes an int ((-1.0) → (-1))

Every numeric literal leaf is put in the spelling Number gives it ((2.0) → (2), Scalar("0.5", value=0.5) → (0.5)), so equal numbers print, and compare, the same. simplify.svmul_zero v·0 = 0·s = 0 (vector) simplify.svmul_one v·1 = v simplify.smmul_zero M·0 = 0·s = 0 (matrix) simplify.smmul_one M·1 = M simplify.mvmul_zero 0·v = M·0 = 0 simplify.mvmul_identity I·v = v left factor flagged identity (or its transpose) simplify.mvmul_hat_to_cross Hat(a)·v = Cross(a, v) simplify.mvmul_reassociate (A·B)·v = A·(B·v) simplify.mvmul_combine A·(B·v) = (A·B)·v only when A·B simplifies to a non-product (e.g. RᵀR = I) simplify.mmmul_zero 0·B = A·0 = 0 simplify.mmmul_identity I·B = B, A·I = A factor flagged identity (or its transpose) simplify.mmmul_reassociate (A·B)·C = A·(B·C) simplify.mmmul_combine A·(B·C) = (A·B)·C only when A·B simplifies to a non-product (e.g. RᵀR = I) simplify.orthogonal_transpose RᵀR = I and RRᵀ = I R flagged orthogonal (SO3), both factors equal by name simplify.vvmul_zero 0ᵀw = vᵀ0 = 0 (scalar), v0ᵀ = 0 (matrix) simplify.dot_zero Dot(0, w) = Dot(v, 0) = 0 simplify.cross_zero Cross(0, w) = Cross(v, 0) = 0 simplify.hat_zero Hat(0) = 0 simplify.hat_vee_skew Hat(Vee(X)) = X X skew-symmetric: a Hat, a leaf flagged SkewSymmetricMatrix, or a sum/scaling/transpose of such simplify.vee_zero Vee(0) = 0 simplify.vee_hat Vee(Hat(v)) = v simplify.transpose_transpose (Xᵀ)ᵀ = X simplify.transpose_symmetric Jᵀ = J J flagged symmetric (the identity I is) simplify.transpose_hat_skew Hat(v)ᵀ = -Hat(v) simplify.transpose_skew Sᵀ = -S S skew-symmetric (a leaf flagged SkewSymmetricMatrix, a sum or transpose of such), not a Hat or a scaled matrix simplify.transpose_scaled (M s)ᵀ = Mᵀ s simplify.transpose_scaled_row (aᵀ s)ᵀ = a s simplify.transpose_product (A·B)ᵀ = Bᵀ·Aᵀ simplify.variation_zero δ(0) = 0 simplify.time_derivative_zero d/dt(0) = 0 simplify.time_derivative_integral d/dt(∫x dt) = x simplify.time_integral_zero ∫0 dt = 0 simplify.time_integral_derivative ∫d/dt(x) dt = x

The rules of the other two stages of a pass are listed in pull and vector_rules.

docs.text: Expand once, then loop simplify until convergence.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
max_iter : int Safety cap on the number of passes (default 10). Hitting it emits a RuntimeWarning ("no confirmed fixed point after N passes") naming the expression: the result may be unsimplified. A pass that changes nothing ends the loop, so the warning fires only when the last allowed pass still changed the expression; that last result may already be the fixed point, which only one more pass could confirm (hence "confirmed").

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/simplification.py 
def full_simplify(expr, max_iter=10):
    """Expand once, then loop simplify until convergence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    max_iter : int
        Safety cap on the number of passes (default 10). Hitting it emits a
        ``RuntimeWarning`` ("no confirmed fixed point after N passes") naming the
        expression: the result may be unsimplified. A pass that changes nothing ends the
        loop, so the warning fires only when the last allowed pass still changed the
        expression; that last result may already be the fixed point, which only one more
        pass could confirm (hence "confirmed").
    """
    expr = expand(expr)
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        prev = expr
        expr = simplify(expr)
        if str(expr) == str(prev):
            break
    else:
        why = (
            "max_iter=0: no simplify pass ran"
            if max_iter <= 0
            else f"the last pass still changed the expression, so no fixed point after"
            f" {max_iter} passes was confirmed by an unchanged pass"
        )
        warnings.warn(
            f"full_simplify: no confirmed fixed point after {max_iter} passes ({why});"
            f" result may be unsimplified: {expr!r}",
            RuntimeWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return expr

docs.title: term_key(expr)
docs.text:
A canonical string for expr up to the commutativity the like-term merge knows.

Two expressions have the same key exactly when they are the same tree except that the operands of a Dot may be swapped, the factors of a Mul chain may be reordered, and an inner product aᵀb of two columns (VVMul(Transpose(a), b)) may be written bᵀa (at any depth). Every other node compares its operands in order, and a leaf by class and printed name. The key is injective on such classes: a leaf is written Class#len#name (the length makes it self-delimiting), a node Class(key,key,...) with the operand keys sorted for Dot and the flattened Mul factors, and an inner product VVMul.inner(key,key) with the keys of its two columns sorted.

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/simplification.py 
def term_key(expr) -> str:
    """A canonical string for *expr* up to the commutativity the like-term merge knows.

    Two expressions have the same key exactly when they are the same tree except that the
    operands of a ``Dot`` may be swapped, the factors of a ``Mul`` chain may be reordered,
    and an inner product ``aᵀb`` of two columns (``VVMul(Transpose(a), b)``) may be
    written ``bᵀa`` (at any depth). Every other node compares its operands in order, and a leaf
    by class and printed name. The key is injective on such classes: a leaf is written
    ``Class#len#name`` (the length makes it self-delimiting), a node
    ``Class(key,key,...)`` with the operand keys sorted for ``Dot`` and the flattened
    ``Mul`` factors, and an inner product ``VVMul.inner(key,key)`` with the keys of its
    two columns sorted.
    """
    nodes = getattr(expr, "nodes", None)
    cls = type(expr).__name__
    if not nodes:
        name = str(expr)
        return f"{cls}#{len(name)}#{name}"
    if isinstance(expr, Mul):
        keys = sorted(term_key(f) for f in flatten_mul(expr))
    elif (
        isinstance(expr, VVMul)
        and expr.type == ExprType.SCALAR
        and isinstance(expr.left, Transpose)
    ):
        # the inner product aᵀb of two columns is symmetric: aᵀb = bᵀa
        keys = sorted((term_key(expr.left.expr), term_key(expr.right)))
        return "VVMul.inner(" + ",".join(keys) + ")"
    elif isinstance(expr, Dot):
        keys = sorted(term_key(n) for n in nodes)
    else:
        keys = [term_key(n) for n in nodes]
    return cls + "(" + ",".join(keys) + ")"

Structural helpers shared by the tree rewrites.

rebuild(expr, children) makes a node of the same class as expr with new children, and map_children(expr, fn) applies fn to every child and rebuilds only when a child changed. vector_rules, pull and apply_manifold_rules recurse through every node class with these two functions, so a rule written for one node fires wherever that node sits in the tree (under a Dot, Hat, MVMul, a calculus operator, ...).

addends(expr), sum_of(terms, expr_type) and flatten_mul(expr) take sums and product chains apart and put them back together; the simplifier, integration by parts, to_standard_form and linearize share them.

cls(operand) for a calculus class, in eager form over a manifold point.

A rewrite of the operand of TimeDerivative/Variation can reduce it to a bare S2/SO3 leaf (d/dt(q·(q·q)) → d/dt(q)). The tree never holds that node (the constructor rejects it), so the leaf's own kinematics are returned instead: q.t_diff()/R.t_diff() for TimeDerivative and q.delta()/R.delta() for Variation. Any other operand gives cls(operand).

def calculus_node(cls, operand):
    """``cls(operand)`` for a calculus class, in eager form over a manifold point.

    A rewrite of the operand of ``TimeDerivative``/``Variation`` can reduce it to a bare
    ``S2``/``SO3`` leaf (``d/dt(q·(q·q))`` → ``d/dt(q)``). The tree never holds that node
    (the constructor rejects it), so the leaf's own kinematics are returned instead:
    ``q.t_diff()``/``R.t_diff()`` for ``TimeDerivative`` and ``q.delta()``/``R.delta()`` for
    ``Variation``. Any other operand gives ``cls(operand)``.
    """
    if isinstance(operand, (S2, SO3)):
        if cls is TimeDerivative:
            return operand.t_diff()
        if cls is Variation:
            return operand.delta()
    return cls(operand)

docs.title: flatten_mul(expr)
docs.text:
The factors of a scalar Mul chain, left to right ([expr] for a non-Mul).

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/utils.py 
def flatten_mul(expr: Expr) -> list[Expr]:
    """The factors of a scalar ``Mul`` chain, left to right (``[expr]`` for a non-``Mul``)."""
    factors: list[Expr] = []
    stack = [expr]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(node, Mul):
            stack.append(node.right)
            stack.append(node.left)
        else:
            factors.append(node)
    return factors

def map_children(expr, fn, caller="map_children"):
    """*expr* with *fn* applied to each child; the same object when no child changed.

    A leaf (no children) is returned as is.
    """
    nodes = getattr(expr, "nodes", None)
    if not nodes:
        return expr
    new = [fn(n) for n in nodes]
    if all(a is b for a, b in zip(new, nodes)):
        return expr
    return rebuild(expr, new, caller)

def rebuild(expr, children, caller="rebuild"):
    """A node of the class of *expr* with *children* in place of its operands.

    N-ary sums take all children, the binary products and ``Dot``/``Cross`` two, the unary
    operators (``Hat``, ``Vee``, ``Transpose`` and the calculus nodes) one. A
    ``TimeDerivative``/``Variation`` whose new operand is a bare manifold leaf is built in
    eager form (see ``calculus_node``). Any other class
    raises ``TypeError`` naming *caller*: returning the old node would silently drop the
    rewrite of a child.
    """
    cls = type(expr)
    if isinstance(expr, (Add, VAdd, MAdd)):
        return cls(*children)
    if isinstance(expr, (Mul, SVMul, SMMul, MVMul, MMMul, VVMul, Dot, Cross)):
        return cls(children[0], children[1])
    if isinstance(expr, (Variation, TimeDerivative)):
        return calculus_node(cls, children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, (Hat, Vee, Transpose, TimeIntegral)):
        return cls(children[0])
    raise TypeError(
        f"{caller}: cannot rebuild a {cls.__name__} node ('{expr}') with rewritten"
        " children; add the class to geomech.core.transformations.utils.rebuild"
    )

terms added up as a sum of expr_type: the inverse of addends.

No term gives the zero of the type (zero_of), one term is returned as it is, several make an Add, VAdd or MAdd. A missing type counts as scalar.

Source code in geomech/core/transformations/utils.py 
def sum_of(terms: list[Expr], expr_type: ExprType | None) -> Expr:
    """``terms`` added up as a sum of *expr_type*: the inverse of ``addends``.

    No term gives the zero of the type (``zero_of``), one term is returned as it is,
    several make an ``Add``, ``VAdd`` or ``MAdd``. A missing type counts as scalar.
    """
    if not terms:
        return zero_of(expr_type)
    if len(terms) == 1:
        return terms[0]
    match expr_type:
        case ExprType.VECTOR:
            return VAdd(*terms)
        case ExprType.MATRIX:
            return MAdd(*terms)
        case _:
            return Add(*terms)

docs.title: vector_identities
docs.text:
Algebraic identities for vector/matrix geometry operations (vector_rules).

One bottom-up pass over every node class (map_children in transformations.utils): the operands of a node are rewritten first, then the rules below are tried at the node, so an identity fires wherever its node sits, under a Dot, Hat, MVMul, Transpose or a calculus operator included. Equality of two operands is == (type + printed name), so two S2("q") objects are the same point.

Rules (name, identity, hypothesis the code checks):

vector.dot_zero Dot(x, 0) = Dot(0, x) = 0 an operand is flagged zero vector.dot_cross_orthogonal Dot(x, Cross(x, y)) = Dot(x, Cross(y, x)) = 0, Dot(z, Cross(y, y)) = 0, and the mirror with the Cross on the left; x equal to a Cross operand, or the two Cross operands equal vector.dot_unit_norm Dot(q, q) = 1 both operands flagged unit norm (S2 points) and equal vector.dot_tangent_orthogonal Dot(w, q) = Dot(q, w) = 0 w a TS2 leaf (ω or ξ) whose S2 point equals q by name vector.cross_self Cross(x, x) = 0 operands equal vector.cross_zero Cross(x, 0) = Cross(0, x) = 0 an operand is flagged zero vector.cross_scaled_self Cross(a, a s) = Cross(a s, a) = 0 the SVMul's vector equals the other operand vector.s2_tangent_recovery Cross(q, Cross(a, q)) = a and Cross(Cross(q, a), q) = a q an S2 point (unit norm), a tangent to q: a TS2 leaf of q (by name) or a Cross with q as an operand vector.s2_tangent_negated Cross(q, Cross(q, a)) = -a and Cross(Cross(a, q), q) = -a same hypothesis as vector.s2_tangent_recovery vector.s2_double_cross Cross(a, Cross(a, q)) = -q (a·a) q an S2 point, a tangent to q (as above) vector.hat_zero Hat(0) = 0 (matrix) the operand is flagged zero

Before 5.1 the pass stopped at Dot operands, Hat, MVMul and the calculus nodes, so Dot(v, q×(ω×q)), Hat(a×a) or J(a×a) survived full_simplify.

The tangency test does not look inside TimeDerivative/Variation: ω̇ ⊥ q holds on S² but needs a constraint system to prove, so Cross(q, Cross(ω̇, q)) is kept.

def block_shape(self, row, col) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Shape of the block at (*row*, *col*); *col* may be a symbol or its ``str``."""
    row_key = row if isinstance(row, str) else str(row)
    col_key = col if isinstance(col, str) else str(col)
    if row_key not in self.row_types:
        raise KeyError(f"LinearizedSystem: unknown row '{row_key}'")
    if col_key not in self.col_types:
        raise KeyError(f"LinearizedSystem: unknown column '{col_key}'")
    n_rows = 1 if self.row_types[row_key] == ExprType.SCALAR else 3
    n_cols = 1 if self.col_types[col_key] == ExprType.SCALAR else 3
    return (n_rows, n_cols)

docs.title: compute_eom(lagrangian, inf_work, variables, params=(), *, trace=None)
docs.text:
Compute equations of motion using the principle of least action.

Stages, in the order the code runs them (docs/pipeline.md has one paragraph per stage; the bracketed names are the EOMTrace stage names):

  1. [dL] the variation of the Lagrangian, [dW] the virtual work, and [dS] the infinitesimal action integral δS = δL + δW
  2. [manifold_rules] apply_manifold_rules: δω and δΩ replaced by their kinematic expansions (S², SO(3))
  3. [simplify] full_simplify (expand once, then simplify to a fixed point)
  4. integration by parts against the time derivative of each variation vector: [ibp.prepare] expand + full_simplify, then per target [ibp.collect[t]] (rotate each term so the target is the left operand of a Dot), [ibp.integrate[t]] (one IBP pass) and [ibp.simplify[t]]; [ibp] is the result
  5. [expand]
  6. per variation vector: extract_linear_coeff [raw[ξ]], then full_simplify [equation[ξ]]

trace (keyword only) is an EOMTrace: it is filled with every stage as the pipeline runs, so after an exception it holds the stages before the failure and trace.failed_at names the stage that raised (trace.summary(), trace.show("simplify")). The trace is cleared first, so a reused trace holds this run only. Without a trace, and with the geomech logger not at DEBUG, nothing is recorded. With GEOMECH_DEBUG=1 each stage is logged and check_tree runs on the inputs and the equations.

An extraction failure is re-raised with the same exception type and the pipeline context: the variation vector, and when a time derivative of a variation vector survived integration by parts, the term it survived in.

inf_work may be None or 0 for a conservative system. It must be linear in the variation vectors themselves: a time derivative of a listed variation vector in inf_work (Dot(x.t_diff().delta(), f), Dot(ξ.t_diff(), f)) raises ValueError. variables must list at least one configuration variable (ValueError "no configuration variables" otherwise; this check runs last, so a Lagrangian that holds a symbol first fails the stray-variation check below); params must be a sequence of leaves (TypeError).

Every symbol in lagrangian and inf_work is one of three things: a configuration variable (listed in variables, varied by Hamilton's principle), a constant (attr=["Constant"]), or a prescribed time-varying parameter declared in params (a plain non-constant Scalar/Vector/Matrix leaf such as a cable length l(t): its rate l̇ appears in the equations, its variation δl is not free and is dropped). A variation symbol that survives extraction and belongs to none of these (δx of an unlisted x, ξ/δω of an unlisted S2 point, …) raises ValueError naming it: before, such terms were dropped silently and the system lost a degree of freedom. numeric.check_eom takes the same params. A param printed like a different leaf of lagrangian or inf_work (a constant l of L declared as Scalar("l")) raises ValueError: it would have no effect. to_standard_form accepts the result (a param's rate stays in f, the param itself in M); linearize does not support prescribed parameters yet and raises AlgebraicError on the δl term.

Source code in geomech/dynamics/eom.py 
def compute_eom(
    lagrangian: Expr,
    inf_work: Expr | int | float | None,
    variables: SystemVariables,
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    *,
    trace: EOMTrace | None = None,
) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """Compute equations of motion using the principle of least action.

    Stages, in the order the code runs them (``docs/pipeline.md`` has one paragraph per
    stage; the bracketed names are the ``EOMTrace`` stage names):

    1. ``[dL]`` the variation of the Lagrangian, ``[dW]`` the virtual work, and
       ``[dS]`` the infinitesimal action integral δS = δL + δW
    2. ``[manifold_rules]`` ``apply_manifold_rules``: δω and δΩ replaced by their
       kinematic expansions (S², SO(3))
    3. ``[simplify]`` ``full_simplify`` (expand once, then simplify to a fixed point)
    4. integration by parts against the time derivative of each variation vector:
       ``[ibp.prepare]`` expand + full_simplify, then per target ``[ibp.collect[t]]``
       (rotate each term so the target is the left operand of a ``Dot``),
       ``[ibp.integrate[t]]`` (one IBP pass) and ``[ibp.simplify[t]]``; ``[ibp]`` is
       the result
    5. ``[expand]``
    6. per variation vector: ``extract_linear_coeff`` ``[raw[ξ]]``, then
       ``full_simplify`` ``[equation[ξ]]``

    ``trace`` (keyword only) is an ``EOMTrace``: it is filled with every stage as the
    pipeline runs, so after an exception it holds the stages before the failure and
    ``trace.failed_at`` names the stage that raised (``trace.summary()``,
    ``trace.show("simplify")``). The trace is cleared first, so a reused trace holds
    this run only. Without a trace, and with the
    ``geomech`` logger not at ``DEBUG``, nothing is recorded. With ``GEOMECH_DEBUG=1``
    each stage is logged and ``check_tree`` runs on the inputs and the equations.

    An extraction failure is re-raised with the same exception type and the pipeline
    context: the variation vector, and when a time derivative of a variation vector
    survived integration by parts, the term it survived in.

    ``inf_work`` may be ``None`` or ``0`` for a conservative system. It must be linear in
    the variation vectors themselves: a time derivative of a listed variation vector in
    ``inf_work`` (``Dot(x.t_diff().delta(), f)``, ``Dot(ξ.t_diff(), f)``) raises
    ``ValueError``. ``variables`` must list at least one configuration variable
    (``ValueError`` "no configuration variables" otherwise; this check runs last, so a
    Lagrangian that holds a symbol first fails the stray-variation check below);
    ``params`` must be a sequence of leaves (``TypeError``).

    Every symbol in ``lagrangian`` and ``inf_work`` is one of three things: a
    configuration variable (listed in ``variables``, varied by Hamilton's principle), a
    constant (``attr=["Constant"]``), or a prescribed time-varying parameter declared in
    ``params`` (a plain non-constant ``Scalar``/``Vector``/``Matrix`` leaf such as a cable
    length ``l(t)``: its rate ``l̇`` appears in the equations, its variation ``δl`` is not
    free and is dropped). A variation symbol that survives extraction and belongs to none
    of these (``δx`` of an unlisted ``x``, ``ξ``/``δω`` of an unlisted ``S2`` point, …)
    raises ``ValueError`` naming it: before, such terms were dropped silently and the
    system lost a degree of freedom. ``numeric.check_eom`` takes the same ``params``. A
    param printed like a different leaf of ``lagrangian`` or ``inf_work`` (a constant
    ``l`` of ``L`` declared as ``Scalar("l")``) raises ``ValueError``: it would have no
    effect.
    ``to_standard_form`` accepts the result (a param's rate stays in ``f``, the param
    itself in ``M``); ``linearize`` does not support prescribed parameters yet and raises
    ``AlgebraicError`` on the ``δl`` term.
    """
    if trace is not None:
        trace._reset()
    stage = "validation"
    try:
        check_variables(variables)
        if not isinstance(params, (Expr, str)) and hasattr(params, "__iter__"):
            params = list(params)  # a generator is read twice (here and the clash check)
        param_names = _check_params(params, variables)
        if isinstance(inf_work, bool):
            raise TypeError(
                "compute_eom: inf_work must be a scalar expression, None or 0, got bool"
                f" {inf_work}"
            )
        if inf_work is None or (isinstance(inf_work, (int, float)) and inf_work == 0):
            inf_work = Zero
        _check_scalar_input("lagrangian", lagrangian)
        _check_scalar_input("inf_work", inf_work)
        check_symbol_clash(
            params,
            [lagrangian, inf_work],
            "compute_eom",
            role="params entry",
            what="a prescribed parameter",
            where="the Lagrangian or the virtual work",
        )

        # gather variation vectors and their time derivatives
        variation_vectors = []
        variation_vector_dots = []

        for s in variables.scalars:
            ds = s.delta()  # Variation(scalar) — scalar type
            variation_vectors.append(ds)
            variation_vector_dots.append(ds.t_diff())

        for vec in variables.vectors:
            x = vec.get_variation_vector()
            variation_vectors.append(x)
            variation_vector_dots.append(x.t_diff())

        for mat in variables.matrices:
            x = mat.get_variation_vector()
            variation_vectors.append(x)
            variation_vector_dots.append(x.t_diff())

        allowed = {str(v) for v in variation_vectors}
        _check_virtual_work(inf_work, variables, allowed)

        debug = debug_enabled()
        if debug:
            check_tree(lagrangian)
            check_tree(inf_work)
        record = stage_recorder(trace, "compute_eom")
        if trace is not None:
            trace.variation_vectors = list(variation_vectors)
            trace.ibp_targets = list(variation_vector_dots)

        # variation of the Lagrangian
        stage = "dL"
        dL = lagrangian.delta()

        # infinitesimal action integral
        dS = dL + inf_work
        if record is not None:
            record("dL", dL)
            record("dW", inf_work)
            record("dS", dS)

        # apply manifold kinematic substitutions
        stage = "manifold_rules"
        dS = apply_manifold_rules(dS, variables)
        if record is not None:
            record("manifold_rules", dS)

        stage = "simplify"
        dS = full_simplify(dS)
        if record is not None:
            record("simplify", dS)

        # integration by parts
        stage = "ibp"
        try:
            dS = _integrate_by_parts(dS, variation_vector_dots, record)
        except (AlgebraicError, NonLinearError) as err:
            raise type(err)(
                f"compute_eom: while integrating by parts (stage ibp, targets"
                f" {', '.join(f'{t}' for t in variation_vector_dots)}): {err}"
            ) from err
        if record is not None:
            record("ibp", dS)

        # expand
        stage = "expand"
        dS = expand(dS)
        if record is not None:
            record("expand", dS)

        # extract equations of motion
        stage = "extract"
        try:
            eom = _separate_variations(dS, variation_vectors, record)
        except _ExtractionFailure as failure:
            # retold with L when it depends on accelerations; otherwise the δS message
            raise failure.retold(dS, variation_vectors, lagrangian, variables) from (
                failure.engine
            )
        if debug:
            for _, eq in eom.values():
                check_tree(eq)

        stage = "stray_check"
        # a variation symbol that survives extraction belongs to no listed variable or param
        wrapped: dict[str, str] = {}  # δ(d/dt(x)) built by hand → x
        stray = _stray_variation_symbols(dS, allowed, param_names, wrapped)
        for _, eq in eom.values():
            stray.update(_stray_variation_symbols(eq, allowed, param_names, wrapped))
        if stray:
            symbols = ", ".join(f"'{s}'" for s in sorted(stray))
            names = ", ".join(f"'{n}'" for n in sorted(set(stray.values())))
            message = (
                f"compute_eom: δS still contains the variation symbols {symbols} of the symbols"
                f" {names}, which are neither entries of SystemVariables nor declared in params"
            )
            if any(sym not in wrapped for sym in stray):
                message += (
                    "; for each symbol, list it in SystemVariables, declare it in params=..., or"
                    " mark it 'Constant'"
                )
            for sym, leaf in sorted(wrapped.items()):
                message += (
                    f"; '{sym}' is the variation of a time derivative, which the engine never"
                    f" builds: write the variation of the configuration variable itself,"
                    f" {leaf}.delta() (the variation of the velocity is {leaf}.t_diff().delta(),"
                    " built as d/dt of the variation, and is not allowed in inf_work)"
                )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if not variation_vectors:
            raise ValueError(
                "compute_eom: no configuration variables listed in SystemVariables; a system"
                " with no degree of freedom has no equation of motion"
            )
        return eom
    except Exception as err:
        if trace is not None:
            trace._fail(_failed_stage(trace, stage, err), err)
        raise

Source code in geomech/dynamics/vbl.py 
def linearize(
    eom: dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]],
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] | None = None,
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    *,
    trace: LinearizationTrace | None = None,
) -> LinearizedSystem:
    """Linearize the equations of motion along an arbitrary trajectory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    eom : dict
        Output of ``compute_eom``: ``{str(variation_vec): (variation_vec, eom_expr)}``.
    variables : SystemVariables
        The configuration variables used for ``compute_eom``.
    inputs : list[Scalar | Vector], optional
        Input symbols (forces, torques, thrust). Their variations form δu.
    params : list, optional
        The prescribed parameters passed to ``compute_eom(..., params=...)``. Prescribed
        parameters are not supported by ``linearize`` yet: a term carrying the variation
        of a declared param raises ``AlgebraicError`` saying so (without ``params`` the
        message cannot tell a param from a missing input or a missing ``Constant``).
    trace : LinearizationTrace, optional
        Keyword only. Filled per dynamic row with δE, the partition buckets, the raw
        coefficients (before ``full_simplify`` and before the mass blocks are negated)
        and the final blocks; see ``LinearizationTrace``. Cleared when the call
        starts; after an exception ``trace.failed_at`` names the stage that raised.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearizedSystem
        Blocks of ``M δẋ = A δx + B δu`` (see the module docstring for the sign
        convention and the kinematic rows).

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        Invalid ``variables`` or ``inputs`` (not plain ``Scalar``/``Vector`` leaves, or a
        ``set``/``dict``, whose order would be that of the columns of ``B``),
        a non-``SO3`` matrix configuration, or an equation whose type differs from
        that of its variation vector (a scalar equation under a vector key).
    ValueError
        Constant or duplicate inputs (the input checks are ``check_inputs``, shared with
        ``to_standard_form``), an input that is also a configuration variable
        or a tangent vector (``Ω``, ``ω``) whose variation is already a state, an input
        printed like a velocity, an acceleration or a different node of the equations
        (a constant ``g`` of ``L`` given as ``Scalar("g")``, another class, ``attr`` or
        size, or an operation node such as ``d/dt(l)``), or
        ``eom`` keys that do not match ``variables``. A stray variation symbol in an
        equation also surfaces as the engine's ``ValueError`` (δ of a variation is
        not representable).
    AlgebraicError
        An input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of ``compute_eom`` given as
        an input, ``check_inputs``). A term of δE carries no perturbation symbol, more
        than one (a nonlinear or incompletely distributed term), or one only inside a
        non-canonical calculus node, or a coefficient could not be factored.
    """
    if trace is not None:
        trace._reset()
    stage = "validation"
    try:
        check_variables(variables, caller="linearize")
        cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts = perturbation_variables(variables)
        _check_eom(eom, variables)
        param_names = _param_names(params)
        debug = debug_enabled()
        if debug:
            for _, eq in eom.values():
                check_tree(eq)
        record = stage_recorder(trace, "linearize")
        states = cfg_perts + vel_perts
        dstates = [s.t_diff() for s in states]
        inputs = check_inputs(inputs, variables, [eq for _, eq in eom.values()], "linearize")
        input_perts = [u.delta() for u in inputs]
        dvel_perts = dstates[len(cfg_perts) :]

        col_types = {}
        for sym in states + dstates + input_perts:
            col_types[str(sym)] = sym.type

        rows: list[str] = []
        row_types: dict[str, ExprType] = {}
        M: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        A: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        B: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        blocks = _Blocks(rows, row_types, M, A, B, dstates, states, input_perts)

        for i, var in enumerate(cfg_vars):
            _kinematic_row(blocks, var, cfg_perts[i], vel_perts[i], dstates[i])

        # Priority order for assigning a term to its perturbation symbol: the most
        # deeply wrapped symbols first, so that a term in d/dt(δv) is never tested
        # for δv (which would raise inside has_algebraic).
        priority = dvel_perts + vel_perts + cfg_perts + input_perts
        all_perts = priority + [d for d in dstates[: len(cfg_perts)]]
        n_mass = len(dvel_perts)
        n_state = n_mass + len(vel_perts) + len(cfg_perts)

        for label, (var_vec, eq) in eom.items():
            stage = f"row[{label}]"
            _dynamic_row(
                blocks,
                label,
                var_vec,
                eq,
                priority,
                all_perts,
                n_mass,
                n_state,
                param_names,
                record,
                debug,
            )

        return LinearizedSystem(
            rows=rows,
            states=states,
            dstates=dstates,
            inputs=input_perts,
            M=M,
            A=A,
            B=B,
            row_types=row_types,
            col_types=col_types,
        )
    except Exception as err:
        if trace is not None:
            trace._fail(_failed_row_stage(trace, stage), err)
        raise

def separate_variations(
    inf_action_integral: Expr, variation_vectors: Sequence[Expr]
) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """Extract the equation of motion for each variation vector.

    Returns a dict mapping str(variation_vector) → (variation_vector, equation). An
    ``AlgebraicError``/``NonLinearError`` from the extraction is re-raised (same type)
    naming the variation vector and, if a time derivative of a variation vector is left
    in δS, the term that holds it.
    """
    try:
        return _separate_variations(inf_action_integral, variation_vectors)
    except _ExtractionFailure as failure:
        raise failure.retold(inf_action_integral, variation_vectors) from failure.engine

docs.title: Parameters

Default (None): no inputs. Validated by check_inputs, exactly as in linearize: a TypeError for an entry that is not a plain Scalar/Vector leaf, one leaf instead of a sequence, or a set/dict (the order of inputs is the order of the input columns), a ValueError for a constant or duplicate input, a configuration variable, a tangent or variation vector (ω, ξ, Ω, η), or an input printed like a velocity or acceleration, or like a different node of the equations (a constant g of L given as Scalar("g"), another class, attr or size, or an operation node such as d/dt(l)), since leaves are matched by printed name; an AlgebraicError for an input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of compute_eom). A non-dict eom_dict raises TypeError.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: dict[str, StandardFormEquation] Keyed by the same variation vector names as eom_dict.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
On S² the equation E = 0 of a variable q is only meaningful on the tangent plane, (I − qqᵀ) E = 0: E is the coefficient of ξ ⊥ q and in general has a component along q (from the forcing, from ω × c, from A ω̇, …). The blocks returned here are the terms of E as derived, not projected. To solve for ω̇ solve (I − qqᵀ)(M ω̇ + f + Σ G u) = 0 with ω̇ ⊥ q; the unprojected 3×3 solve gives q · ω̇ ≠ 0 and a trajectory that leaves the sphere. The same holds for the rows of linearize.

Errors name the equation and the term: a term that holds an acceleration only under a further time derivative (a jerk d/dt(ẍ)) raises AlgebraicError saying the equation is not second order; a term bilinear in two accelerations raises NonLinearError. With GEOMECH_DEBUG=1 the blocks of each equation are logged on the geomech logger and check_tree runs on every equation and block.

def to_standard_form(
    eom_dict: dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]],
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, StandardFormEquation]:
    """Decompose EOM into standard manipulator form.

    Parameters
    ----------
    eom_dict : dict
        Output of ``compute_eom()``:
        ``{str(variation_vec): (variation_vec, eom_expr)}``.
    variables : SystemVariables
        Configuration variables (used to derive acceleration variables).
    inputs : list[Scalar | Vector], optional
        Input variables (forces, torques). Default (``None``): no inputs. Validated by
        ``check_inputs``, exactly as in ``linearize``: a ``TypeError`` for an entry that
        is not a plain ``Scalar``/``Vector`` leaf, one leaf instead of a sequence, or a
        ``set``/``dict`` (the order of *inputs* is the order of the input columns), a
        ``ValueError`` for a constant or duplicate input, a configuration variable, a
        tangent or variation vector (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``), or an input printed like
        a velocity or acceleration, or like a different node of the equations (a constant
        ``g`` of ``L`` given as ``Scalar("g")``, another class, ``attr`` or size, or an
        operation node such as ``d/dt(l)``), since leaves are matched by printed name; an
        ``AlgebraicError`` for an input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of
        ``compute_eom``). A non-dict *eom_dict* raises ``TypeError``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, StandardFormEquation]
        Keyed by the same variation vector names as *eom_dict*.

    Notes
    -----
    On S² the equation ``E = 0`` of a variable ``q`` is only meaningful on the tangent
    plane, ``(I − qqᵀ) E = 0``: ``E`` is the coefficient of ``ξ ⊥ q`` and in general has
    a component along ``q`` (from the forcing, from ``ω × c``, from ``A ω̇``, …). The
    blocks returned here are the terms of ``E`` as derived, not projected. To solve for
    ``ω̇`` solve ``(I − qqᵀ)(M ω̇ + f + Σ G u) = 0`` with ``ω̇ ⊥ q``; the unprojected
    3×3 solve gives ``q · ω̇ ≠ 0`` and a trajectory that leaves the sphere. The same
    holds for the rows of ``linearize``.

    Errors name the equation and the term: a term that holds an acceleration only under
    a further time derivative (a jerk ``d/dt(ẍ)``) raises ``AlgebraicError`` saying the
    equation is not second order; a term bilinear in two accelerations raises
    ``NonLinearError``. With ``GEOMECH_DEBUG=1`` the blocks of each equation are logged
    on the ``geomech`` logger and ``check_tree`` runs on every equation and block.
    """
    if not isinstance(eom_dict, dict):
        raise TypeError(
            f"to_standard_form: eom must be the dict returned by compute_eom, got {type(eom_dict)}"
        )
    inputs = check_inputs(
        inputs, variables, [eq for _, eq in eom_dict.values()], "to_standard_form"
    )

    accel_vars = _get_accel_vars(variables)
    debug = debug_enabled()
    record = stage_recorder(None, "to_standard_form")

    result = {}
    for key, (var_vec, eom_expr) in eom_dict.items():
        if debug:
            check_tree(eom_expr)
        sf = _extract_single(eom_expr, accel_vars, inputs, key)
        if record is not None:
            for name, block in sf.M.items():
                record(f"M[{key}][{name}]", block)
            record(f"f[{key}]", sf.f)
            for name, block in sf.G.items():
                record(f"G[{key}][{name}]", block)
        if debug:
            for block in (*sf.M.values(), sf.f, *sf.G.values()):
                check_tree(block)
        result[key] = sf

    return result

docs.title: check_inputs(inputs, variables, exprs, caller)
docs.text:
Validate the inputs of to_standard_form/linearize; return them as a list.

None means no inputs. inputs must be an ordered sequence of leaves (a list, tuple or generator), not one leaf, nor a set or a dict (TypeError): the order is the order of the columns of B and of the codegen u vector. Each input must be a plain non-manifold Scalar or Vector leaf (TypeError for an S2/SO3 point, a Matrix or an expression such as d/dt(x) or F + u), and is rejected with ValueError if it is a tangent or variation vector (ω, ξ, Ω, η), constant (attr=['Constant'], a number, zero), a configuration variable, printed like the velocity or acceleration of one (Vector("\frac{d}{dt}(x)")), a symbol whose variation prints like a perturbation state (a plain Vector named like Ω), listed twice, or printed like a different node of exprs (check_symbol_clash: another leaf, or an operation node). An input whose time derivative occurs in exprs (a prescribed param of compute_eom given as an input, l with l̇ in the equations) raises AlgebraicError: neither function can take a coefficient of u̇. Messages start with caller. to_standard_form, linearize and StateLayout (with no exprs) call this, so they accept and reject the same inputs.

def check_inputs(
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] | None,
    variables: SystemVariables,
    exprs: Sequence[object],
    caller: str,
) -> list[Expr]:
    """Validate the ``inputs`` of ``to_standard_form``/``linearize``; return them as a list.

    ``None`` means no inputs. *inputs* must be an ordered sequence of leaves (a list,
    tuple or generator), not one leaf, nor a ``set`` or a ``dict`` (``TypeError``): the
    order is the order of the columns of ``B`` and of the codegen ``u`` vector. Each
    input must be a plain non-manifold ``Scalar`` or ``Vector`` leaf (``TypeError`` for
    an ``S2``/``SO3`` point, a ``Matrix`` or an expression such as ``d/dt(x)`` or
    ``F + u``), and is rejected with ``ValueError`` if it is a tangent or variation
    vector (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``), constant (``attr=['Constant']``, a number,
    zero), a configuration variable, printed like the velocity or acceleration of one
    (``Vector("\\frac{d}{dt}(x)")``), a symbol whose variation prints like a perturbation
    state (a plain ``Vector`` named like ``Ω``), listed twice, or printed like a
    different node of *exprs* (``check_symbol_clash``: another leaf, or an operation
    node). An input whose time derivative occurs in *exprs* (a prescribed param of
    ``compute_eom`` given as an input, ``l`` with ``l̇`` in the equations) raises
    ``AlgebraicError``: neither function can take a coefficient of ``u̇``. Messages start
    with *caller*. ``to_standard_form``, ``linearize`` and ``StateLayout`` (with no
    *exprs*) call this, so they accept and reject the same inputs.
    """
    if inputs is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(inputs, (Expr, str)) or not hasattr(inputs, "__iter__"):
        hint = f"; write inputs=[{inputs}]" if isinstance(inputs, Expr) else ""
        raise TypeError(
            f"{caller}: inputs must be a sequence of Scalar/Vector leaves, got"
            f" {type(inputs).__name__} {str(inputs)!r}{hint}"
        )
    container = inputs
    inputs = list(inputs)
    for u in inputs:
        if not isinstance(u, (Scalar, Vector)) or isinstance(u, S2):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' must be a Scalar or Vector leaf, got {type(u).__name__}"
            )
    if isinstance(container, (AbstractSet, Mapping)):
        why = (
            "a mapping is iterated by its keys (pass a list of the inputs)"
            if isinstance(container, Mapping)
            else "a set has no order, so the columns of B would depend on the hash seed"
        )
        raise TypeError(
            f"{caller}: inputs must be an ordered sequence (list or tuple), got"
            f" {type(container).__name__}; {why}"
        )
    config = {str(v) for v in variables.scalars + variables.vectors + variables.matrices}
    kinematic = _kinematic_names(variables)
    states = _input_state_symbols(variables)
    seen = set()
    for u in inputs:
        if isinstance(u, (TS2, TSO3)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' is a tangent or variation vector of a configuration"
                " variable; its variation is part of the perturbation state, not an input"
            )
        if u.is_constant or u.is_numeric or u.is_zero:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' is constant: its variation vanishes,"
                " so it cannot be an input"
            )
        name = str(u)
        if name in config:
            raise ValueError(f"{caller}: input '{u}' is also a configuration variable")
        if str(u.delta()) in states:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{caller}: the variation '{u.delta()}' of input '{u}' is already a"
                f" perturbation state (is '{u}' a tangent vector of a configuration"
                " variable?)"
            )
        if name in kinematic:
            kind, var = kinematic[name]
            raise ValueError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' prints like the {kind} '{name}' of the configuration"
                f" variable '{var}'; leaves are matched by printed name, so the two would be"
                " confused (rename the input)"
            )
        if name in seen:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' is listed more than once (an entry that prints like"
                f" '{u}' is the same symbol)"
            )
        seen.add(name)
    # an input clashes with a node printed like it; its rate d/dt(u) is the longest
    # name looked up, so nodes printed longer than every rate are not printed at all
    rates = [str(TimeDerivative(u)) for u in inputs]
    nodes = _printed_nodes(exprs, max((len(r) for r in rates), default=0))
    _clash_against(inputs, nodes, caller, "input", "an input", "the equations")
    for u, rate in zip(inputs, rates):
        if any(isinstance(n, TimeDerivative) for n in nodes.get(rate, ())):
            raise AlgebraicError(
                f"{caller}: input '{u}' occurs in the equations inside the calculus operator"
                f" '{rate}'; an input enters the equations as itself, not through its rate"
                f" (is '{u}' a prescribed parameter of compute_eom(..., params=[...])? It can"
                " be an input only if its rate does not occur)"
            )
    return inputs

docs.title: check_symbol_clash(symbols, exprs, caller, role='input', what='an input', where='the equations')
docs.text:
Reject a declared symbol printed like a different node of exprs.

symbols are the inputs of to_standard_form/linearize or the params of compute_eom; exprs the equations (or the Lagrangian and the virtual work). The engine identifies a leaf by its printed name, so a declared Scalar("g") would be matched against, or silently miss, a constant Scalar("g", attr=['Constant']) in the equations. A declared symbol whose printed name equals that of a leaf of another class, other flags (Constant, UnitNorm, ...) or another size, or that of an operation node (a Vector named \frac{d}{dt}(x) against the node d/dt(x)), raises ValueError naming both; the same symbol (the normal case) passes. The hint names what to change: attr=['Constant'] or value= against a constant, the sizes when they are all that differs. role, what and where word the message (params entry, a prescribed parameter, the Lagrangian or the virtual work).

def check_symbol_clash(
    symbols: Sequence[Expr],
    exprs: Sequence[object],
    caller: str,
    role: str = "input",
    what: str = "an input",
    where: str = "the equations",
) -> None:
    """Reject a declared symbol printed like a *different* node of *exprs*.

    *symbols* are the inputs of ``to_standard_form``/``linearize`` or the ``params`` of
    ``compute_eom``; *exprs* the equations (or the Lagrangian and the virtual work). The
    engine identifies a leaf by its printed name, so a declared ``Scalar("g")`` would be
    matched against, or silently miss, a constant ``Scalar("g", attr=['Constant'])`` in
    the equations. A declared symbol whose printed name equals that of a leaf of another
    class, other flags (``Constant``, ``UnitNorm``, ...) or another size, or that of an
    operation node (a ``Vector`` named ``\\frac{d}{dt}(x)`` against the node ``d/dt(x)``),
    raises ``ValueError`` naming both; the same symbol (the normal case) passes. The hint
    names what to change: ``attr=['Constant']`` or ``value=`` against a constant, the
    sizes when they are all that differs. *role*, *what* and *where* word the message
    (``params entry``, ``a prescribed parameter``, ``the Lagrangian or the virtual work``).
    """
    symbols = list(symbols)
    max_len = max((len(str(sym)) for sym in symbols), default=0)
    _clash_against(symbols, _printed_nodes(exprs, max_len), caller, role, what, where)

docs.title: check_variables(variables, caller='compute_eom')
docs.text:
Every configuration variable must be a distinct symbol with a non-vanishing δq.

Rejected, naming the entry: a group that is not a list (vectors=x, TypeError); a variable of the wrong type (a Vector in scalars), a tangent or variation vector (ω, ξ, Ω, η) or a TimeDerivative/Variation node listed as a configuration variable (TypeError); a Constant/numeric leaf, whose δq = 0 would yield an empty equation (ValueError); a plain Matrix in matrices, since only SO3 is supported (TypeError); and the same printed name listed twice, across groups or as a Scalar and a Vector, or an entry printed like another entry's variation or tangent vector, which would silently merge two symbols into one (ValueError). Messages start with caller (compute_eom/linearize).

def check_variables(variables: SystemVariables, caller: str = "compute_eom") -> None:
    """Every configuration variable must be a distinct symbol with a non-vanishing δq.

    Rejected, naming the entry: a group that is not a list (``vectors=x``,
    ``TypeError``); a variable of the wrong type (a Vector in ``scalars``), a tangent or
    variation vector (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``) or a ``TimeDerivative``/``Variation``
    node listed as a configuration variable (``TypeError``); a Constant/numeric leaf,
    whose δq = 0 would yield an empty equation (``ValueError``); a plain ``Matrix`` in
    ``matrices``, since only SO3 is supported (``TypeError``); and the same printed name
    listed twice, across groups or as a Scalar and a Vector, or an entry printed like
    another entry's variation or tangent vector, which would silently merge two symbols
    into one (``ValueError``). Messages start with *caller* (``compute_eom``/``linearize``).
    """
    groups = (
        ("scalars", variables.scalars, ExprType.SCALAR),
        ("vectors", variables.vectors, ExprType.VECTOR),
        ("matrices", variables.matrices, ExprType.MATRIX),
    )
    for group_name, group, _ in groups:
        try:
            check_group_is_sequence(group_name, group)
        except TypeError as e:
            raise TypeError(f"{caller}: {e}") from None
    tangent_names = _tangent_names(variables)  # printed ω_q/Ω_R → printed point
    seen_names: dict[str, str] = {}  # printed name → group it was listed in
    seen_variations: dict[str, str] = {}  # printed variation vector → printed variable
    for group_name, group, expected_type in groups:
        for var in group:
            where = f"{caller}: SystemVariables.{group_name} entry"
            if getattr(var, "type", None) != expected_type:
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' has type {getattr(var, 'type', None)}, expected"
                    f" {expected_type}"
                )
            if isinstance(var, (TS2, TSO3)):
                parent = var.S2 if isinstance(var, TS2) else var.SO3
                hint = f"; list the manifold point '{parent}' instead" if parent else ""
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' is a tangent or variation vector, not a configuration"
                    f" variable{hint}"
                )
            if isinstance(var, (TimeDerivative, Variation)):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' is a {type(var).__name__} node, not a configuration"
                    f" variable; list the underlying variable '{var.expr}' instead"
                )
            if getattr(var, "nodes", None):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' is a {type(var).__name__} expression, not a single"
                    " symbol; a configuration variable is one Scalar, Vector, S2 or SO3 leaf"
                    " (list the symbols it is built from instead)"
                )
            if var.is_constant or var.is_numeric or var.is_zero or var.delta().is_zero:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' is constant: its variation vanishes, so it cannot be a"
                    " configuration variable"
                )
            if group_name == "matrices" and not isinstance(var, SO3):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{where} '{var}' is a general {type(var).__name__}; only SO3 rotation"
                    " matrices are supported as matrix configuration variables"
                )
            name = str(var)
            variation = str(
                var.delta() if expected_type == ExprType.SCALAR else var.get_variation_vector()
            )
            if name in seen_names:
                groups_text = (
                    f"twice in SystemVariables.{group_name}"
                    if seen_names[name] == group_name
                    else f"in SystemVariables.{seen_names[name]} and {group_name}"
                )
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{caller}: SystemVariables: the name '{name}' is listed more than once"
                    f" ({groups_text}); configuration variables must be distinct symbols"
                )
            if name in tangent_names:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{where} '{name}' has the printed name of the tangent vector of"
                    f" '{tangent_names[name]}'; configuration variables must be distinct"
                    " symbols (rename it)"
                )
            if name in seen_variations:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{where} '{name}' has the printed name of the variation vector of"
                    f" '{seen_variations[name]}'; configuration variables must be distinct"
                    " symbols"
                )
            if variation in seen_names:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{where} '{name}' has the variation vector '{variation}', which is also"
                    f" the name of the entry listed in {seen_names[variation]};"
                    " configuration variables must be distinct symbols"
                )
            if variation in seen_variations:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{caller}: SystemVariables: entries '{seen_variations[variation]}' and"
                    f" '{name}' share the variation vector '{variation}'; configuration"
                    " variables must be distinct symbols"
                )
            seen_names[name] = group_name
            seen_variations[variation] = name

docs.title: compute_eom(lagrangian, inf_work, variables, params=(), *, trace=None)
docs.text:
Compute equations of motion using the principle of least action.

Stages, in the order the code runs them (docs/pipeline.md has one paragraph per stage; the bracketed names are the EOMTrace stage names):

  1. [dL] the variation of the Lagrangian, [dW] the virtual work, and [dS] the infinitesimal action integral δS = δL + δW
  2. [manifold_rules] apply_manifold_rules: δω and δΩ replaced by their kinematic expansions (S², SO(3))
  3. [simplify] full_simplify (expand once, then simplify to a fixed point)
  4. integration by parts against the time derivative of each variation vector: [ibp.prepare] expand + full_simplify, then per target [ibp.collect[t]] (rotate each term so the target is the left operand of a Dot), [ibp.integrate[t]] (one IBP pass) and [ibp.simplify[t]]; [ibp] is the result
  5. [expand]
  6. per variation vector: extract_linear_coeff [raw[ξ]], then full_simplify [equation[ξ]]

trace (keyword only) is an EOMTrace: it is filled with every stage as the pipeline runs, so after an exception it holds the stages before the failure and trace.failed_at names the stage that raised (trace.summary(), trace.show("simplify")). The trace is cleared first, so a reused trace holds this run only. Without a trace, and with the geomech logger not at DEBUG, nothing is recorded. With GEOMECH_DEBUG=1 each stage is logged and check_tree runs on the inputs and the equations.

An extraction failure is re-raised with the same exception type and the pipeline context: the variation vector, and when a time derivative of a variation vector survived integration by parts, the term it survived in.

inf_work may be None or 0 for a conservative system. It must be linear in the variation vectors themselves: a time derivative of a listed variation vector in inf_work (Dot(x.t_diff().delta(), f), Dot(ξ.t_diff(), f)) raises ValueError. variables must list at least one configuration variable (ValueError "no configuration variables" otherwise; this check runs last, so a Lagrangian that holds a symbol first fails the stray-variation check below); params must be a sequence of leaves (TypeError).

Every symbol in lagrangian and inf_work is one of three things: a configuration variable (listed in variables, varied by Hamilton's principle), a constant (attr=["Constant"]), or a prescribed time-varying parameter declared in params (a plain non-constant Scalar/Vector/Matrix leaf such as a cable length l(t): its rate l̇ appears in the equations, its variation δl is not free and is dropped). A variation symbol that survives extraction and belongs to none of these (δx of an unlisted x, ξ/δω of an unlisted S2 point, …) raises ValueError naming it: before, such terms were dropped silently and the system lost a degree of freedom. numeric.check_eom takes the same params. A param printed like a different leaf of lagrangian or inf_work (a constant l of L declared as Scalar("l")) raises ValueError: it would have no effect. to_standard_form accepts the result (a param's rate stays in f, the param itself in M); linearize does not support prescribed parameters yet and raises AlgebraicError on the δl term.

def compute_eom(
    lagrangian: Expr,
    inf_work: Expr | int | float | None,
    variables: SystemVariables,
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    *,
    trace: EOMTrace | None = None,
) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """Compute equations of motion using the principle of least action.

    Stages, in the order the code runs them (``docs/pipeline.md`` has one paragraph per
    stage; the bracketed names are the ``EOMTrace`` stage names):

    1. ``[dL]`` the variation of the Lagrangian, ``[dW]`` the virtual work, and
       ``[dS]`` the infinitesimal action integral δS = δL + δW
    2. ``[manifold_rules]`` ``apply_manifold_rules``: δω and δΩ replaced by their
       kinematic expansions (S², SO(3))
    3. ``[simplify]`` ``full_simplify`` (expand once, then simplify to a fixed point)
    4. integration by parts against the time derivative of each variation vector:
       ``[ibp.prepare]`` expand + full_simplify, then per target ``[ibp.collect[t]]``
       (rotate each term so the target is the left operand of a ``Dot``),
       ``[ibp.integrate[t]]`` (one IBP pass) and ``[ibp.simplify[t]]``; ``[ibp]`` is
       the result
    5. ``[expand]``
    6. per variation vector: ``extract_linear_coeff`` ``[raw[ξ]]``, then
       ``full_simplify`` ``[equation[ξ]]``

    ``trace`` (keyword only) is an ``EOMTrace``: it is filled with every stage as the
    pipeline runs, so after an exception it holds the stages before the failure and
    ``trace.failed_at`` names the stage that raised (``trace.summary()``,
    ``trace.show("simplify")``). The trace is cleared first, so a reused trace holds
    this run only. Without a trace, and with the
    ``geomech`` logger not at ``DEBUG``, nothing is recorded. With ``GEOMECH_DEBUG=1``
    each stage is logged and ``check_tree`` runs on the inputs and the equations.

    An extraction failure is re-raised with the same exception type and the pipeline
    context: the variation vector, and when a time derivative of a variation vector
    survived integration by parts, the term it survived in.

    ``inf_work`` may be ``None`` or ``0`` for a conservative system. It must be linear in
    the variation vectors themselves: a time derivative of a listed variation vector in
    ``inf_work`` (``Dot(x.t_diff().delta(), f)``, ``Dot(ξ.t_diff(), f)``) raises
    ``ValueError``. ``variables`` must list at least one configuration variable
    (``ValueError`` "no configuration variables" otherwise; this check runs last, so a
    Lagrangian that holds a symbol first fails the stray-variation check below);
    ``params`` must be a sequence of leaves (``TypeError``).

    Every symbol in ``lagrangian`` and ``inf_work`` is one of three things: a
    configuration variable (listed in ``variables``, varied by Hamilton's principle), a
    constant (``attr=["Constant"]``), or a prescribed time-varying parameter declared in
    ``params`` (a plain non-constant ``Scalar``/``Vector``/``Matrix`` leaf such as a cable
    length ``l(t)``: its rate ``l̇`` appears in the equations, its variation ``δl`` is not
    free and is dropped). A variation symbol that survives extraction and belongs to none
    of these (``δx`` of an unlisted ``x``, ``ξ``/``δω`` of an unlisted ``S2`` point, …)
    raises ``ValueError`` naming it: before, such terms were dropped silently and the
    system lost a degree of freedom. ``numeric.check_eom`` takes the same ``params``. A
    param printed like a different leaf of ``lagrangian`` or ``inf_work`` (a constant
    ``l`` of ``L`` declared as ``Scalar("l")``) raises ``ValueError``: it would have no
    effect.
    ``to_standard_form`` accepts the result (a param's rate stays in ``f``, the param
    itself in ``M``); ``linearize`` does not support prescribed parameters yet and raises
    ``AlgebraicError`` on the ``δl`` term.
    """
    if trace is not None:
        trace._reset()
    stage = "validation"
    try:
        check_variables(variables)
        if not isinstance(params, (Expr, str)) and hasattr(params, "__iter__"):
            params = list(params)  # a generator is read twice (here and the clash check)
        param_names = _check_params(params, variables)
        if isinstance(inf_work, bool):
            raise TypeError(
                "compute_eom: inf_work must be a scalar expression, None or 0, got bool"
                f" {inf_work}"
            )
        if inf_work is None or (isinstance(inf_work, (int, float)) and inf_work == 0):
            inf_work = Zero
        _check_scalar_input("lagrangian", lagrangian)
        _check_scalar_input("inf_work", inf_work)
        check_symbol_clash(
            params,
            [lagrangian, inf_work],
            "compute_eom",
            role="params entry",
            what="a prescribed parameter",
            where="the Lagrangian or the virtual work",
        )

        # gather variation vectors and their time derivatives
        variation_vectors = []
        variation_vector_dots = []

        for s in variables.scalars:
            ds = s.delta()  # Variation(scalar) — scalar type
            variation_vectors.append(ds)
            variation_vector_dots.append(ds.t_diff())

        for vec in variables.vectors:
            x = vec.get_variation_vector()
            variation_vectors.append(x)
            variation_vector_dots.append(x.t_diff())

        for mat in variables.matrices:
            x = mat.get_variation_vector()
            variation_vectors.append(x)
            variation_vector_dots.append(x.t_diff())

        allowed = {str(v) for v in variation_vectors}
        _check_virtual_work(inf_work, variables, allowed)

        debug = debug_enabled()
        if debug:
            check_tree(lagrangian)
            check_tree(inf_work)
        record = stage_recorder(trace, "compute_eom")
        if trace is not None:
            trace.variation_vectors = list(variation_vectors)
            trace.ibp_targets = list(variation_vector_dots)

        # variation of the Lagrangian
        stage = "dL"
        dL = lagrangian.delta()

        # infinitesimal action integral
        dS = dL + inf_work
        if record is not None:
            record("dL", dL)
            record("dW", inf_work)
            record("dS", dS)

        # apply manifold kinematic substitutions
        stage = "manifold_rules"
        dS = apply_manifold_rules(dS, variables)
        if record is not None:
            record("manifold_rules", dS)

        stage = "simplify"
        dS = full_simplify(dS)
        if record is not None:
            record("simplify", dS)

        # integration by parts
        stage = "ibp"
        try:
            dS = _integrate_by_parts(dS, variation_vector_dots, record)
        except (AlgebraicError, NonLinearError) as err:
            raise type(err)(
                f"compute_eom: while integrating by parts (stage ibp, targets"
                f" {', '.join(f'{t}' for t in variation_vector_dots)}): {err}"
            ) from err
        if record is not None:
            record("ibp", dS)

        # expand
        stage = "expand"
        dS = expand(dS)
        if record is not None:
            record("expand", dS)

        # extract equations of motion
        stage = "extract"
        try:
            eom = _separate_variations(dS, variation_vectors, record)
        except _ExtractionFailure as failure:
            # retold with L when it depends on accelerations; otherwise the δS message
            raise failure.retold(dS, variation_vectors, lagrangian, variables) from (
                failure.engine
            )
        if debug:
            for _, eq in eom.values():
                check_tree(eq)

        stage = "stray_check"
        # a variation symbol that survives extraction belongs to no listed variable or param
        wrapped: dict[str, str] = {}  # δ(d/dt(x)) built by hand → x
        stray = _stray_variation_symbols(dS, allowed, param_names, wrapped)
        for _, eq in eom.values():
            stray.update(_stray_variation_symbols(eq, allowed, param_names, wrapped))
        if stray:
            symbols = ", ".join(f"'{s}'" for s in sorted(stray))
            names = ", ".join(f"'{n}'" for n in sorted(set(stray.values())))
            message = (
                f"compute_eom: δS still contains the variation symbols {symbols} of the symbols"
                f" {names}, which are neither entries of SystemVariables nor declared in params"
            )
            if any(sym not in wrapped for sym in stray):
                message += (
                    "; for each symbol, list it in SystemVariables, declare it in params=..., or"
                    " mark it 'Constant'"
                )
            for sym, leaf in sorted(wrapped.items()):
                message += (
                    f"; '{sym}' is the variation of a time derivative, which the engine never"
                    f" builds: write the variation of the configuration variable itself,"
                    f" {leaf}.delta() (the variation of the velocity is {leaf}.t_diff().delta(),"
                    " built as d/dt of the variation, and is not allowed in inf_work)"
                )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if not variation_vectors:
            raise ValueError(
                "compute_eom: no configuration variables listed in SystemVariables; a system"
                " with no degree of freedom has no equation of motion"
            )
        return eom
    except Exception as err:
        if trace is not None:
            trace._fail(_failed_stage(trace, stage, err), err)
        raise

def separate_variations(
    inf_action_integral: Expr, variation_vectors: Sequence[Expr]
) -> dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]]:
    """Extract the equation of motion for each variation vector.

    Returns a dict mapping str(variation_vector) → (variation_vector, equation). An
    ``AlgebraicError``/``NonLinearError`` from the extraction is re-raised (same type)
    naming the variation vector and, if a time derivative of a variation vector is left
    in δS, the term that holds it.
    """
    try:
        return _separate_variations(inf_action_integral, variation_vectors)
    except _ExtractionFailure as failure:
        raise failure.retold(inf_action_integral, variation_vectors) from failure.engine
