docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: eom_dict : dict Output of compute_eom(): {str(variation_vec): (variation_vec, eom_expr)}. variables : SystemVariables Configuration variables (used to derive acceleration variables). inputs : list[Scalar | Vector], optional Input variables (forces, torques). Default (None): no inputs. Validated by check_inputs, exactly as in linearize: a TypeError for an entry that is not a plain Scalar/Vector leaf, one leaf instead of a sequence, or a set/dict (the order of inputs is the order of the input columns), a ValueError for a constant or duplicate input, a configuration variable, a tangent or variation vector (ω, ξ, Ω, η), or an input printed like a velocity or acceleration, or like a different node of the equations (a constant g of L given as Scalar("g"), another class, attr or size, or an operation node such as d/dt(l)), since leaves are matched by printed name; an AlgebraicError for an input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of compute_eom). A non-dict eom_dict raises TypeError.

docs.text: dict[str, StandardFormEquation] Keyed by the same variation vector names as eom_dict.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
On S² the equation E = 0 of a variable q is only meaningful on the tangent plane, (I − qqᵀ) E = 0: E is the coefficient of ξ ⊥ q and in general has a component along q (from the forcing, from ω × c, from A ω̇, …). The blocks returned here are the terms of E as derived, not projected. To solve for ω̇ solve (I − qqᵀ)(M ω̇ + f + Σ G u) = 0 with ω̇ ⊥ q; the unprojected 3×3 solve gives q · ω̇ ≠ 0 and a trajectory that leaves the sphere. The same holds for the rows of linearize.

Errors name the equation and the term: a term that holds an acceleration only under a further time derivative (a jerk d/dt(ẍ)) raises AlgebraicError saying the equation is not second order; a term bilinear in two accelerations raises NonLinearError. With GEOMECH_DEBUG=1 the blocks of each equation are logged on the geomech logger and check_tree runs on every equation and block.

def to_standard_form(
    eom_dict: dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]],
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, StandardFormEquation]:
    """Decompose EOM into standard manipulator form.

    Parameters
    ----------
    eom_dict : dict
        Output of ``compute_eom()``:
        ``{str(variation_vec): (variation_vec, eom_expr)}``.
    variables : SystemVariables
        Configuration variables (used to derive acceleration variables).
    inputs : list[Scalar | Vector], optional
        Input variables (forces, torques). Default (``None``): no inputs. Validated by
        ``check_inputs``, exactly as in ``linearize``: a ``TypeError`` for an entry that
        is not a plain ``Scalar``/``Vector`` leaf, one leaf instead of a sequence, or a
        ``set``/``dict`` (the order of *inputs* is the order of the input columns), a
        ``ValueError`` for a constant or duplicate input, a configuration variable, a
        tangent or variation vector (``ω``, ``ξ``, ``Ω``, ``η``), or an input printed like
        a velocity or acceleration, or like a different node of the equations (a constant
        ``g`` of ``L`` given as ``Scalar("g")``, another class, ``attr`` or size, or an
        operation node such as ``d/dt(l)``), since leaves are matched by printed name; an
        ``AlgebraicError`` for an input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of
        ``compute_eom``). A non-dict *eom_dict* raises ``TypeError``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, StandardFormEquation]
        Keyed by the same variation vector names as *eom_dict*.

    Notes
    -----
    On S² the equation ``E = 0`` of a variable ``q`` is only meaningful on the tangent
    plane, ``(I − qqᵀ) E = 0``: ``E`` is the coefficient of ``ξ ⊥ q`` and in general has
    a component along ``q`` (from the forcing, from ``ω × c``, from ``A ω̇``, …). The
    blocks returned here are the terms of ``E`` as derived, not projected. To solve for
    ``ω̇`` solve ``(I − qqᵀ)(M ω̇ + f + Σ G u) = 0`` with ``ω̇ ⊥ q``; the unprojected
    3×3 solve gives ``q · ω̇ ≠ 0`` and a trajectory that leaves the sphere. The same
    holds for the rows of ``linearize``.

    Errors name the equation and the term: a term that holds an acceleration only under
    a further time derivative (a jerk ``d/dt(ẍ)``) raises ``AlgebraicError`` saying the
    equation is not second order; a term bilinear in two accelerations raises
    ``NonLinearError``. With ``GEOMECH_DEBUG=1`` the blocks of each equation are logged
    on the ``geomech`` logger and ``check_tree`` runs on every equation and block.
    """
    if not isinstance(eom_dict, dict):
        raise TypeError(
            f"to_standard_form: eom must be the dict returned by compute_eom, got {type(eom_dict)}"
        )
    inputs = check_inputs(
        inputs, variables, [eq for _, eq in eom_dict.values()], "to_standard_form"
    )

    accel_vars = _get_accel_vars(variables)
    debug = debug_enabled()
    record = stage_recorder(None, "to_standard_form")

    result = {}
    for key, (var_vec, eom_expr) in eom_dict.items():
        if debug:
            check_tree(eom_expr)
        sf = _extract_single(eom_expr, accel_vars, inputs, key)
        if record is not None:
            for name, block in sf.M.items():
                record(f"M[{key}][{name}]", block)
            record(f"f[{key}]", sf.f)
            for name, block in sf.G.items():
                record(f"G[{key}][{name}]", block)
        if debug:
            for block in (*sf.M.values(), sf.f, *sf.G.values()):
                check_tree(block)
        result[key] = sf

    return result

def check_group_is_sequence(group_name: str, group: object) -> None:
    """A ``SystemVariables`` group must be a list (or tuple) of variables, not one leaf.

    A bare leaf (``vectors=x``) or a one-shot iterator would otherwise fail with Python's
    own ``'Vector' object is not iterable`` or be consumed by the first pass over it.
    """
    if not isinstance(group, (list, tuple)):
        hint = f"; write {group_name}=[{group}]" if hasattr(group, "type") else ""
        raise TypeError(
            f"SystemVariables.{group_name} must be a list of configuration variables, got"
            f" {type(group).__name__} {str(group)!r}{hint}"
        )

docs.title: vbl
docs.text:
Variation-based linearization (VBL) of the equations of motion.

linearize(eom, variables, inputs) takes the equations returned by compute_eom and produces their linearization along an arbitrary trajectory in the first-order form

M δẋ = A δx + B δu

where the perturbation state δx is built from manifold-respecting perturbation variables rather than local coordinates (Wu & Sreenath 2015; Lee et al. Appendix B). The blocks M, A, B are symbolic functions of the trajectory (q, v, v̇, u).

docs.title: Perturbation variables
docs.text:
Each configuration variable contributes one configuration perturbation and one velocity perturbation. Velocity perturbations are the Variation of the velocity symbol and are not substituted by the EOM manifold rules (apply_manifold_rules is never called here):

configuration      config. perturbation          velocity perturbation
s : Scalar (R)     δs  = Variation(s)            δṡ = TimeDerivative(Variation(s))
x : Vector (R³)    δx  = Variation(x)            δẋ = TimeDerivative(Variation(x))
q : S2             ξ   = q.get_variation_vector  δω = Variation(ω),  ω = q.get_tangent_vector()
R : SO3            η   = R.get_variation_vector  δΩ = Variation(Ω),  Ω = R.get_tangent_vector()

δ(constant) = 0, δq = ξ × q and δR = R·Hat(η) are produced eagerly by the leaf types, and δ(v̇) is canonicalised to TimeDerivative(Variation(v)).

docs.title: Kinematic rows (one per configuration variable)
docs.text:
• R and R³: d/dt(δs) = δṡ and d/dt(δx) = δẋ (identities between the same symbols, included so that the block structure is uniform).

  • S² with q̇ = ω × q, ω ⊥ q, δq = ξ × q, ξ ⊥ q: equating δ(q̇) with d/dt(δq) and using the tangency constraint d/dt(ξ·q) = 0 gives

    ξ̇ = q qᵀ Hat(ω) ξ + (I − q qᵀ) δω

so M[ξ̇] = I, A[ξ] = q qᵀ Hat(ω), A[δω] = I − q qᵀ. - SO(3) with Ṙ = R·Hat(Ω), δR = R·Hat(η): δΩ = η̇ + Ω × η rearranged,

  η̇ = −Hat(Ω) η + δΩ

so M[η̇] = I, A[η] = −Hat(Ω), A[δΩ] = I.

docs.title: Dynamic rows (one per equation of compute_eom) and sign convention
docs.text:
compute_eom returns, for each variation vector, an expression E(q, v, v̇, u) with E = 0. E is the coefficient of the variation in the post-IBP integrand, i.e. the negative of the Euler–Lagrange expression, which is why to_standard_form reports M = −(physical inertia). VBL takes the first variation δE, which is linear in the perturbation variables, and defines the blocks so that the physical inertia comes out positive:

δE = −M δv̇ + A δx + B δu

M[row][δv̇_j] = −coeff(δv̇_j, δE)
A[row][δx_j] =  coeff(δx_j, δE)      (δx_j over configuration and velocity perturbations)
B[row][δu_j] =  coeff(δu_j, δE)

Free rigid body (Lee et al. Eq. 6.16): E = −JΩ̇ − Ω × JΩ + M_in gives δE = −J δΩ̇ + (Hat(JΩ) − Hat(Ω) J) δΩ + δM, so M = J, A[δΩ] = Hat(JΩ) − Hat(Ω) J and B = I.

docs.title: Completeness rule
docs.text: After extraction every additive term of expand(δE) must contain exactly one perturbation symbol (configuration, velocity, d/dt of velocity, or input variation). A term with none, or with a perturbation symbol only inside a non-canonical calculus node, means the linearization is incomplete and linearize raises AlgebraicError naming the term. Nothing is silently dropped or set to zero.

docs.title: LinearizedSystem(rows=list(), states=list(), dstates=list(), inputs=list(), M=dict(), A=dict(), B=dict(), row_types=dict(), col_types=dict()) dataclass

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: rows : list[str] Ordered row labels: kinematic rows first ("kin:" + str(var), one per configuration variable in SystemVariables order), then the dynamic rows labelled by the compute_eom keys. states : list[Expr] Perturbation symbols of δx: configuration perturbations in SystemVariables order, then velocity perturbations in the same order. dstates : list[Expr] [s.t_diff() for s in states]. inputs : list[Expr] [u.delta() for u in inputs]. M, A, B : dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] M[row][str(dstate)], A[row][str(state)], B[row][str(input_variation)]. Dense: every (row, column) pair is present. Block shapes follow row type × column type (vector × vector → 3×3 Matrix, scalar × vector → 1×3 Transpose(Vector), vector × scalar → 3×1 Vector, scalar × scalar → Scalar); zero blocks are the library zero constants of that shape. row_types, col_types : dict[str, ExprType] Expression type of each row and of each column symbol (used by block_shape).

def block_shape(self, row, col) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Shape of the block at (*row*, *col*); *col* may be a symbol or its ``str``."""
    row_key = row if isinstance(row, str) else str(row)
    col_key = col if isinstance(col, str) else str(col)
    if row_key not in self.row_types:
        raise KeyError(f"LinearizedSystem: unknown row '{row_key}'")
    if col_key not in self.col_types:
        raise KeyError(f"LinearizedSystem: unknown column '{col_key}'")
    n_rows = 1 if self.row_types[row_key] == ExprType.SCALAR else 3
    n_cols = 1 if self.col_types[col_key] == ExprType.SCALAR else 3
    return (n_rows, n_cols)

Their variations form δu. params : list, optional The prescribed parameters passed to compute_eom(..., params=...). ValueError Constant or duplicate inputs (the input checks are check_inputs, shared with to_standard_form), an input that is also a configuration variable or a tangent vector (Ω, ω) whose variation is already a state, an input printed like a velocity, an acceleration or a different node of the equations (a constant g of L given as Scalar("g"), another class, attr or size, or an operation node such as d/dt(l)), or eom keys that do not match variables. A stray variation symbol in an equation also surfaces as the engine's ValueError (δ of a variation is not representable). AlgebraicError An input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of compute_eom given as an input, check_inputs). A term of δE carries no perturbation symbol, more than one (a nonlinear or incompletely distributed term), or one only inside a non-canonical calculus node, or a coefficient could not be factored.

def linearize(
    eom: dict[str, tuple[Expr, Expr]],
    variables: SystemVariables,
    inputs: Sequence[Expr] | None = None,
    params: Sequence[Expr] = (),
    *,
    trace: LinearizationTrace | None = None,
) -> LinearizedSystem:
    """Linearize the equations of motion along an arbitrary trajectory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    eom : dict
        Output of ``compute_eom``: ``{str(variation_vec): (variation_vec, eom_expr)}``.
    variables : SystemVariables
        The configuration variables used for ``compute_eom``.
    inputs : list[Scalar | Vector], optional
        Input symbols (forces, torques, thrust). Their variations form δu.
    params : list, optional
        The prescribed parameters passed to ``compute_eom(..., params=...)``. Prescribed
        parameters are not supported by ``linearize`` yet: a term carrying the variation
        of a declared param raises ``AlgebraicError`` saying so (without ``params`` the
        message cannot tell a param from a missing input or a missing ``Constant``).
    trace : LinearizationTrace, optional
        Keyword only. Filled per dynamic row with δE, the partition buckets, the raw
        coefficients (before ``full_simplify`` and before the mass blocks are negated)
        and the final blocks; see ``LinearizationTrace``. Cleared when the call
        starts; after an exception ``trace.failed_at`` names the stage that raised.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearizedSystem
        Blocks of ``M δẋ = A δx + B δu`` (see the module docstring for the sign
        convention and the kinematic rows).

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        Invalid ``variables`` or ``inputs`` (not plain ``Scalar``/``Vector`` leaves, or a
        ``set``/``dict``, whose order would be that of the columns of ``B``),
        a non-``SO3`` matrix configuration, or an equation whose type differs from
        that of its variation vector (a scalar equation under a vector key).
    ValueError
        Constant or duplicate inputs (the input checks are ``check_inputs``, shared with
        ``to_standard_form``), an input that is also a configuration variable
        or a tangent vector (``Ω``, ``ω``) whose variation is already a state, an input
        printed like a velocity, an acceleration or a different node of the equations
        (a constant ``g`` of ``L`` given as ``Scalar("g")``, another class, ``attr`` or
        size, or an operation node such as ``d/dt(l)``), or
        ``eom`` keys that do not match ``variables``. A stray variation symbol in an
        equation also surfaces as the engine's ``ValueError`` (δ of a variation is
        not representable).
    AlgebraicError
        An input whose rate occurs in the equations (a param of ``compute_eom`` given as
        an input, ``check_inputs``). A term of δE carries no perturbation symbol, more
        than one (a nonlinear or incompletely distributed term), or one only inside a
        non-canonical calculus node, or a coefficient could not be factored.
    """
    if trace is not None:
        trace._reset()
    stage = "validation"
    try:
        check_variables(variables, caller="linearize")
        cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts = perturbation_variables(variables)
        _check_eom(eom, variables)
        param_names = _param_names(params)
        debug = debug_enabled()
        if debug:
            for _, eq in eom.values():
                check_tree(eq)
        record = stage_recorder(trace, "linearize")
        states = cfg_perts + vel_perts
        dstates = [s.t_diff() for s in states]
        inputs = check_inputs(inputs, variables, [eq for _, eq in eom.values()], "linearize")
        input_perts = [u.delta() for u in inputs]
        dvel_perts = dstates[len(cfg_perts) :]

        col_types = {}
        for sym in states + dstates + input_perts:
            col_types[str(sym)] = sym.type

        rows: list[str] = []
        row_types: dict[str, ExprType] = {}
        M: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        A: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        B: dict[str, dict[str, Expr]] = {}
        blocks = _Blocks(rows, row_types, M, A, B, dstates, states, input_perts)

        for i, var in enumerate(cfg_vars):
            _kinematic_row(blocks, var, cfg_perts[i], vel_perts[i], dstates[i])

        # Priority order for assigning a term to its perturbation symbol: the most
        # deeply wrapped symbols first, so that a term in d/dt(δv) is never tested
        # for δv (which would raise inside has_algebraic).
        priority = dvel_perts + vel_perts + cfg_perts + input_perts
        all_perts = priority + [d for d in dstates[: len(cfg_perts)]]
        n_mass = len(dvel_perts)
        n_state = n_mass + len(vel_perts) + len(cfg_perts)

        for label, (var_vec, eq) in eom.items():
            stage = f"row[{label}]"
            _dynamic_row(
                blocks,
                label,
                var_vec,
                eq,
                priority,
                all_perts,
                n_mass,
                n_state,
                param_names,
                record,
                debug,
            )

        return LinearizedSystem(
            rows=rows,
            states=states,
            dstates=dstates,
            inputs=input_perts,
            M=M,
            A=A,
            B=B,
            row_types=row_types,
            col_types=col_types,
        )
    except Exception as err:
        if trace is not None:
            trace._fail(_failed_row_stage(trace, stage), err)
        raise

docs.title: partition_terms(dE, priority, label, param_names=frozenset())
docs.text:
Assign every additive term of dE to exactly one perturbation symbol.

Returns one list of terms per entry of priority (same order). A term that carries no perturbation symbol, one only inside a calculus operator, or more than one distinct symbol raises AlgebraicError: the first two mean the linearization is incomplete, the last that the term is nonlinear or was not fully distributed by expand and would be extracted wrongly.

Source code in geomech/dynamics/vbl.py 
def partition_terms(dE, priority, label, param_names=frozenset()):
    """Assign every additive term of *dE* to exactly one perturbation symbol.

    Returns one list of terms per entry of *priority* (same order). A term that
    carries no perturbation symbol, one only inside a calculus operator, or more
    than one distinct symbol raises ``AlgebraicError``: the first two mean the
    linearization is incomplete, the last that the term is nonlinear or was not
    fully distributed by ``expand`` and would be extracted wrongly.
    """
    buckets = [[] for _ in priority]
    for term in addends(dE):
        if _is_zero_block(term):
            continue
        owner = None
        for index, sym in enumerate(priority):
            try:
                found = has_algebraic(term, sym)
            except AlgebraicError as err:
                raise AlgebraicError(
                    f"linearize: in row '{label}', the term '{term}' of the variation"
                    f" carries '{sym}' only inside a calculus operator; the"
                    f" linearization is incomplete ({err})"
                ) from None
            if found:
                owner = index
                break
        if owner is None:
            raise AlgebraicError(
                f"linearize: in row '{label}', the term '{term}' of the variation"
                " contains no perturbation symbol (configuration, velocity or input"
                " variation); the linearization is incomplete."
                + _no_perturbation_hint(term, param_names)
            )
        for other in priority[owner + 1 :]:
            if _occurs_outside(term, other, priority[owner]):
                raise AlgebraicError(
                    f"linearize: in row '{label}', the term '{term}' of the variation"
                    f" carries both '{priority[owner]}' and '{other}'; a term must be"
                    " linear in exactly one perturbation symbol"
                )
        buckets[owner].append(term)
    return buckets

This is the column order of LinearizedSystem.states; geomech.codegen uses it to match a layout.

def perturbation_variables(variables):
    """``(cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts)``: the configuration variables of *variables* in
    ``SystemVariables`` order (scalars, vectors, matrices) with their configuration and
    velocity perturbation symbols (see the module docstring). This is the column order of
    ``LinearizedSystem.states``; ``geomech.codegen`` uses it to match a layout."""
    cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts = [], [], []
    for s in variables.scalars:
        cfg_vars.append(s)
        cfg_perts.append(s.delta())
        vel_perts.append(s.t_diff().delta())
    for v in variables.vectors:
        cfg_vars.append(v)
        if isinstance(v, S2):
            cfg_perts.append(v.get_variation_vector())
            vel_perts.append(Variation(v.get_tangent_vector()))
        else:
            cfg_perts.append(v.delta())
            vel_perts.append(v.t_diff().delta())
    for m in variables.matrices:
        if not isinstance(m, SO3):
            raise TypeError(
                f"linearize: matrix configuration variable '{m}' must be an SO3;"
                " general matrix configurations have no perturbation vector"
            )
        cfg_vars.append(m)
        cfg_perts.append(m.get_variation_vector())
        vel_perts.append(Variation(m.get_tangent_vector()))
    return cfg_vars, cfg_perts, vel_perts

The reduced state error δx of state about x_eq (see the module docstring).

def error(self, state) -> np.ndarray:
    """The reduced state error ``δx`` of *state* about ``x_eq`` (see the module
    docstring)."""
    x = np.asarray(state, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    xe = self.x_eq
    cfg, vel = [], []
    for var in self.model.variables:
        if var.manifold == "S2":
            Bq = self.bases[var.key]
            cfg.append(Bq.T @ np.cross(xe[var.cfg], x[var.cfg]))
            vel.append(Bq.T @ (x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel]))
        elif var.manifold == "SO3":
            Re, R = xe[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3), x[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3)
            cfg.append(log_so3(Re.T @ R))
            vel.append(x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel])
        else:
            cfg.append(x[var.cfg] - xe[var.cfg])
            vel.append(x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel])
    return np.concatenate(cfg + vel)

docs.text:
The values of one state slot over time, by printed symbol ("q", "\\omega_{q}") or generated name ("omega_q"): (N,), (N, 3) or (N, 3, 3) for an SO(3) point.

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """The values of one state slot over time, by printed symbol (``"q"``,
    ``"\\\\omega_{q}"``) or generated name (``"omega_q"``): ``(N,)``, ``(N, 3)`` or
    ``(N, 3, 3)`` for an SO(3) point."""
    lay = self.module.LAYOUT
    for slot in lay["configuration"] + lay["velocity"]:
        if key in (slot["symbol"], slot["name"]):
            vals = self.state[:, slice(*slot["slice"])]
            shape = tuple(slot["shape"])
            return vals[:, 0] if shape == () else vals.reshape((len(self.t), *shape))
    names = [s["name"] for s in lay["configuration"] + lay["velocity"]]
    raise KeyError(f"Trajectory: no state slot {key!r} (slots: {names})")

def energy(self, fn: Callable | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """``fn(state, p)`` at every output state, ``(N,)``.

    *fn* defaults to the module's ``energy`` (``generate_module(...,
    lagrangian=L)``); ``geomech.codegen.energy_function(L, layout)`` gives one for any
    Lagrangian.
    """
    if fn is None:
        fn = getattr(self.module, "energy", None)
        if fn is None:
            raise TypeError(
                "Trajectory.energy: the module has no energy(); generate it with"
                " generate_module(..., lagrangian=L) or pass energy_function(L, layout)"
            )
    # The generated functions take one state at a time; at about 20 µs per state
    # (double rigid pendulum) this loop is a few percent of the simulation that
    # produced the states, so it is not vectorised.
    return np.fromiter((float(fn(x, self.p)) for x in self.state), float, len(self.state))

docs.title: accelerations(module, state, u=None, p=None)
docs.text:
The accelerations a of a generated standard-form module at (state, u).

Solves mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0. Every S² equation is meaningful only on the tangent plane of its point q (docs/conventions.md), and its acceleration ω̇ satisfies q · ω̇ = 0 (from d/dt (q · ω) = 0 with q̇ · ω = (ω × q) · ω = 0). So each S² row block is replaced by P_q · row plus a multiple of q qᵀ on its own ω̇ column, with right-hand side −P_q (bias + G u), P_q = I − q qᵀ; the couplings of that row to the other accelerations are projected too. This works whether the derived S² mass block is singular (Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²) or already full rank (−m l² I, when the engine used q · ω̇ = 0 itself).

Scaling, so that the result does not depend on the units: the stabiliser is s q qᵀ with s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2, D the row's own diagonal mass block. Both forms of D project to −m l² P_q and ‖P_q‖_F = √2, so s = m l²: the normal direction gets the same magnitude as the two tangent directions (for an anisotropic tangent inertia, the root mean square of the two). Then every row of the system and of the right-hand side is divided by its largest entry (row equilibration), and the system is solved with np.linalg.solve. The condition number is taken on the equilibrated matrix, so a light link (m₂/m₁ = 1e-9) or a large one (1 t on a 100 km tether, SI units) is solved to round-off and accepted, while a kinetic energy that is degenerate for every parameter value still raises.

Name Type Description Default module Any

a module from generate_module of a to_standard_form result.

required state ArrayLike

the flat state (LAYOUT: configuration slots, then velocity slots).

required u ArrayLike | None

the inputs (None for zeros).

None p dict | None

the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.

None

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

The flat accelerations, ordered like LAYOUT["acceleration"].

Raises:

Type Description LinAlgError

the system is singular, i.e. its condition number after row equilibration exceeds MAX_COND (1e12); the message gives the condition number and the state. Examples: a zero mass, a singular inertia, a degenerate kinetic energy.

ValueError

u has the wrong shape or non-finite entries.

def accelerations(
    module: Any, state: ArrayLike, u: ArrayLike | None = None, p: dict | None = None
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The accelerations ``a`` of a generated standard-form module at ``(state, u)``.

    Solves ``mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0``. Every S² equation is meaningful
    only on the tangent plane of its point ``q`` (``docs/conventions.md``), and its
    acceleration ``ω̇`` satisfies ``q · ω̇ = 0`` (from ``d/dt (q · ω) = 0`` with
    ``q̇ · ω = (ω × q) · ω = 0``). So each S² row block is replaced by ``P_q · row`` plus
    a multiple of ``q qᵀ`` on its own ``ω̇`` column, with right-hand side ``−P_q (bias + G u)``,
    ``P_q = I − q qᵀ``; the couplings of that row to the other accelerations are
    projected too. This works whether the derived S² mass block is singular
    (``Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²``) or already full rank (``−m l² I``, when the engine used
    ``q · ω̇ = 0`` itself).

    Scaling, so that the result does not depend on the units: the stabiliser is
    ``s q qᵀ`` with ``s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2``, ``D`` the row's own diagonal mass block.
    Both forms of ``D`` project to ``−m l² P_q`` and ``‖P_q‖_F = √2``, so ``s = m l²``:
    the normal direction gets the same magnitude as the two tangent directions (for an
    anisotropic tangent inertia, the root mean square of the two). Then every row of the
    system and of the right-hand side is divided by its largest entry (row
    equilibration), and the system is solved with ``np.linalg.solve``. The condition
    number is taken on the equilibrated matrix, so a light link (``m₂/m₁ = 1e-9``) or a
    large one (1 t on a 100 km tether, SI units) is solved to round-off and accepted,
    while a kinetic energy that is degenerate for every parameter value still raises.

    Args:
        module: a module from ``generate_module`` of a ``to_standard_form`` result.
        state: the flat state (``LAYOUT``: configuration slots, then velocity slots).
        u: the inputs (``None`` for zeros).
        p: the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.

    Returns:
        The flat accelerations, ordered like ``LAYOUT["acceleration"]``.

    Raises:
        np.linalg.LinAlgError: the system is singular, i.e. its condition number after
            row equilibration exceeds ``MAX_COND`` (1e12); the message gives the
            condition number and the state. Examples: a zero mass, a singular
            inertia, a degenerate kinetic energy.
        ValueError: *u* has the wrong shape or non-finite entries.
    """
    model = model_of(module).require("mass", "bias", "input_matrix")
    x, u = model.as_state(state), model.as_input(u)
    return solve_accelerations(model, x, u, p or {}, check=True)

docs.title: check_state(module, state, tol=STATE_TOL, what='x0')
docs.text:
Check that state lies on the state manifold of module and return it flat.

Each S² point has unit norm and its velocity ω is orthogonal to it; each SO(3) point is orthogonal with determinant +1; every entry is finite. The tolerance is tol (1e-9). Raises ValueError naming the slot otherwise.

Source code in geomech/simulation/model.py 
def check_state(
    module: Any, state: ArrayLike, tol: float = STATE_TOL, what: str = "x0"
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Check that *state* lies on the state manifold of *module* and return it flat.

    Each S² point has unit norm and its velocity ``ω`` is orthogonal to it; each SO(3)
    point is orthogonal with determinant +1; every entry is finite. The tolerance is
    *tol* (1e-9). Raises ``ValueError`` naming the slot otherwise.
    """
    model = model_of(module)
    x = model.as_state(state, what)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(x)):
        raise ValueError(f"{what}: non-finite entries {np.flatnonzero(~np.isfinite(x))}")
    for var in model.s2:
        q, w = x[var.cfg], x[var.vel]
        if abs(np.linalg.norm(q) - 1.0) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the S2 slot '{var.key}' must have unit norm, got"
                f" |{var.key}| = {np.linalg.norm(q):.12g}"
            )
        if abs(q @ w) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the velocity slot '{var.vel_key}' must be orthogonal to"
                f" '{var.key}', got {var.key}·{var.vel_key} = {q @ w:.3g}"
            )
    for var in model.so3:
        R = x[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3)
        err = np.linalg.norm(R.T @ R - np.eye(3))
        if err > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the SO3 slot '{var.key}' must be orthogonal, got"
                f" |RᵀR − I| = {err:.3g} (row-major, 9 entries)"
            )
        det = np.linalg.det(R)
        if abs(det - 1.0) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the SO3 slot '{var.key}' must have determinant +1, got {det:.12g}"
            )
    return x

docs.text:
{name: (N,) array} of the manifold constraint violations of states.

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def constraint_drift(model: Model, states: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """``{name: (N,) array}`` of the manifold constraint violations of *states*."""
    states = np.atleast_2d(states)
    out = {}
    for var in model.s2:
        q, w = states[:, var.cfg], states[:, var.vel]
        name = _name(model, var.key)
        out[f"|{name}|-1"] = np.abs(np.linalg.norm(q, axis=1) - 1.0)
        out[f"{name}.{_name(model, var.vel_key)}"] = np.abs(np.einsum("ij,ij->i", q, w))
    for var in model.so3:
        R = states[:, var.cfg].reshape(-1, 3, 3)
        name = _name(model, var.key)
        RtR = np.einsum("nki,nkj->nij", R, R)
        out[f"{name}^T {name}-I"] = np.linalg.norm(RtR - np.eye(3), axis=(1, 2))
    return out

docs.title: lqr(lin_module, x_eq, u_eq, p, Q, R, *, a_eq=None, tol=STATE_TOL, module=None, eq_tol=1e-08)
docs.text:
The continuous-time LQR gain of a generated linearization about an equilibrium.

Evaluates M_lin, A_lin, B_lin of lin_module (generate_module of a LinearizedSystem) at (x_eq, a_eq, u_eq), reduces them to the tangent coordinates δx = Tᵀ δx_full (Mr = Tᵀ M T, Ar = Tᵀ A T, Br = Tᵀ B), forms Ā = Mr⁻¹ Ar, B̄ = Mr⁻¹ Br, solves scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_are and returns K = R⁻¹ B̄ᵀ P in an LQRController.

The S² reduction: the 3-D perturbations ξ and δω of an S² point satisfy ξ · q = δω · q = 0 at an equilibrium (where ω = 0), so each has 2 degrees of freedom. In 3-D the normal direction is an uncontrollable mode with a zero eigenvalue, so the Riccati equation has no stabilising solution. T maps the 2-D tangent coordinates in the basis tangent_basis(q_eq) to the 3-D ones, and the S² rows (whose equations hold only on the tangent plane) are projected with Tᵀ. A singular S² mass block (Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²) becomes invertible in this basis.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lin_module Any

the generated module of linearize (M_lin, A_lin, B_lin, LINEARIZATION).

required x_eq ArrayLike

the equilibrium state (checked like simulate's x0).

required u_eq ArrayLike

the equilibrium input.

required p dict

the parameters.

required Q ArrayLike

the weight of the reduced state: a scalar (times the identity), a vector (the diagonal) or a matrix.

required R ArrayLike

the weight of the input, in the same forms.

required a_eq ArrayLike | None

the accelerations at x_eq (zeros by default).

None tol float

the tolerance of the x_eq check.

STATE_TOL module Any

the generated standard-form module of the same system (generate_module of to_standard_form, with the same layout: the same variables, velocities and inputs in the same order, checked). When given, (x_eq, u_eq) is checked to be an equilibrium, see below. When omitted, it is not checked and a UserWarning says so.

None eq_tol float

the relative tolerance of the equilibrium check.

1e-08

The gain is only meaningful about an equilibrium: the linearization is evaluated at (x_eq, a_eq, u_eq) and the S² reduction assumes ω_eq = 0. At a point that is not an equilibrium lqr still returns a gain with stable closed-loop eigenvalues, but the nonlinear loop settles somewhere else. With module, lqr therefore requires every velocity of x_eq to be zero (to tol) and the equation residual r = mass·a_eq + bias + G u_eq (S² rows projected on the tangent plane) to satisfy ‖r‖∞ ≤ eq_tol · scale, with scale the largest of ‖bias‖∞, ‖G u_eq‖∞ and ‖A_lin T‖∞ (the force per unit perturbation, which is nonzero at an equilibrium held by a potential even when the bias itself is zero there). Otherwise it raises ValueError with the residual and the accelerations accelerations(module, x_eq, u_eq, p).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

bad arguments; a LINEARIZATION whose variables or inputs are not those of its LAYOUT in the same order; module with another layout than lin_module (the message names both variable and input orders); or (x_eq, u_eq) is not an equilibrium of module.

LinAlgError

the reduced M_lin is singular.

def lqr(
    lin_module: Any,
    x_eq: ArrayLike,
    u_eq: ArrayLike,
    p: dict,
    Q: ArrayLike,
    R: ArrayLike,
    *,
    a_eq: ArrayLike | None = None,
    tol: float = STATE_TOL,
    module: Any = None,
    eq_tol: float = 1e-8,
) -> LQRController:
    """The continuous-time LQR gain of a generated linearization about an equilibrium.

    Evaluates ``M_lin``, ``A_lin``, ``B_lin`` of *lin_module* (``generate_module`` of a
    ``LinearizedSystem``) at ``(x_eq, a_eq, u_eq)``, reduces them to the tangent
    coordinates ``δx = Tᵀ δx_full`` (``Mr = Tᵀ M T``, ``Ar = Tᵀ A T``, ``Br = Tᵀ B``),
    forms ``Ā = Mr⁻¹ Ar``, ``B̄ = Mr⁻¹ Br``, solves ``scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_are``
    and returns ``K = R⁻¹ B̄ᵀ P`` in an ``LQRController``.

    The S² reduction: the 3-D perturbations ``ξ`` and ``δω`` of an S² point satisfy
    ``ξ · q = δω · q = 0`` at an equilibrium (where ``ω = 0``), so each has 2 degrees of
    freedom. In 3-D the normal direction is an uncontrollable mode with a zero
    eigenvalue, so the Riccati equation has no stabilising solution. ``T`` maps the 2-D
    tangent coordinates in the basis ``tangent_basis(q_eq)`` to the 3-D ones, and the S²
    rows (whose equations hold only on the tangent plane) are projected with ``Tᵀ``.
    A singular S² mass block (``Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²``) becomes invertible in this basis.

    Args:
        lin_module: the generated module of ``linearize`` (``M_lin``, ``A_lin``,
            ``B_lin``, ``LINEARIZATION``).
        x_eq: the equilibrium state (checked like ``simulate``'s ``x0``).
        u_eq: the equilibrium input.
        p: the parameters.
        Q: the weight of the reduced state: a scalar (times the identity), a vector (the
            diagonal) or a matrix.
        R: the weight of the input, in the same forms.
        a_eq: the accelerations at ``x_eq`` (zeros by default).
        tol: the tolerance of the ``x_eq`` check.
        module: the generated standard-form module of the same system
            (``generate_module`` of ``to_standard_form``, with the same layout: the same
            variables, velocities and inputs in the same order, checked). When
            given, ``(x_eq, u_eq)`` is checked to be an equilibrium, see below. When
            omitted, it is not checked and a ``UserWarning`` says so.
        eq_tol: the relative tolerance of the equilibrium check.

    The gain is only meaningful about an equilibrium: the linearization is evaluated at
    ``(x_eq, a_eq, u_eq)`` and the S² reduction assumes ``ω_eq = 0``. At a point that is
    not an equilibrium ``lqr`` still returns a gain with stable closed-loop eigenvalues,
    but the nonlinear loop settles somewhere else. With *module*, ``lqr`` therefore
    requires every velocity of ``x_eq`` to be zero (to *tol*) and the equation residual
    ``r = mass·a_eq + bias + G u_eq`` (S² rows projected on the tangent plane) to satisfy
    ``‖r‖∞ ≤ eq_tol · scale``, with ``scale`` the largest of ``‖bias‖∞``,
    ``‖G u_eq‖∞`` and ``‖A_lin T‖∞`` (the force per unit perturbation, which is nonzero
    at an equilibrium held by a potential even when the bias itself is zero there).
    Otherwise it raises ``ValueError`` with the residual and the accelerations
    ``accelerations(module, x_eq, u_eq, p)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: bad arguments; a ``LINEARIZATION`` whose variables or inputs are not
            those of its ``LAYOUT`` in the same order; *module* with another layout than
            *lin_module* (the message names both variable and input orders); or
            ``(x_eq, u_eq)`` is not an equilibrium of *module*.
        np.linalg.LinAlgError: the reduced ``M_lin`` is singular.
    """
    try:
        from scipy.linalg import solve_continuous_are
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the environment
        raise ImportError("lqr needs scipy: pip install 'geomech[sim]'") from exc
    model = model_of(lin_module).require("M_lin", "A_lin", "B_lin")
    lin = getattr(lin_module, "LINEARIZATION", None)
    if not isinstance(lin, dict):
        raise TypeError("lqr: the module has no LINEARIZATION; generate it from linearize")
    x_eq = check_state(lin_module, x_eq, tol=tol, what="x_eq")
    u_eq = model.as_input(u_eq, "u_eq")
    a_eq = np.zeros(model.n_accel) if a_eq is None else np.asarray(a_eq, float).reshape(-1)
    if module is not None:
        _check_same_layout(model, model_of(module).require("mass", "bias", "input_matrix"))

    T, bases, labels = _reduction(model, lin, x_eq)
    M = lin_module.M_lin(x_eq, a_eq, u_eq, p)
    A = lin_module.A_lin(x_eq, a_eq, u_eq, p)
    B = lin_module.B_lin(x_eq, a_eq, u_eq, p)
    Mr = T.T @ M @ T
    try:
        Abar = np.linalg.solve(Mr, T.T @ A @ T)
        Bbar = np.linalg.solve(Mr, T.T @ B)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError as exc:
        raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(
            f"lqr: the reduced M_lin is singular at x_eq (condition number"
            f" {np.linalg.cond(Mr):.3g})"
        ) from exc
    n = T.shape[1]
    Qm = _weight(Q, n, "Q")
    Rm = _weight(R, model.n_inputs, "R")
    if module is None:
        warnings.warn(
            "lqr: (x_eq, u_eq) is not checked to be an equilibrium; pass module=<the"
            " standard-form module> to check it (a gain about a non-equilibrium point"
            " stabilises the loop somewhere else)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    else:
        _check_equilibrium(model, module, x_eq, u_eq, a_eq, p, tol, eq_tol, A @ T)
    P = solve_continuous_are(Abar, Bbar, Qm, Rm)
    K = np.linalg.solve(Rm, Bbar.T @ P)
    return LQRController(K, P, Abar, Bbar, T, x_eq, u_eq, labels, model, bases)

def simulate(
    module: Any,
    x0: ArrayLike,
    t_span: float | tuple[float, float],
    p: dict,
    u: ArrayLike | Callable | None = None,
    method: str = "rkmk4",
    dt: float = 1e-3,
    *,
    rtol: float = 1e-10,
    atol: float = 1e-12,
    ivp_method: str = "DOP853",
    tol: float = STATE_TOL,
    output_every: int = 1,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Integrate a generated standard-form model from *x0* over *t_span*.

    Args:
        module: a module from ``geomech.codegen.generate_module`` of a
            ``to_standard_form`` result (``mass``, ``bias``, ``input_matrix``,
            ``kinematics``).
        x0: the initial state, flat in ``LAYOUT`` order. It must lie on the manifold
            (``|q| = 1``, ``q·ω = 0``, ``R`` orthogonal with ``det R = +1``, to *tol*),
            else ``ValueError`` naming the slot.
        t_span: ``(t0, tf)``, or ``tf`` for ``(0, tf)``.
        p: the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.
        u: ``None`` (zero inputs), a constant 1-D array, or a callable ``u(t, state)``
            returning the inputs (e.g. an ``LQRController``). The inputs must be finite;
            a callable that returns ``None`` raises ``TypeError``. A callable is
            evaluated once per RKMK4 stage, and ``traj.u`` records the values of each
            stored step's first stage (plus one call at the final state), so no state
            is evaluated twice. With ``"solve_ivp"`` it is evaluated at trial steps that
            may be rejected and at times that are not monotone, and once more at each
            stored (interpolated) state after the run: there it should be a pure
            function of ``(t, state)``. An exception raised by the callable propagates
            unchanged, as soon as it is raised, with a note giving ``t``.
        method: ``"rkmk4"`` (fixed step, default) or ``"solve_ivp"``.
        dt: the step of ``"rkmk4"`` (shortened so that it divides ``tf − t0``) and the
            output spacing of ``"solve_ivp"``.
        rtol: passed to ``scipy.integrate.solve_ivp``.
        atol: passed to ``scipy.integrate.solve_ivp``.
        ivp_method: the ``solve_ivp`` method (``"DOP853"``, ``"RK45"``, …).
        tol: the tolerance of the *x0* check.
        output_every: store every ``output_every``-th step of the ``dt`` grid (and
            always the last), to thin long runs; the integration itself is unchanged.

    The accelerations come from ``geomech.simulation.accelerations`` (the S² rows solved
    on the tangent plane). The stored states are on the manifold (``project_state``), so
    ``traj.state[-1]`` is a valid *x0* for the next segment. See ``docs/simulation.md``.
    """
    if method not in _METHODS:
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: method must be one of {_METHODS}, got {method!r}")
    model = model_of(module).require("mass", "bias", "input_matrix", "kinematics")
    x0 = check_state(module, x0, tol=tol, what="x0")
    t0, tf = _span(t_span)
    if not (dt > 0 and np.isfinite(dt)):
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: dt must be positive, got {dt}")
    if isinstance(output_every, bool) or not isinstance(output_every, (int, np.integer)):
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: output_every must be a positive int, got {output_every!r}")
    if output_every < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: output_every must be a positive int, got {output_every}")
    n_steps = max(1, int(np.ceil((tf - t0) / dt - 1e-9)))
    keep = np.unique(np.r_[np.arange(0, n_steps + 1, int(output_every)), n_steps])
    ufun = _input_function(model, u)
    p = dict(p or {})
    u0 = ufun(t0, x0)
    solve_accelerations(model, x0, u0, p, check=True)  # singular system: raise now
    if method == "rkmk4":
        t, states, inputs = _rkmk4(model, x0, t0, tf, n_steps, p, ufun, keep, u0)
        drift = constraint_drift(model, states)
        info = {"n_steps": n_steps, "dt": (tf - t0) / n_steps, "nfev": 4 * n_steps}
    else:
        t, raw, info = _solve_ivp(
            model, x0, t0, tf, n_steps, p, ufun, rtol, atol, ivp_method, keep
        )
        drift = constraint_drift(model, raw)
        states = np.array([project_state(model, x) for x in raw])
        # the stored states are interpolated, never evaluated during the run
        inputs = np.array([ufun(ti, x) for ti, x in zip(t, states)], dtype=float)
    info["output_every"] = int(output_every)
    inputs = inputs.reshape(len(t), model.n_inputs)
    return Trajectory(t, states, drift, method, p, module, info, inputs)

docs.title: tangent_basis(q)
docs.text:
An orthonormal basis [b₁ b₂] (3×2) of the plane orthogonal to the unit vector q, with b₁ × b₂ = q. b₁ is the coordinate axis least aligned with q, projected and normalised, so the basis is a deterministic function of q.

Source code in geomech/simulation/control.py 
def tangent_basis(q) -> np.ndarray:
    """An orthonormal basis ``[b₁ b₂]`` (3×2) of the plane orthogonal to the unit vector
    *q*, with ``b₁ × b₂ = q``. ``b₁`` is the coordinate axis least aligned with *q*,
    projected and normalised, so the basis is a deterministic function of *q*."""
    q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float).reshape(3)
    q = q / np.linalg.norm(q)
    e = np.eye(3)[int(np.argmin(np.abs(q)))]
    b1 = e - (e @ q) * q
    b1 /= np.linalg.norm(b1)
    b2 = np.cross(q, b1)
    return np.column_stack([b1, b2])

docs.title: control
docs.text:
LQR about an equilibrium from the variation-based linearization (linearize).

lqr(lin_module, x_eq, u_eq, p, Q, R) evaluates the generated M_lin, A_lin and B_lin at the equilibrium, reduces the S² perturbations to a 2-D tangent basis, solves the continuous algebraic Riccati equation and returns an LQRController: the gain K and the state error δx(state) on the manifold, callable as u(t, state) for simulate.

The perturbation coordinates are those of linearize (docs/vbl.md):

========== ========================== ========================================= Variable Configuration error Velocity error ========== ========================== ========================================= R, R³ x − x_eq ẋ − ẋ_eq S² Bᵀ (q_eq × q) (2-D) Bᵀ (ω − ω_eq) (2-D) SO(3) vee(log(R_eqᵀ R)) Ω − Ω_eq ========== ========================== =========================================

δq = ξ × q with ξ ⊥ q, so ξ = q_eq × q to first order, and δR = R η̂ so R = R_eq exp(η̂). B = [b₁ b₂] is an orthonormal basis of the tangent plane at q_eq (tangent_basis).

scipy (scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_are) is imported only when lqr is called.

docs.text:
The reduced state error δx of state about x_eq (see the module docstring).

def error(self, state) -> np.ndarray:
    """The reduced state error ``δx`` of *state* about ``x_eq`` (see the module
    docstring)."""
    x = np.asarray(state, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    xe = self.x_eq
    cfg, vel = [], []
    for var in self.model.variables:
        if var.manifold == "S2":
            Bq = self.bases[var.key]
            cfg.append(Bq.T @ np.cross(xe[var.cfg], x[var.cfg]))
            vel.append(Bq.T @ (x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel]))
        elif var.manifold == "SO3":
            Re, R = xe[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3), x[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3)
            cfg.append(log_so3(Re.T @ R))
            vel.append(x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel])
        else:
            cfg.append(x[var.cfg] - xe[var.cfg])
            vel.append(x[var.vel] - xe[var.vel])
    return np.concatenate(cfg + vel)

            f" {np.linalg.cond(Mr):.3g})"
        ) from exc
    n = T.shape[1]
    Qm = _weight(Q, n, "Q")
    Rm = _weight(R, model.n_inputs, "R")
    if module is None:
        warnings.warn(
            "lqr: (x_eq, u_eq) is not checked to be an equilibrium; pass module=<the"
            " standard-form module> to check it (a gain about a non-equilibrium point"
            " stabilises the loop somewhere else)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    else:
        _check_equilibrium(model, module, x_eq, u_eq, a_eq, p, tol, eq_tol, A @ T)
    P = solve_continuous_are(Abar, Bbar, Qm, Rm)
    K = np.linalg.solve(Rm, Bbar.T @ P)
    return LQRController(K, P, Abar, Bbar, T, x_eq, u_eq, labels, model, bases)

docs.title: tangent_basis(q)
docs.text:
An orthonormal basis [b₁ b₂] (3×2) of the plane orthogonal to the unit vector q, with b₁ × b₂ = q. b₁ is the coordinate axis least aligned with q, projected and normalised, so the basis is a deterministic function of q.

Source code in geomech/simulation/control.py 
def tangent_basis(q) -> np.ndarray:
    """An orthonormal basis ``[b₁ b₂]`` (3×2) of the plane orthogonal to the unit vector
    *q*, with ``b₁ × b₂ = q``. ``b₁`` is the coordinate axis least aligned with *q*,
    projected and normalised, so the basis is a deterministic function of *q*."""
    q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float).reshape(3)
    q = q / np.linalg.norm(q)
    e = np.eye(3)[int(np.argmin(np.abs(q)))]
    b1 = e - (e @ q) * q
    b1 /= np.linalg.norm(b1)
    b2 = np.cross(q, b1)
    return np.column_stack([b1, b2])

docs.title: integrators
docs.text:
Integrators on the state manifold of a generated model: simulate and Trajectory.

Two methods:

  • "rkmk4" (default): fixed-step Runge–Kutta–Munthe-Kaas of order 4. S² and SO(3) points are moved by rotations, so |q| = 1 and RᵀR = I hold to round-off with no projection; every other slot (R, R³ and all velocities) gets classical RK4.
  • "solve_ivp": scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (DOP853 by default) on the embedded state; the outputs are projected onto the manifold and the drift before projection is reported.

scipy is imported only by method="solve_ivp".

docs.title: __getitem__(key)
docs.text:
The values of one state slot over time, by printed symbol ("q", "\\omega_{q}") or generated name ("omega_q"): (N,), (N, 3) or (N, 3, 3) for an SO(3) point.

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """The values of one state slot over time, by printed symbol (``"q"``,
    ``"\\\\omega_{q}"``) or generated name (``"omega_q"``): ``(N,)``, ``(N, 3)`` or
    ``(N, 3, 3)`` for an SO(3) point."""
    lay = self.module.LAYOUT
    for slot in lay["configuration"] + lay["velocity"]:
        if key in (slot["symbol"], slot["name"]):
            vals = self.state[:, slice(*slot["slice"])]
            shape = tuple(slot["shape"])
            return vals[:, 0] if shape == () else vals.reshape((len(self.t), *shape))
    names = [s["name"] for s in lay["configuration"] + lay["velocity"]]
    raise KeyError(f"Trajectory: no state slot {key!r} (slots: {names})")

def energy(self, fn: Callable | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """``fn(state, p)`` at every output state, ``(N,)``.

    *fn* defaults to the module's ``energy`` (``generate_module(...,
    lagrangian=L)``); ``geomech.codegen.energy_function(L, layout)`` gives one for any
    Lagrangian.
    """
    if fn is None:
        fn = getattr(self.module, "energy", None)
        if fn is None:
            raise TypeError(
                "Trajectory.energy: the module has no energy(); generate it with"
                " generate_module(..., lagrangian=L) or pass energy_function(L, layout)"
            )
    # The generated functions take one state at a time; at about 20 µs per state
    # (double rigid pendulum) this loop is a few percent of the simulation that
    # produced the states, so it is not vectorised.
    return np.fromiter((float(fn(x, self.p)) for x in self.state), float, len(self.state))

docs.title: constraint_drift(model, states)
docs.text:
{name: (N,) array} of the manifold constraint violations of states.

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def constraint_drift(model: Model, states: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """``{name: (N,) array}`` of the manifold constraint violations of *states*."""
    states = np.atleast_2d(states)
    out = {}
    for var in model.s2:
        q, w = states[:, var.cfg], states[:, var.vel]
        name = _name(model, var.key)
        out[f"|{name}|-1"] = np.abs(np.linalg.norm(q, axis=1) - 1.0)
        out[f"{name}.{_name(model, var.vel_key)}"] = np.abs(np.einsum("ij,ij->i", q, w))
    for var in model.so3:
        R = states[:, var.cfg].reshape(-1, 3, 3)
        name = _name(model, var.key)
        RtR = np.einsum("nki,nkj->nij", R, R)
        out[f"{name}^T {name}-I"] = np.linalg.norm(RtR - np.eye(3), axis=(1, 2))
    return out

docs.title: project_state(model, state)
docs.text:
state projected onto the state manifold: each S² point normalised and its velocity made tangent (ω ← ω − (q·ω) q), each SO(3) point replaced by its polar factor (the nearest rotation, U Vᵀ of the SVD). A projected state passes check_state, so it can start another simulate.

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def project_state(model: Model, state: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """*state* projected onto the state manifold: each S² point normalised and its
    velocity made tangent (``ω ← ω − (q·ω) q``), each SO(3) point replaced by its polar
    factor (the nearest rotation, ``U Vᵀ`` of the SVD). A projected state passes
    ``check_state``, so it can start another ``simulate``."""
    x = np.array(state, dtype=float)
    for var in model.s2:
        q = x[var.cfg] / np.linalg.norm(x[var.cfg])
        x[var.cfg] = q
        x[var.vel] -= (q @ x[var.vel]) * q
    for var in model.so3:
        U, _, Vt = np.linalg.svd(x[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3))
        R = U @ Vt
        if np.linalg.det(R) < 0:  # not reachable from a rotation by small drift
            U[:, -1] = -U[:, -1]
            R = U @ Vt
        x[var.cfg] = R.reshape(9)
    return x

Source code in geomech/simulation/integrators.py 
def simulate(
    module: Any,
    x0: ArrayLike,
    t_span: float | tuple[float, float],
    p: dict,
    u: ArrayLike | Callable | None = None,
    method: str = "rkmk4",
    dt: float = 1e-3,
    *,
    rtol: float = 1e-10,
    atol: float = 1e-12,
    ivp_method: str = "DOP853",
    tol: float = STATE_TOL,
    output_every: int = 1,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Integrate a generated standard-form model from *x0* over *t_span*.

    Args:
        module: a module from ``geomech.codegen.generate_module`` of a
            ``to_standard_form`` result (``mass``, ``bias``, ``input_matrix``,
            ``kinematics``).
        x0: the initial state, flat in ``LAYOUT`` order. It must lie on the manifold
            (``|q| = 1``, ``q·ω = 0``, ``R`` orthogonal with ``det R = +1``, to *tol*),
            else ``ValueError`` naming the slot.
        t_span: ``(t0, tf)``, or ``tf`` for ``(0, tf)``.
        p: the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.
        u: ``None`` (zero inputs), a constant 1-D array, or a callable ``u(t, state)``
            returning the inputs (e.g. an ``LQRController``). The inputs must be finite;
            a callable that returns ``None`` raises ``TypeError``. A callable is
            evaluated once per RKMK4 stage, and ``traj.u`` records the values of each
            stored step's first stage (plus one call at the final state), so no state
            is evaluated twice. With ``"solve_ivp"`` it is evaluated at trial steps that
            may be rejected and at times that are not monotone, and once more at each
            stored (interpolated) state after the run: there it should be a pure
            function of ``(t, state)``. An exception raised by the callable propagates
            unchanged, as soon as it is raised, with a note giving ``t``.
        method: ``"rkmk4"`` (fixed step, default) or ``"solve_ivp"``.
        dt: the step of ``"rkmk4"`` (shortened so that it divides ``tf − t0``) and the
            output spacing of ``"solve_ivp"``.
        rtol: passed to ``scipy.integrate.solve_ivp``.
        atol: passed to ``scipy.integrate.solve_ivp``.
        ivp_method: the ``solve_ivp`` method (``"DOP853"``, ``"RK45"``, …).
        tol: the tolerance of the *x0* check.
        output_every: store every ``output_every``-th step of the ``dt`` grid (and
            always the last), to thin long runs; the integration itself is unchanged.

    The accelerations come from ``geomech.simulation.accelerations`` (the S² rows solved
    on the tangent plane). The stored states are on the manifold (``project_state``), so
    ``traj.state[-1]`` is a valid *x0* for the next segment. See ``docs/simulation.md``.
    """
    if method not in _METHODS:
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: method must be one of {_METHODS}, got {method!r}")
    model = model_of(module).require("mass", "bias", "input_matrix", "kinematics")
    x0 = check_state(module, x0, tol=tol, what="x0")
    t0, tf = _span(t_span)
    if not (dt > 0 and np.isfinite(dt)):
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: dt must be positive, got {dt}")
    if isinstance(output_every, bool) or not isinstance(output_every, (int, np.integer)):
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: output_every must be a positive int, got {output_every!r}")
    if output_every < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"simulate: output_every must be a positive int, got {output_every}")
    n_steps = max(1, int(np.ceil((tf - t0) / dt - 1e-9)))
    keep = np.unique(np.r_[np.arange(0, n_steps + 1, int(output_every)), n_steps])
    ufun = _input_function(model, u)
    p = dict(p or {})
    u0 = ufun(t0, x0)
    solve_accelerations(model, x0, u0, p, check=True)  # singular system: raise now
    if method == "rkmk4":
        t, states, inputs = _rkmk4(model, x0, t0, tf, n_steps, p, ufun, keep, u0)
        drift = constraint_drift(model, states)
        info = {"n_steps": n_steps, "dt": (tf - t0) / n_steps, "nfev": 4 * n_steps}
    else:
        t, raw, info = _solve_ivp(
            model, x0, t0, tf, n_steps, p, ufun, rtol, atol, ivp_method, keep
        )
        drift = constraint_drift(model, raw)
        states = np.array([project_state(model, x) for x in raw])
        # the stored states are interpolated, never evaluated during the run
        inputs = np.array([ufun(ti, x) for ti, x in zip(t, states)], dtype=float)
    info["output_every"] = int(output_every)
    inputs = inputs.reshape(len(t), model.n_inputs)
    return Trajectory(t, states, drift, method, p, module, info, inputs)

A model is a module written by geomech.codegen.generate_module from to_standard_form: it defines LAYOUT, mass, bias, input_matrix and kinematics (and energy with lagrangian=L), with the equations mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0 (signs as in docs/conventions.md).

Source code in geomech/simulation/model.py 
def __init__(self, module: Any):
    layout = getattr(module, "LAYOUT", None)
    if not isinstance(layout, dict):
        raise TypeError(
            "simulation: expected a module generated by geomech.codegen (with LAYOUT),"
            f" got {type(module).__name__}"
        )
    self.module = module
    self.layout = layout
    self.n_state = int(layout["n_state"])
    self.n_config = int(layout["n_config"])
    self.n_accel = int(layout["n_accel"])
    self.n_inputs = int(layout["n_inputs"])
    self.variables = [
        _Var(
            key=c["symbol"],
            vel_key=v["symbol"],
            manifold=c["manifold"],
            cfg=slice(*c["slice"]),
            vel=slice(*v["slice"]),
            acc=slice(*a["slice"]),
        )
        for c, v, a in zip(layout["configuration"], layout["velocity"], layout["acceleration"])
    ]
    self.s2 = [v for v in self.variables if v.manifold == "S2"]
    self.so3 = [v for v in self.variables if v.manifold == "SO3"]
    self.euclid = [v for v in self.variables if v.manifold in ("R", "R3")]

A scalar is accepted for a single input; an array of any other dimension than 1 raises ValueError rather than being flattened (a (2, 2) array for four inputs is almost certainly a mistake). Non-finite entries raise ValueError naming them.

Source code in geomech/simulation/model.py 
def as_input(self, u, what="u") -> np.ndarray:
    """*u* as a flat float array of ``n_inputs`` finite entries (``None``: zeros).

    A scalar is accepted for a single input; an array of any other dimension than 1
    raises ``ValueError`` rather than being flattened (a ``(2, 2)`` array for four
    inputs is almost certainly a mistake). Non-finite entries raise ``ValueError``
    naming them."""
    if u is None:
        return np.zeros(self.n_inputs)
    arr = np.asarray(u, dtype=float)
    if arr.ndim > 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{what} must be a 1-D array of {self.n_inputs} entries, got shape {arr.shape}"
        )
    arr = arr.reshape(-1)
    if arr.size != self.n_inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} must have {self.n_inputs} entries, got {arr.size}")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(arr)):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{what} has non-finite entries at {np.flatnonzero(~np.isfinite(arr)).tolist()}:"
            f" {np.array2string(arr, precision=6)}"
        )
    return arr

def require(self, *names: str) -> Model:
    """Raise ``TypeError`` unless the module defines every function in *names*."""
    for name in names:
        if not callable(getattr(self.module, name, None)):
            hint = (
                "; generate it from to_standard_form"
                if name in ("mass", "bias", "input_matrix")
                else "; generate it from linearize"
                if name.endswith("_lin")
                else ""
            )
            raise TypeError(f"simulation: the module has no {name}(){hint}")
    return self

docs.title: accelerations(module, state, u=None, p=None)
docs.text:
The accelerations a of a generated standard-form module at (state, u).

Solves mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0. Every S² equation is meaningful only on the tangent plane of its point q (docs/conventions.md), and its acceleration ω̇ satisfies q · ω̇ = 0 (from d/dt (q · ω) = 0 with q̇ · ω = (ω × q) · ω = 0). So each S² row block is replaced by P_q · row plus a multiple of q qᵀ on its own ω̇ column, with right-hand side −P_q (bias + G u), P_q = I − q qᵀ; the couplings of that row to the other accelerations are projected too. This works whether the derived S² mass block is singular (Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²) or already full rank (−m l² I, when the engine used q · ω̇ = 0 itself).

Scaling, so that the result does not depend on the units: the stabiliser is s q qᵀ with s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2, D the row's own diagonal mass block. Both forms of D project to −m l² P_q and ‖P_q‖_F = √2, so s = m l²: the normal direction gets the same magnitude as the two tangent directions (for an anisotropic tangent inertia, the root mean square of the two). Then every row of the system and of the right-hand side is divided by its largest entry (row equilibration), and the system is solved with np.linalg.solve. The condition number is taken on the equilibrated matrix, so a light link (m₂/m₁ = 1e-9) or a large one (1 t on a 100 km tether, SI units) is solved to round-off and accepted, while a kinetic energy that is degenerate for every parameter value still raises.

Name Type Description Default module Any

a module from generate_module of a to_standard_form result.

required state ArrayLike

the flat state (LAYOUT: configuration slots, then velocity slots).

required u ArrayLike | None

the inputs (None for zeros).

None p dict | None

the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.

None

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

The flat accelerations, ordered like LAYOUT["acceleration"].

Raises:

Type Description LinAlgError

the system is singular, i.e. its condition number after row equilibration exceeds MAX_COND (1e12); the message gives the condition number and the state. Examples: a zero mass, a singular inertia, a degenerate kinetic energy.

ValueError

u has the wrong shape or non-finite entries.

def accelerations(
    module: Any, state: ArrayLike, u: ArrayLike | None = None, p: dict | None = None
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The accelerations ``a`` of a generated standard-form module at ``(state, u)``.

    Solves ``mass @ a + bias + input_matrix @ u = 0``. Every S² equation is meaningful
    only on the tangent plane of its point ``q`` (``docs/conventions.md``), and its
    acceleration ``ω̇`` satisfies ``q · ω̇ = 0`` (from ``d/dt (q · ω) = 0`` with
    ``q̇ · ω = (ω × q) · ω = 0``). So each S² row block is replaced by ``P_q · row`` plus
    a multiple of ``q qᵀ`` on its own ``ω̇`` column, with right-hand side ``−P_q (bias + G u)``,
    ``P_q = I − q qᵀ``; the couplings of that row to the other accelerations are
    projected too. This works whether the derived S² mass block is singular
    (``Hat(q) Hat(q) m l²``) or already full rank (``−m l² I``, when the engine used
    ``q · ω̇ = 0`` itself).

    Scaling, so that the result does not depend on the units: the stabiliser is
    ``s q qᵀ`` with ``s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2``, ``D`` the row's own diagonal mass block.
    Both forms of ``D`` project to ``−m l² P_q`` and ``‖P_q‖_F = √2``, so ``s = m l²``:
    the normal direction gets the same magnitude as the two tangent directions (for an
    anisotropic tangent inertia, the root mean square of the two). Then every row of the
    system and of the right-hand side is divided by its largest entry (row
    equilibration), and the system is solved with ``np.linalg.solve``. The condition
    number is taken on the equilibrated matrix, so a light link (``m₂/m₁ = 1e-9``) or a
    large one (1 t on a 100 km tether, SI units) is solved to round-off and accepted,
    while a kinetic energy that is degenerate for every parameter value still raises.

    Args:
        module: a module from ``generate_module`` of a ``to_standard_form`` result.
        state: the flat state (``LAYOUT``: configuration slots, then velocity slots).
        u: the inputs (``None`` for zeros).
        p: the parameters, keyed by printed symbol.

    Returns:
        The flat accelerations, ordered like ``LAYOUT["acceleration"]``.

    Raises:
        np.linalg.LinAlgError: the system is singular, i.e. its condition number after
            row equilibration exceeds ``MAX_COND`` (1e12); the message gives the
            condition number and the state. Examples: a zero mass, a singular
            inertia, a degenerate kinetic energy.
        ValueError: *u* has the wrong shape or non-finite entries.
    """
    model = model_of(module).require("mass", "bias", "input_matrix")
    x, u = model.as_state(state), model.as_input(u)
    return solve_accelerations(model, x, u, p or {}, check=True)

def check_state(
    module: Any, state: ArrayLike, tol: float = STATE_TOL, what: str = "x0"
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Check that *state* lies on the state manifold of *module* and return it flat.

    Each S² point has unit norm and its velocity ``ω`` is orthogonal to it; each SO(3)
    point is orthogonal with determinant +1; every entry is finite. The tolerance is
    *tol* (1e-9). Raises ``ValueError`` naming the slot otherwise.
    """
    model = model_of(module)
    x = model.as_state(state, what)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(x)):
        raise ValueError(f"{what}: non-finite entries {np.flatnonzero(~np.isfinite(x))}")
    for var in model.s2:
        q, w = x[var.cfg], x[var.vel]
        if abs(np.linalg.norm(q) - 1.0) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the S2 slot '{var.key}' must have unit norm, got"
                f" |{var.key}| = {np.linalg.norm(q):.12g}"
            )
        if abs(q @ w) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the velocity slot '{var.vel_key}' must be orthogonal to"
                f" '{var.key}', got {var.key}·{var.vel_key} = {q @ w:.3g}"
            )
    for var in model.so3:
        R = x[var.cfg].reshape(3, 3)
        err = np.linalg.norm(R.T @ R - np.eye(3))
        if err > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the SO3 slot '{var.key}' must be orthogonal, got"
                f" |RᵀR − I| = {err:.3g} (row-major, 9 entries)"
            )
        det = np.linalg.det(R)
        if abs(det - 1.0) > tol:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{what}: the SO3 slot '{var.key}' must have determinant +1, got {det:.12g}"
            )
    return x

def model_of(module: Any) -> Model:
    """The ``Model`` of *module*, parsed once per module object."""
    try:
        model = _MODELS.get(module)
    except TypeError:  # not weak-referenceable: parse every time
        return Model(module)
    if model is None:
        model = _MODELS[module] = Model(module)
    return model

docs.text:
The tangent-plane solve of accelerations on already validated arrays.

Each S² row block becomes P_q · row plus s q qᵀ on its own ω̇ column, where s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2 and D is that row's diagonal mass block. Every row of the system is then divided by its largest entry (row equilibration) before the solve and before the condition number is taken; see accelerations.

A failed or non-finite solve always raises; with check, so does a condition number above MAX_COND (one SVD, so the integrators check only the initial state).

Source code in geomech/simulation/model.py 
def solve_accelerations(
    model: Model, state: np.ndarray, u: np.ndarray, p: dict, check: bool = False
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The tangent-plane solve of ``accelerations`` on already validated arrays.

    Each S² row block becomes ``P_q · row`` plus ``s q qᵀ`` on its own ``ω̇`` column,
    where ``s = ‖P_q D‖_F / √2`` and ``D`` is that row's diagonal mass block. Every row
    of the system is then divided by its largest entry (row equilibration) before the
    solve and before the condition number is taken; see ``accelerations``.

    A failed or non-finite solve always raises; with *check*, so does a condition number
    above ``MAX_COND`` (one SVD, so the integrators check only the initial state)."""
    mod = model.module
    A = mod.mass(state, p)
    b = -(mod.bias(state, p) + mod.input_matrix(state, p) @ u)
    for var in model.s2:
        q = state[var.cfg]
        rows = var.acc  # equations are ordered like the variables, so rows = a-slice
        qq = np.outer(q, q)
        P = np.eye(3) - qq
        A[rows] = P @ A[rows]
        # the tangent-plane inertia of this point: m l² for both -m l² I and
        # Hat(q) Hat(q) m l², whose projections are both -m l² P (‖P‖_F = √2)
        s = np.sqrt(np.sum(A[rows, var.acc] ** 2) / 2.0)
        A[rows, var.acc] += s * qq
        b[rows] = P @ b[rows]
    scale = np.abs(A).max(1)
    if not scale.all():
        scale[scale == 0] = 1.0  # a zero row stays zero: singular, and reported as such
    A /= scale[:, None]
    b /= scale
    try:
        a = np.linalg.solve(A, b)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        a = None
    bad = a is None or not np.all(np.isfinite(a))
    if bad or check:
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            cond = np.linalg.cond(A)
        if bad or not cond <= MAX_COND:
            what = "is singular" if not cond <= MAX_COND else "gives non-finite accelerations"
            raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(
                f"accelerations: the mass system {what} (condition number {cond:.3g},"
                " after row equilibration)"
                f" at state {np.array2string(state, precision=6, max_line_width=1000)}"
            )
    assert a is not None
    return a

docs.title: invariants
docs.text:
Structural invariants of expression trees: check_tree(expr).

The constructors validate most of these when a node is built; check_tree re-checks a whole tree after the fact, because a tree can also be assembled by hand (Add([Add(a, b), c]) does not flatten), altered by object.__setattr__ past the frozen node classes, unpickled from an older version, or produced by a rewrite that bypasses a constructor guard. Each violation raises InvariantError naming the invariant, the offending subtree and its path from the root (root.R.0: the right child's first addend; L/R for binary nodes, the index for n-ary nodes, x for the operand of a unary node).

Checks, per node class:

operand types Add/VAdd/MAdd children are SCALAR/VECTOR/MATRIX; Mul (S, S); SVMul (V, S); SMMul (M, S); MVMul (M, V) or a row times a matrix (row V, M); MMMul (M, M); VVMul (V, V); Dot/Cross (V, V); Hat V; Vee M; every node has a type and the number of children its class takes. nested sums no Add directly under an Add (same for VAdd, MAdd): the constructors flatten, so a nested sum means the tree was built around them. row vectors VVMul has exactly one row operand (row × column is the inner product, column × row the outer product); Dot, Cross and Hat take columns only; a VAdd does not mix rows and columns (zero addends are exempt). calculus no TimeDerivative/Variation directly over an S2/SO3 leaf (their kinematics are eager: q.t_diff() is ω × q), no Variation of a Variation, and no Variation of a variation vector (ξ, η). tangent vectors every TS2/TSO3 leaf has its manifold point set (.S2/.SO3) and is named like that point's tangent or variation vector. numeric scalars a Scalar has a value exactly when it is flagged numeric, the value is a real number, and a scalar printed like a number in parentheses ((-1), (0.5), the form Number prints) carries that value: a named Scalar("(-1)") without one would print like the number and be treated as a symbol.
